services.description:
Contact customer service at 718-636-6994 or walk in to schedule an appointment at Restoration Plaza at the Financial Empowerment Center.

Restoration provides a continuum of services from case managers, licensed lawyers, financial counselors, housing ambassadors, and social workers including a free benefit screening, on-site food stamp and Medicaid enrollment, financial and legal counseling, social services referrals, and one-on-one case management.

services.name: Benefits assistance, senior and youth programs, and family services
services.description: Connect with Grand St. Settlement to access financial resources, opportunities for education, counseling, training, and support. Services include one-on-one appointments with Grand St. Settlement staff for financial and insurance support, access to job training and placement programs, and assistance in connecting with and navigating social services. They also offer early childhood and youth programs and services.

services.name: Benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and other services
services.description: Call 212-234-3481 on weekdays to make an appointment for the Resource Center, which provides benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and support services for individuals and families.

services.name: Black Trans Travel Fund
services.description: The Black Trans Travel Fund helps to cover monetary expenses for Black transgender women in New York and New Jersey states in need of money for transportation, in order for them to be able to self-determine, and have access to, their safest transportation options. There is a bi-weekly cap of 75 applicants.

services.name: Bronx Community Fridge and Food Hub
services.description:
Take food from the Friendly Fridge Bronx around the corner from the last stop on the 1 train at 242nd St, or leave fresh food to feed our neighbors and use up food unused food. Available for anyone.

Food Hub Hours: Tues, Thurs & Fri at 2 pm

services.name: BronxWorks Economic and Social Services and Programs
services.description:
BronxWorks provides a range of programs and services including help obtaining health insurance; family and adult shelter; eviction and prevention services; foster care prevention, senior homelessness prevention; chronic illness and health management such as HIV/AIDS; education and youth development; SNAP assistance; food pantry;  immigration and legal services; and workforce development. 

Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities.
TTY: 1-800-662-1220
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: BronxWorks Programs for Elementary School Aged Children
services.description: Access directory of childcare resources including after-school programs, summer camps, and community-center based recreational and education activities for children 5-12 years old operated by BronxWorks.

services.name: Brooklyn Grange CSA
services.description:
A Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program that offers a sliding scale for locally grown vegetables. Runs for 22 weeks from late May through October.

Accepts SNAP benefits.

services.name: Bushwick Free Store
services.description: Tuesdays, 3-5pm at Maria Hernandez Park: Suydam St and Knickerbocker Ave. Share what you have, take what you need. Check Facebook or Instagram (@bushwickfreestore) for weekly updates and/or cancellations for weather.

services.name: CERF+ Emergency Assistance
services.description:
CERF+ offers $3,000 Emergency Relief Grants to craft artists with a public-facing practice who experienced a recent and substantially disruptive emergency or disaster. Applicants must be at least 18 years old and reside or work in the United States or U.S. territories.

To apply, visit the website and complete the online application with supporting documentation.

services.name: Call or Chat to Get Connected with Social Services and Support in NYC
services.description:
CUCS Benefit Centers provide individuals and families with coordinated access to resources, including income support, health insurance enrollment, legal support, and financial coaching. 

Email or call to make an in-person appointment.

services.name: CaringKind Helpline for Support with Dementia
services.description: Call (646) 744-2900, fill out an online form, or email helpline@caringkindnyc.org for resources for caregivers of those diagnosed with Alzheimer's or dementia. Social workers can meet, by appointment, in person in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and The Bronx or by phone and email.

services.name: Case Management Program for Older Adults in Brooklyn
services.description: Case management program to help adults over the age of 60 in Brooklyn stay in their homes and communities as they age. Email info@heightsandhills.org to learn more and schedule a home visit.

services.name: Case Management Program for Older New Yorkers
services.description: Call (718) 892-5520 to access the R.A.I.N. Case Management Program, which serves home bound seniors 60 years of age and over residing in Bronx Community Districts 7,8,11, and 12. Case Managers can assess and link seniors to a wide range of services such as transportation, housekeeping, home care, home delivered meals and assistance with entitlements and benefits.

services.name: Catholic Charities Help Line
services.description: Call 888-744-7900 8:30am-5:30pm to get connected with Catholic Charities' wide range of services for New Yorkers of all religions, including food pantries, housing resources, and services for immigrants and refugees.

services.name: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic
services.description: Provides a single, comprehensive hub for "clients" seeking treatment for their mental health and/or substance use issues. The Bridge partners with Ryan Health, a licensed health clinic, to offer behavioral and primary health care under one roof. Includes outpatient treatment and substance use treatment.

services.name: Child Care Vouchers for Children 6 Weeks - 13 Years Old
services.description: Apply for vouchers from the city to help cover the cost of child care for children 6 weeks to 13 years old at home-based and center-based providers across NYC. Most families are required to pay part of the costs based on their income and family size, but your voucher will cover all of the costs if you are: a family on cash assistance, a family experiencing homelessness, or a foster care parent. Visit the website for eligibility and application details.

services.name: Childcare for Babies and Toddlers: EarlyLearn Program
services.description:
EarlyLearn NYC is free or low-cost child care and education for children six weeks to four years old available for families who qualify for free or low-cost care.

Visit the link to review application process. Must provide proof of address, income, and your citizenship or immigration status.

services.name: Children Wellbeing Programs for Underserved New Yorkers
services.description: Call to connect to educational, health and wellbeing, and family support resources. Visit the website to search for specific programs by age group and neighborhood. Program areas are focused on academic and social-emotional learning, health and nutrition, and support to parents and guardians.

services.name: Circle of Care - Support for Caregivers of People with Chronic Illness or Memory Loss
services.description: If you care for someone who is frail, chronically ill or has memory loss call (866) 665-1713 or fill out an online form to get free personalized support from a Care Consultant. Services include telechat support groups, webinars, and temporary (paid) respite. All New Yorkers are eligible at all income levels.

services.name: City Harvest Map of Food Distribution Sites
services.description: Map of locations that are currently distributing free food throughout NYC. Location sites include soup kitchens, food pantries, City Harvest Mobile Markets, and City Harvest Community Partner Distributions.

services.name: Citywide Doula Initiative to Find Free Doula Services
services.description:
Find professional, no-cost doula services. Check website for contact information for specific doula services by borough. Care is provided depending on zip codes.  To enroll, you must live in one of the neighborhoods shown on the website and be income-eligible for Medicaid. 

The program prioritizes people who: live in a shelter, are in foster care, have no other labor support, are giving birth for the first time, had a previous traumatic birth experience, or have a high-risk medical condition

services.name: Clases de inglés y educación cívica
services.description: Un tercio de los adultos neoyorqinos—más de dos millones de personas—carecen del conocimiento del idioma inglés o un diploma de educación secundaria, pero como resultado de una falta de fondos solo el 3% de ellos pueden acceder a las clases necesarias. Make the Road New York responde a esta necesidad ofreciendo clases de inglés, computación, preparación para la ciudadanía, y cursos de Bridge to Health Careers (Puente a Carreras de Salud) a más de 1,300 adultos al año. Aliados con varias instituciones de la ciudad y el estado, luchamos para aumentar los fondos para la educación de todos los adultos en New York.

services.name: Clinical Supports, Services, & Treatment for Children and Adults
services.description:
Provides services on a sliding scale fee basis. Services include: Psychological Assessment, Psychosocial Evaluation, Sexuality Assessment, and Additional Assessments, to assess and assist in determining needs for individuals with developmental disabilities. Additional clinical services include: Psychotherapy/Counseling, Crisis Intervention Services, Recovery Supports and Wellness Services, OT, PT, & Speech Services, Nutritional Counseling, and Family Reimbursement.

Clinical Services are available to people with developmental disabilities, ages 5 and up. Additionally, certain support services can be provided to other family members who do not themselves have a disability.

Clinics are in Manhattan (Financial District) and the Bronx (Fordham Heights) and open by appointment only; please no walk-ins.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: College Programs for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
services.description: Individuals aged 21 or older with intellectual disabilities who reside in New York City can apply for admission to the Melissa Riggio Higher Education Program at the participating CUNY campus in their borough of residence. To be eligible, applicants must qualify for services from the New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), be enrolled in the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver, and have a Care Manager from a Care Coordination Organization.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Community Cupboard in Hell's Kitchen
services.description: Free food pantry in Hell's Kitchen, open 24/7. Take what you need, leave what you can.

services.name: Community Dining Room for Free Meals
services.description:
Enjoy a healthy meal served to your table.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue
12:30 PM - 3:00 PM Monday-Saturday.

services.name: Community Economic Development Program for Community Groups and Nonprofit Legal Support
services.description: Attorneys provide both short-term legal advice and ongoing representation for community groups and nonprofits, offering a full range of transactional services including corporate formation, contract drafting and negotiation, employment matters, commercial leases, regulatory issues, and real estate transactions.

services.name: Community Fridge Finder
services.description: Find community fridges containing free food near you. Go to the site and click the "Find A Fridge" button for the full map and list of fridges. Update the status of fridges in your own community.

services.name: Community Fridge at Hart and Myrtle
services.description: Community fridge in Bushwick always accepting food donations 24 hours /day. DIY don't ask just go.

services.name: Community Fridge in Brooklyn
services.description: Access the Classon Community Fridge, a refrigerator and pantry, on the street outside of Dean Crossfit that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access.

services.name: Community Fridge in Ridgewood
services.description: Visit the community fridge at 586 Seneca Ave in Ridgewood. There is free food distribution for those in need every Friday at 5pm.

services.name: Community Fridge in Washington Heights
services.description: Community Fridge in Washington Heights at 181st St & Fort Washington Ave. Take what you need, give what you can. Open 24/7.

services.name: Community Health Access to Addiction & Mental Healthcare Project (CHAMP)
services.description:
Call the CHAMP live-answer Helpline for free and confidential assistance accessing mental health and substance use disorder care.   Monday-Friday 9am-4pm. Supports multiple languages and all insurance types (including uninsured folks).

CHAMP assistance includes help finding a mental health or substance use disorder provider, appealing an insurer’s denial of care, and understanding your rights to mental health and substance use disorder care.

CHAMP is a partnership among specialist organizations, community based organizations, and the New York State Offices of Addiction Services and Supports (OASAS) and Mental Health.

services.name: Community Services for Tenants, Immigrants, Seniors, and Youth
services.description: Asian Americans for Equality (AAFE) works with clients one-on-one to ensure their rights to safe and decent housing, to secure and extend appropriate government housing subsidies, to make sure they have access to social support programs, such as food stamps and Medicaid, and to provide assistance with immigration matters.  Counselors are available in storefront offices in Manhattan’s Chinatown; the Lower East Side; Flushing, Queens; and Sunset Park, Brooklyn. Contact by phone or fill out contact form on website.

services.name: Community and Family Services Counseling and Support
services.description: SCO Family of Services provides a range of community, family, and children's services in Brooklyn and Long Island including access to counseling, community centers, literacy, after school, and employment services.

services.name: Connections 2026: A Guide for Formerly Incarcerated People in NYC
services.description: A collection of resources for formally incarcerated people. The guide includes resources related to education, money, housing, mental and physical health, substance use, and more.

services.name: Consumer Debt, Tax & Small Business Help
services.description:
For help with new and existing small businesses and not-for-profit organizations or existing HDFCs contact the Community Development Project at 212-298-3340, CommunityDevProject@legal-aid.org, or reserve a spot in our virtual clinic by completing our online questionnaire.

Visit website to access forms and questionnaires.

services.name: Cost saving programs and resources for HDFC co-op members
services.description: Call 212 479 3337 to learn more about resources for HDFC  co-ops (Housing Development Fund Corporation co-ops), including free classes, cost savings on fuel and insurance, and more.

services.name: Counseling, Legal, and other Resources for People Experiencing Domestic Abuse
services.description: All free & confidential services: 24/7 domestic violence crisis hotline at (631)329-2200, individual and group counseling, legal advocacy, a residential shelter for adults and children, and violence prevention and education programs for children, teenagers and adults, taught in local schools and community-wide.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Covenant House crisis shelter and resources for youth experiencing homelessness
services.description: Any youth 16-21 and their minor child(ren) may go 24/7 to Covenant House NY crisis shelter at 460 West 41st near the Port Authority Bus Terminal. They have beds, clothes, food, showers, laundry, chargers, toiletries, and holistic services. No referral and no immigration status restrictions. States they are a LGBTQ safe space.

services.name: Criminal-Immigration Helpline
services.description:
Immigrants and their loved ones who are affected by the criminal system, including immigrants who have been arrested, ticketed, or convicted of a crime: call the helpline for limited immigration legal advice and information, referrals for free immigration legal services, and referrals for private immigration attorneys. 

The helpline is not live. Leave a voicemail with your name and number at any time and a staff member or volunteer will contact you .

services.name: Crisis Intervention Hotline for Shelter Services
services.description: Call the Crisis Intervention Emergency Hotline at 1-888-358-2384 with questions about accessing shelter or other services, including if you have been denied access to shelter. Leave a detailed message, including your phone number. The Intervention Program is based in NYC and only able to respond to questions regarding NYC services.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Crisis Shelter for Women Survivors of Domestic Violence with Disabilities
services.description: Freedom House is a safe, confidential and fully accessible shelter that offers private living spaces of various sizes to accommodate both singles and larger families. They are also equipped to serve all survivors and their children with disabilities including (but not limited to) wheelchair users, people who are D/deaf or hard of hearing and blind or visually impaired. Call (212) 400-6470 for more information and availability or email info@bflnyc.org.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Crisis Text line: Free text-based crisis counseling
services.description: In the United States, text HOME to 741741 at anytime 24/7 to reach a volunteer crisis counselor.

services.name: Crisis Toolkit
services.description: An assortment of resources that may provide perspective, comfort, and/or tools that could be of assistance to people experiencing various sorts of tough times. Includes links to informational guides, online peer support, and more.

services.name: Day Habilitation Program for People with Developmental Disabilities
services.description:
NYC’s Day Habilitation programs are tailored to adults 18 and over. Programs provide diverse services that cater to people’s individual preferences.​

Day Habilitation is available to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are over the age of 18, in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx. 

To enroll the participant must have Medicaid, Care manager enrolled in CCO (Care Coordination Organization).
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Developmental Disabilities Services
services.description: Offers housing, employment, and other support for both children and adults. See each type of support for the best person to contact.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Dial-A-Teacher Homework Help
services.description:
What: Homework help line for students and their parents, run by classroom teachers
Where: Call (212) 777-3380
Who: Students in K-12
Hours: Monday through Thursday, 4 to 7 p.m. when school is in session.

services.name: Diaper Assistance Program
services.description:
Call 718-402-1212 Mondays between 9:30am-5pm to schedule an appointment for free diapers (walk-ins cannot be accepted at this time). Distribution is in the Bronx. 

To qualify, you must reside with a child 2 years or younger or be expecting (proof of sonogram or official doctors note required), live in the New York City area, and receive WIC and/or SNAP (food stamps). 

Required documents include:
- Photo ID
- Proof of address (no more than 90 days old-electricity bill/light bill/doctors letter/note with client’s name and address)
- Birth certificate(s) for baby or hospital discharge papers for newborn
- WIC proof (WIC app on cellphone or WIC card with a letter/note from WIC office) or Food Stamps/SNAP proof (recent budget letter)

services.name: Digital Resource Map by and for Transgender, Non-binary and/or Intersex People
services.description:
TransAtlas is a map-based guide to community organizations, agencies and spaces across the 5 boroughs of New York City, made by and for people of transgender, non-binary and/or intersex experience. 

Drawn from Callen-Lorde’s Transgender Resource guide and Surgeon guide, and made by a team of transgender folks, TransAtlas maps hundreds of services and organizations across the 5 boroughs where TGNB folks can find trans-competent and friendly resources to help with anything from primary care to hair removal, addiction support, and religious institutions. You can search through dozens of surgeons, therapists, dentists, lawyers, barbers, case managers and more.

services.name: Directory to find access, information, and funding to people seeking an abortion
services.description: A national searchable directory to find abortion care providers, funding, and support. Does not provide direct referrals or actual procedures, but instead connects you to information about places that do.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Domestic Violence Help
services.description: Call 212-568-6616 9am-5pm to access individual counseling, shelter services or help obtaining an order of protection.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Domestic Violence Hotline
services.description: Call 1-800-621-HOPE (4673) for assistance in domestic violence situations, including crisis counseling, safety planning, assistance with finding domestic violence shelters, and information about resources.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Doula Access and Care for Black and Low Income Patients
services.description: A reimbursement service that covers doula care under Medicaid. For New Yorkers who seek support through pregnancy and post partum.

services.name: Drive Change
services.description:
Drive Change runs an 3-month paid fellowship for formerly incarcerated youth ages 18-25 that focuses on hospitality/restaurant industry training and professional development. Apply online.

To apply, you must be between 18-25, and prove you have 8th grade or higher math and reading level (TABE, GED/TASC or HS DIPLOMA preferred but not necessary).

services.name: Education for families of people with developmental disabilities to obtain services
services.description:
AHRC's Family Educational Series includes workshops and informational sessions for families in obtaining services for their family member with a developmental disability and help families to come with challenges that may arise as they care for their loved one. 

Join AHRC's mailing list to receive invitation to their education workshops via email.

services.name: Emergency Financial Aid for Professional Visual Artists
services.description:
The Artists’ Fellowship provides one-time emergency aid to professional visual fine artists and their families in times of sickness, natural disaster, bereavement or unexpected extreme hardship that can be documented through paid or unpaid invoices, bills, or contracts.

Eligibility: please note that “Professional” is defined as those visual artists who make their livelihood through sales as reported on a Schedule C with a U.S. Federal tax return. An active exhibition history is also an important part of documenting “professional.”

services.name: Emergency Grant for Burials
services.description: Apply online or call 718-557-1399 for funds to meet funeral expenses for a deceased low-income New York City resident.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Emergency Meal Delivery for Homebound Elderly New Yorkers
services.description:
This resource is only accessible through a case management agency. If eligible, enter address to get the phone number for the Case Management Agency of your district. The Case Management Agency will guide you through the process of getting meals. 

To qualify, you:
-Must be 60 years of age or older
-Must be physically or mentally incapacitated and in need of some assistance
-Must be unable to prepare nutritious meals or have no one to do so for you
-Must be able to live safely at home if services are provided for you
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Emergency Rental Assistance Program
services.description: New York State Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) will provide economic relief to help low and moderate-income households at risk of experiencing homelessness or housing instability by providing rental arrears, temporary rental assistance and utility arrears assistance. No immigration status requirements to apply. See website for eligibility and application requirements. Funds are not always available, so check website to see if applications are currently being accepted.

services.name: Emotional Support and Crisis Response Hotline
services.description: Call 212-673-3000 to reach The Samaritans of New York completely confidential 24-hour emotional support and crisis response hotline. It's available on an immediate and ongoing basis for individuals who are dealing with every kind of problem, situation, illness, trauma or loss and need someone to talk to who will listen and take you seriously.

services.name: Employment Opportunities for the Long-Term Unemployed
services.description:
The Doe Fund offers employment opportunities for people who have experienced long-term unemployment but who are not homeless. To learn more, call one of the facilities or email info@doe.org: 
Brooklyn: 646-672-2973
Harlem: 718-417-2538

services.name: Employment Services: Job Readiness, Training, and Counseling
services.description: Urban Upbound’s Employment Services team provides job readiness training and one-on-one counseling to help community members gain and retain meaningful employment. Includes job readiness assistance, 1:1 counseling, job training, and computer labs.

services.name: Empowered NYC: Financial Counseling and Coaching
services.description: Fill out the online form to schedule free one-on-one financial counseling. Help with debt reduction, credit scores, savings, budgeting, opening a bank account, and preparing income information for housing applications. Appointment options may be in-person or by phone.

services.name: English, Citizenship Prep, and Community Health Worker Training Classes
services.description:
Complete the online form to apply to Make the Road adult education programs, including: 
- English classes for speakers of other languages 
- Citizenship preparation
- Community health worker training program (Brooklyn only)

For more information, call your preferred location in Bushwick, Jackson Heights, Port Richmond, Brentwood, or White Plains.

services.name: Entertainment Community Fund Emergency Financial Assistance & List of Additional Funds
services.description: Emergency Financial Assistance is available to eligible performing arts and entertainment professionals in times of unexpected critical need and to assist towards basic living expenses such as health care, housing and utilities to prevent eviction or shut-offs. Multiple funds in the entertainment industries are available to apply to, covering a variety of eligibility restrictions.

services.name: Episcopal Actors Guild Fund for Performers in Financial Crisis
services.description: You must live in one of the five NYC boroughs and have an established career working as a performer for at least five consecutive years. Call (212)-685-2927 if you think you may be eligible for the program. EAG's programs and services focus primarily on sustaining and supporting the careers of working performers. At the heart of EAG's charitable outreach is the EARP. Through this program, we give grants to qualified performers in financial crisis regardless of religion, race, national origin or ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental ability, political ideology/affiliations, or language. Through EARP we address critical issues like eviction, housing court stipulations, utility shutoffs, emergency medical and dental costs, and sustenance needs like food and transportation.

services.name: Eviction Prevention Program
services.description: People in danger of being evicted can call the Eviction Prevention Hotline at 888-850-2712 on Wednesday mornings beginning at 9:30 am. Appointments are limited and first-come, first-serve. To qualify for a one-time payment of $1000 (on average), you must be in court, have a signed court stipulation, and have future ability to pay your ongoing rent.

services.name: Exchange childcare with people you trust
services.description: Carefully is a free playdate and childcare exchange platform to build a network of parents you know and trust to share care, redefining the traditional 'care circle' model for the digital age (available for iOS and Android).

services.name: Family Support Program and Benefits Counseling in the Bronx
services.description: Call 718-839-1100 to learn more about WHEDco's Family Support Services or to ask for an appointment. Family support services include public benefits counseling for benefits such as: SNAP, WIC referrals, cash assistance (PA, TANF, SafetyNet), Safelink and Assurance cell phones, social security, health insurance, citizenship and green card applications and renewals (plus fee waiver assistance), housing applications, Senior Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE), and childcare.

services.name: Financial Counseling and Workshops for South Asian Small Businesses
services.description:
To apply for services, fill out survey on the website. 

Chhaya is a community development corporation with the mission to build the power, housing stability, and economic well-being of South Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities. Chhaya executes this work by providing free direct services in the areas of housing counseling and homeownership, asset building and financial empowerment, policy and advocacy, and community organizing.

services.name: Financial Support for Black Transgender People
services.description:
A Black, trans-led collective that curates parties to fundraise money to help Black transgender people pay for their rent, gender-affirming surgeries, smaller co-pays for medicines/doctor’s visits, and travel assistance. Visit website to view currently available applications and to apply for assistance programs. 

Only open to Black transgender people. Application through website. Depending on services, social media access might be necessary.

services.name: Financial guidance, marketing, and planning support for small businesses
services.description: Small Business Support Specialists offer businesses that are opening or reopening support with applying for grants and loans, digital marketing, getting online, lease negotiations, and business planning.

services.name: Find Food Assistance By Address
services.description: Enter an address to find a directory of nearby food assistance resources, including pantries and meal programs.

services.name: Find a Food Pantry Map
services.description:
Visit the link to view a map of food banks operating in New York City. 

NOTE: Hours vary - call ahead to confirm when a food bank will be open.

services.name: Find an HRSA-Funded Health Center Tool
services.description: Find a Health Center the receives government Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) funding by location. Primary care health services should be available at a reduced cost or free of charge depending on your economic status.

services.name: Fiscal Hosting for Mutual Aid Groups in New York City
services.description: NYC Mutual Aid Groups looking for a fiscal sponsor can get in touch at pactbk@gmail.com. A fiscal sponsor is an entity that holds money on behalf of a collective, and takes care of accounting, taxes, and invoices.

services.name: Food Career Training Program
services.description: Apply for this free program on the "career programs" page. This resource is available for women and nonbinary people over 18 who are looking to find a job in food and restaurant services. Must be able to actively take courses for 5 weeks.

services.name: Food Distribution Tuesdays in Washington Square Park
services.description: Weekly distro of food, hot coffee, and more on Tuesdays 12:30pm-2:30pm in Washington Square Park across from Holley Statue. Take what you want, leave what you can.

services.name: Free & Confidential Mental Health Support via Call Or Text
services.description:
Text or call 988 for Free & Confidential Mental Health + Substance Use Support open 24/7. A chat service is also available on the website.

Interpreters are available for 200+ languages. Stay on the line, and you will be connected with a counselor who can connect you to translator services.

services.name: Free & Low-Cost Primary Care, Behavioral Health Services, Dental and Podiatry for the Homeless
services.description: Call (833) 423-4273 24/7 for information or a same-day appointment. Find walk-in locations on the website. You will be treated regardless of your ability to pay.

services.name: Free Abortion Clinic and Pill Directory
services.description: Search the database to find verified abortion clinics near you that keeps your information private.

services.name: Free Adult English Classes
services.description:
A 10-month program to help improve  listening, reading, speaking and writing skills. Textbooks are provided. We offer English for Speakers of Other Language (ESOL) classes at a variety of levels to adult immigrant students during the daytime, evenings, and weekends, free of charge.

Requirements: 
- Must be at least 18 years old
- Must be a NYC resident and provide proof of address
- Must be able to attend 10 months of in-person classes

services.name: Free Assistance with Health Insurance, Healthcare, Medicaid
services.description: Call (888) 614-5400 or email cha@cssny.org for assistance with understanding how to use your health insurance, resolving medical billing and debt issues, disputing coverage denials and eligibility determinations, getting the most from your coverage (get prior authorizations, access specialists, and out-of-network services when needed), accessing affordable health care services, and hospital and prescription financial assistance program.

services.name: Free Baby Formula Exchange
services.description: Submit an online form to offer or request baby formula on this nationwide platform. You can also search for available formula by location and contact donors directly.

services.name: Free Benefits Counseling for People with Disabilities
services.description:
Call 1-844-862-7930 to reach counselors available 9 am until 5 pm, Monday through Friday. You can also request to be contacted by a counselor by filling out the form at https://www.cidny.org/getnyconnects
Support includes SNAP, Unemployment Insurance, Social Security, Medicaid, etc. for people with disabilities and older adults; help getting connected with various resources including food, toiletries, mental health, etc.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Free Bikes for Fellow New Yorkers
services.description: Donate a spare bike or apply for a free one at bikematch.nyc. Fill out a form, get paired with a neighbor of about the same height, and arrange a time to meet up and exchange the bike.

services.name: Free Clinic Directory
services.description: Free Clinic Directory is a directory of medical and dental clinics and community health centers that can help low-income and uninsured people by offering free and discounted rates for medical and/or dental care. Search by location, name, or phone number.

services.name: Free Counseling and Assistance with Medicare
services.description: Call 1-800-333-4114 to get assistance with understanding Medicare benefits, making enrollment decisions, coordinating Medicare with other insurance, appealing denials of care, determining eligibility for Medicare cost-saving programs, or another topic.

services.name: Free Daily Showers
services.description:
Hot showers, fresh towels and toiletries are available.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Ave
8:30-11:30 a.m. / 12:30-2:20 p.m.
Monday-Friday

services.name: Free Dating Abuse and Domestic Violence Services and Resources for Youth Under 24 Years Old

community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Free Diapers and Wipes for Brooklyn Families
services.description: ​Visit Rain or Shine Diaper Fund every Monday at The Living Gallery in Brooklyn, NY, to receive free diapers and wipes. Get a number at 8am, and distribution is at 1pm. No ID or sign-up required.

services.name: Free Digital Mental Health Resources
services.description: Library of apps and online services offering mental health support, including for depression, anxiety, and addiction.

services.name: Free Downloadable Deportation Defense Manual
services.description: Read this to familiarize yourself with how to respond to ICE.  Broken into three sections: Know Your Rights, Rapid Response to Raids, and Deportation Defense.

services.name: Free Educational Courses, SAT and AP Prep
services.description: Access Khan Academy’s library of practice and lessons covering math K-12 through early college, grammar, science, history, AP®, SAT®, and more. Free for learners and teachers.

services.name: Free Food Delivery for East Asian Elders throughout NYC
services.description:
Deliver weekly hot lunches, fresh produce, and bulk ingredients to East Asian elders while supporting local small businesses.

Fill out the form to join the waitlist. During the next onboarding cycle, they will review your eligibility for receiving Heart of Dinner care packages for free. The criteria:

1. Be a local NYC Asian American person aged 60 or above.
2. Have a gross monthly income as a single elderly at or below $1,869; or have a gross monthly income as an elderly couple at or below $2,518.
3. Unable to prepare meals because of the lack of money to purchase food, inability to shop or cook, or lack of facilities.
4. Isolated due to lack of family, friend or neighbor support.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Mondays and Saturdays in Astoria
services.description: Pick up a pre-packaged bag of groceries Mondays 8am-10:30am and Saturdays 1-1:30pm. No sign-up, id, or name required. 25-82 Steinway St in Queens.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays at Woodside Houses
services.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays 1:30pm at the Woodside Houses at 49th St & Broadway

services.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Tompkins Square Park
services.description: Free food distribution Saturdays, 11am at Tompkins Square Park at the corner of East 7th Street & Avenue B. Dropoff donations of food and goods can be received at the distro 10:45-noon.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Woodside at the 61st St-Woodside Station
services.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays at 1:30pm at the 61st St-Woodside MTA Station in Queens.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Second Saturdays in Jamaica
services.description: Free food and produce distribution at 12pm every 2nd Saturday of the month at the corner of Jamaica Ave and Parsons Blvd, outside of the old Jamaica Multiplex.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Sundays in Tompkins Square Park
services.description: Free food distribution Sundays, 12-2pm in the SW corner of Tompkins Square park at Ave A and East 7th St.

services.name: Free Food Distribution Thursdays in Sunnyside
services.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Sunnyside on Thursdays at 1:15pm at Bliss Plaza on Queens Blvd & 46th St.

services.name: Free Food Distribution, Clothing, & Community Care on Saturdays in the Bronx
services.description: Pick up free produce, hot food, clothing, books, and toiletries every Saturday from 1 - 2pm @ St. Mary's Park 601 E. 149th St, Bronx, NY.

services.name: Free Food and Clothing Distribution in Brooklyn
services.description: Tuesdays, 12-2pm at 1046 Broadway in Brooklyn. Free food distribution available to anyone.

services.name: Free Gender-Affirming Clothes and Resources - Marsha's Closet
services.description: Give what you can, take what you need! Pull up every 3rd Monday of the month on 135th and St Nick to drop off/pick up Clothing Donations for our queer and unhoused community in Harlem & beyond.

services.name: Free Grocery and Supply Delivery
services.description: Free grocery and supply delivery to elderly, disabled, and/or immunocompromised New Yorkers. Call (732) 639-1579 (open seven days a week) or fill out the form on the website to request a delivery.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Free Haircuts
services.description:
Free haircuts for the first 30 clients (with ticket - given at POTS) of all ages.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue. Starts at 8:30 am – First 30 Clients Tuesday and Thursday.

services.name: Free Health Clinic for Sex Workers
services.description: Sex workers can call 212-271-8134 to schedule an appointment with COIN, a free healthcare program through Callen-Lorde for sex workers in an affirming, supportive environment. The clinic offers primary medical care, sexual health, HIV treatment & prevention, transgender health, GYN care, and more.

services.name: Free Healthcare for Ages 10-26, Including Primary Care
services.description: Call (212) 423-3000 for free and confidential care for young people ages 10-26. Fundamental care for all patients includes primary care, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, social services, optical, health education and prescriptions, plus specialized services for LGBTQ young people, teen parents, young people living with HIV, and young people dealing with trauma.

services.name: Free Housing Legal Services & Eviction Prevention Program
services.description:
Call 718-538-3344 Ext. 100 or 117, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm.
NAICA's primary focus is geared towards providing legal eviction prevention services to families and individuals who are working, receiving public assistance, or that meet the low-income eligibility and are at risk of losing their homes.

services.name: Free Legal Hotline for People with Limited Income
services.description:
Call the Legal Hotline or fill out an online application to connect with staff attorneys who assist callers of limited income on a range of civil legal issues, including matrimonial and family law, housing law, domestic violence, bankruptcy, and debt collection and benefits. Our staff includes bilingual attorneys who speak English and Spanish, and we can accept calls in any language through interpreting services.

The Hotline is open Monday through Thursday from 10am-12pm and 2pm-4pm, and Friday from 9am-12pm.

services.name: Free Legal Support for New Yorkers
services.description:
Call 917-661-4500 for the Access Line to speak to an intake specialist in any language.

The website also includes FAQs for common legal questions including topics related to immigration and asylum, LGBTQ+ rights, health and disability rights, housing and foreclosure, and more.

services.name: Free Legal Support for People Experiencing Poverty or In Crisis
services.description: For legal assistance or financial counseling, contact the office by either filling out the online intake form or calling and leaving a message with full name, contact info, and description of legal or financial counseling needs. Legal support focuses on helping immigrants, survivors of violence and discrimination, and people who need support securing access to health care and essential benefits, demanding safe and affordable housing , and protecting their economic rights.

services.name: Free Legal and Social Services Support for Low Income People in the Bronx
services.description:
Call 718-838-7878 (Mon-Fri 9am-4pm) for free legal and social services for immigration, housing, criminal, and family defense, as well as social work support and advocacy. Legal Emergency Hotline: 347-778-1266 (Available 24/7)
Housing Hotline: 347-842-1122 (Available two Mondays* every month, from 9:00AM to 5:00PM)

services.name: Free Meal Distribution Saturdays in Greenpoint
services.description: Visit Greenpoint Community Kitchen at 155 Milton Street every Saturday from 11 am to 1 pm to receive hot meals and coffee. Meals can be enjoyed on-site or taken to go. Bread is packaged and available to take home as well.

services.name: Free Meals in Park Slope
services.description: CHiPS serves breakfast (9-10:30am) and lunch (11:30am-1pm) Monday-Saturday at 200 4th Avenue in Park Slope Brooklyn. Meals are available to anyone who is in need.

services.name: Free Mediation Services for Brooklyn and Manhattan
services.description: New York Peace Institute offers free in-person mediation for Brooklyn and Manhattan residents. Also offers conflict coaching and restorative processes to help you resolve your conflict.

services.name: Free Medical and Dental Clinic
services.description: Free Clinic operated by Care for the Homeless at our POTS 2759 Webster Avenue location.

services.name: Free Mental Health Crisis Intervention for LGBTQ Youth via Phone Hotline, Text, or Chat
services.description: Call 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678-678 if you are thinking about harming yourself. Get immediate crisis support, connect to a crisis counselor 24/7, 365 days a year, from anywhere in the U.S via text, chat, or phone. Confidential and free.

services.name: Free Mental Health Support for Parents
services.description: State-wide help line to support parents before and after having a baby. Call 7 days a week, 9am-5pm to access non-judgmental and confidential emotional support, educational information, healthcare and support group resources, and to connect to parental mental health peer support groups.

services.name: Free Monthly Grocery Distribution in Brooklyn
services.description: Grocery distributions at 641 Classon Avenue on the second Monday of each month.

services.name: Free National Mental Health HelpLine
services.description: Call 1-800-950-6264 (NAMI) or email info@nami.org, Monday-Friday, 10am to 10pm. Operators can provide information about mental illness and refer callers to treatment, support groups, family support, and legal support, if needed.

services.name: Free Phone Caption Service
services.description: Caption service for phone calls. Can be used on internet phones, landlines, and mobile phones. You must be a U.S. resident and certify that your hearing loss inhibits your ability to use the phone.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Free Programs and Services for Young People Ages 12 to 24
services.description: The Door offers a variety of services in health, mental health, legal, education, arts, housing, and more for youth and young people ages 12 through 24.

services.name: Free Rapid PCR Testing in Brooklyn
services.description:
Periodic free Rapid PCR tests for COVID, Flu A + B, and RSV. If you are positive for any of them, G-REBELS will provide you with a care kit and discuss support services so you can focus on rest and recovery. 

Tests, kits, and support services are completely free of charge to community members, but are limited to the uninsured to prioritize those who need it most. 

Find upcoming appointment times and locations on Instagram or the sign-up form.

services.name: Free Resources - Children's Mental Health and Learning Challenges
services.description: Visit the Family Resource Center to find information to help support children who are struggling with mental health, behavior or learning challenges. Resources available in English and Spanish.

services.name: Free Services for Residents of Upper Manhattan and the Bronx
services.description: Call the hotline at 929-415-8970 to get assistance in a number of areas including a food pantry, tax preparation, unemployment insurance, benefits, housing, or immigration needs.

services.name: Free Showers and Personal Hygiene
services.description: Get free showers, toiletries, clean clothes, snacks, and water with Shower Power NYC’s Fresh City program in Harlem (Mon/Fri at Harlem United) and Ridgewood (Tues at Ridgewood Presbyterian Church), 10am–2pm. No ID or appointment needed.

services.name: Free Store in Greenpoint
services.description: Free store open 24/7 at the corner of Adelphi St and Greene Ave in Greenpoint. Anyone can come anytime to donate or take items from the store’s shelves, from clothing and linens to toys and home decor. Please no large items, make sure things are suitable for redistribution, and help keep things tidy.

services.name: Free Vegan Meal Distribution Sundays in the Lower East Side
services.description: Free vegan meals served every Sunday at 4:30pm inside the SW corner of Tompkins Square Park (E 7th st & Ave A).

services.name: Free Vegetable Distribution Sundays in Queens
services.description: Free veggie distro every Sunday, ~2:30pm at Roosevelt Ave & 58th St in Woodside, Queens until November 2026.

services.name: Free Virtual Support Groups for Eating Disorders
services.description:
Communities of Healing virtual support groups are free and open to anyone with an eating disorder. Each group is facilitated by someone who has personally experienced and recovered from an eating disorder. Groups meet weekly to share with and learn from other people who understand what it means to fight for recovery.

To join, fill out the information request form, and ANAD will contact you with more information and joining info.

services.name: Free Virtual Tutoring for NYC Public School Students
services.description: EduMate NYC provides free virtual tutoring from volunteer college students for K-12 students enrolled in the NYC public school system. Priority will be given to students who are on free and reduced-price meal programs. Our tutoring covers all traditional school subjects, standardized test prep, and the college application process!

services.name: Free Water Testing Kits for Lead
services.description: Fill out the request form to receive a free kit to test your drinking water for lead. The kit comes with a pre-paid label to send it to a laboratory for lead analysis, and the results will be mailed to you within 30 days of the sample being tested. Limited to one per household at a time.

services.name: Free confidential anti-violence chat & hotline in multiple languages
services.description:
Highly trained helpline advocates can answer general questions about domestic violence, human trafficking, and sexual violence across the lifespan, provide crisis counseling and help develop safety plans, and/or make referrals for ongoing support. Womankind also provides emergency safety shelter.

Online chat & text available Mon-Fri 10am-6pm (English, Chinese)
Text Womankind for help in: English 1.929.207.5907, Chinese 1.929.207.5901
24-Hour Multilingual Helpline: 1.888.888.7702 (English, Spanish and 18+ Asian languages and dialects, including Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Tagalog, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, and Vietnamese)
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Free dancing lessons, group exercise, and interactive activities
services.description: The Y @ Home includes free programs for all ages and populations open to the wider community, including exercise activities, congregate lunches, dance classes, and more.

services.name: Free diabetes supplies/medication, insurance/PAP help
services.description:
Mutual Aid Diabetes (MAD) is available to help anyone with any type of diabetes to access free or low cost supplies and medication as well as assist with insurance coverage and patient assistance programs. To request aid, please fill out our intake form here: https://airtable.com/shrr0XQLbZXNn1oGv.

Aid hotline (text or call): 646-780-9571
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Free food, clothes and supplies in Washington Square Park
services.description: WSP Mutual Aid collects and distributes free food, clothes, and supplies in Washington Square Park every Friday starting at 5pm.

services.name: Free healthcare access application for people with HIV/AIDS
services.description: The Uninsured Care Programs provide access to free health care (Drugs, Outpatient Primary Care, Home Care, Insurance Premium Payments, and Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to prevent HIV infection) for New York State residents who are uninsured or underinsured. The Uninsured Care Programs are committed to working closely with providers and individuals to support access to the wide range of options for payment for health care services and medications for persons living with or at risk of acquiring HIV/AIDS.

services.name: Free job training and placements
services.description: The HOPE Program is a non-profit organization that offers 5 different job training programs: job readiness training, construction training, industry certifications such as OSHA-30 internships, HSE prep, job placement, and more. Virtual Info sessions every Tuesday and Thursday at 1pm, as well as in-person info sessions every Wednesday at 1pm at both HOPE locations. Call 347-7730-4623 to learn how to apply. Government ID required.

services.name: Free legal services for immigrant New Yorkers
services.description:
Call the city-funded, free, and safe MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365, or call 311 and say, "Immigration Legal," between 9:00am to 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, to get help in any language:

Get answers to immigration policy questions and information on how and where to find help at Legal Support Centers across the City, housed in community sites, public health facilities, public schools, and libraries. Must be a New York City resident and making 200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

services.name: Free meal delivery for people with severe or chronic illness
services.description:
If you or someone you know is living with a severe or chronic illness and having trouble shopping or cooking, visit our website to confirm eligibility and apply for free, medically-tailored meals delivered to your door.

To be eligible, you must be living with a serious illness and have an ADL (Activities of Daily Living) limitation that prevents you from shopping or cooking for yourself which must be verified by a healthcare provider. Application forms and supporting documentation are available on the website and can be submitted electronically or mailed.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Free mental health resources for BIPOC in NYC
services.description: Visit the website to get connected to free resources and tools including "Find Me a Therapist", a Black Mental Health Resource Packet, and a Black Mental Health Provider Database.

services.name: Free weekly grocery distribution in Bedstuy and Long Island
services.description:
Find a Food Share location and weekly date/time on the website: Bedstuy, Farmingville, Wyandanch, Hemstead, and Huntington

Anyone can come to a Community Solidarity Food Share and get most, if not all, of the groceries they need for the week. Each Food Share is a free supermarket where community members share instead of pay for what they need. There are no prerequisites, there is no paperwork, all are welcome and everyone will be helped. We also share clothing, books, toys, school supplies, and other necessities.

services.name: Friendly VOICES Program
services.description: The Friendly VOICES program builds friendships and limits social isolation for older adults who are isolated for reasons such as COVID-19. Volunteers can do virtual or in-person visits. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or apply online.

services.name: From Shelter to Apartment: A Guide to New York City's Department of Homeless Services
services.description: A foldout poster (English and Spanish versions) that breaks down people’s rights in homeless shelters and the different programs available to help them leave shelter and find affordable permanent housing. It also provides resources on other services shelter residents may have access to, like transportation benefits and storage grants, and what to do when your rights have been violated.

services.name: Gay Men’s Health Crisis (GMHC) Hotline
services.description: Call 1-800-243-7692 for a safe space to discuss a wide range of concerns. They provide information about topics such as HIV/AIDS, STDs, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), sexual health, and resources such as testing, healthcare, benefits, and counseling.

services.name: Generation Q, at Queens Community House
services.description: An after-school youth center for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer youth and allies, between the ages of 13 and 21. They offer a wide variety of educational and recreational opportunities, as well as social and emotional support. Open Tuesday through Friday 3-7pm.

services.name: Get Someone to Accompany You During an ICE Checkin Date
services.description: Got an upcoming ICE check-in date? Fill out the form linked on the website with your name, email, and ICE check-in date, and Families for Freedom staff will reach out to accompany you during the process.

services.name: Growing Up Healthy Hotline for Families with Children
services.description:
Call the hotline anytime at 1-800-522-5006. We're open 24/7. TTY 1-800-655-1789.

Help is available for health care, nutrition, pregnancy, family planning, children's needs, and more.

services.name: Guidance on Applying for WIC for Families with Children
services.description: Information on how to apply for WIC. The WIC program provides support with accessing food, nutrition education, and resources for expecting parents and caregivers. Government ID required.

services.name: Guide to Reduced-Cost Veterinary Care
services.description: An informational guide to programs offering financial assistance to help pay for veterinary care for your companion animals in the New York City area.

services.name: Harlem Community Fridge at 155th St
services.description: Harlem community fridge open 24/7 at 155th St and Bradhurst. Fresh produce on Saturdays 11 AM-1pm, and hot meals on Sundays 3-5pm.

services.name: Health Insurance Enrollment Assistance
services.description:
Free or inexpensive public health insurance is available for those meeting financial eligibility requirements.
Call 1-855-355-5777 to enroll directly or call the Medicaid Helpline (800) 541-2831 for assistance.
Free enrollment assistance through city - call 311 or text CoveredNYC (SeguroNYC en Español) to 877877.
For assistance enrolling through a local community-based organization: call (888) 614-5400 or email enroll@cssny.org.
All NYC Health + Hospitals centers will provide healthcare regardless of insurance coverage, and can help with insurance enrollment: call 1-844-NYC-4NYC.

services.name: Health Insurance Information, Counseling and Assistance Program
services.description: Call 1-800-701-0501 Monday - Friday, 8:30am-5pm to get answers to questions about Medicare, Medicare Advantage programs (managed care), Medicare prescription drug coverage, Medigap, and other health and long-term care insurance issues

services.name: Health Services for Indigenous New Yorkers
services.description: Call 718-215-8417 or enroll online to schedule health services or receive referrals at no charge. Services include urgent and emergency care, preventive care, primary and specialty care, behavioral health & recovery support, and transportation assistance. Note that we are only able to cover services arranged or referred by NYIC in advance. NYIC cannot reimburse members for services they book or receive independently (i.e. without prior approval).

services.name: Health and Disability Benefits support for People Living with HIV/AIDS
services.description: Call the Legal Aid Society's HIV/AIDS Representation Project’s helpline at 718-579-8989 if you are a person living with HIV/AIDS and need assistance with a legal matter.

services.name: Health and Human Services Help
services.description: Call 1.844.ONE.CALL (1.844.663.2255) during business hours to make an appointment for assistance including with mental health, family violence, and intellectual and developmental disabilities. There are no eligibility requirements.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence
People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Health insurance enrollment, benefits screening, legal services, financial services, parenting guidance, and other services
services.description: Call 212-471-2400 to make an appointment for Dale Jones Burch Neighborhood Center, located at 269 Henry Street on the Lower East Side. Services include health insurance enrollment, benefits screening, legal services, financial services, and parenting guidance.

services.name: Healthcare Enrollment Help Hotline
services.description:
Call 844-614-8800 for assistance with enrolling in and using managed care plans that cover long term care or behavioral health services.
Services include one-on-one counseling about health insurance options by phone or live chat on their website.

services.name: Help Line to Access Resources for Families of Children and Young Adults with Disabilities
services.description:
IncludeNYC seeks to support families who have children with disabilities for people ages 0-26 years of age. Services include providing access to education, family advocacy, employment and will assist in gaining independent living status. Call the help line to gain access to resources.
Helpline:  call: 212-677-4660
                 text: 646-693-3175

Español: llame: 212-677-4668
                texto: 646-693-3175
                whatsapp: 212-858-0795

You do not need to have a disability diagnosis to call, and immigration status is not considered.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Help for Seniors Accessing Benefits & Support
services.description: Call to make an appointment or find out about a regularly scheduled social work clinics. Connect with case managers for help to access benefits, including medical, financial, housing, and other needs; and get references for legal care and mental health care. Or enroll in the Daily Money Management program to help seniors with day-to-day financial tasks.

services.name: Help with Eviction Prevention and Other Issues at POTS Legal Clinic
services.description: Speak with an attorney or legal advocate if you are behind on your rent or otherwise in danger of eviction, or for help accessing public benefits. POTS can also offer brief advice and referrals on other legal issues. Call 718-220-4892, ext. 101 and leave a message or send an email to legalclinc@potsbronx.org.

services.name: Help with Moving Expenses
services.description: Assistance for HRA clients related to moving, including help with moving expenses, broker's fees, and NYCHA security deposits. See Special Grant Document Guide webpage for specific forms.

services.name: Helpline For Education-Related Information in New York City
services.description:
Call (866) 427-6033 Monday through Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm to speak to an education specialist. 

Advocates for Children’s Jill Chaifetz Education Helpline is a resource for information and guidance on all education-related matters in New York City. If your child is struggling in school or experiencing school discrimination of any kind, specialists will assess the problem and provide free assistance, ranging from information you can use to advocate on your own, or assign you an education specialist or attorney to work with you directly.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Hire Harm-Reduction Medics with Sliding-Scale Rates for Events
services.description:
Hire harm-reduction medics from PartySafe Medics on a sliding-scale for events. Message on SMS, Signal, or WhatsApp, or visit the website or Instagram @partysafemedics. 

Services include safer drug use education, first aid, and overdose prevention. Medics are supplied with Naloxone, drug testing strips, safer drug use supplies, sexual health and hygiene products, oxygen tanks, and more.

services.name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP): Money for Heat, Cooling, and Utility Expenses
services.description: Apply for money to pay for fuel, your utility source, equipment and/or repairs through the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP). Apply online or call the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance at 800-692-0557 for assistance. A government ID is required.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

services.name: Home Health Care Services and Assistance
services.description:
A range of home health care services to meet the needs of eligible persons with and without disabilities, including home health aides, personal care aides / companions, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapies, respiratory therapy, and social work services

To contact or ask questions about home health care services, contact the referral and information center, available 24/7, or visit the office Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

Fill out the form to contact the referral and information center. Additionally, they accept fee-for-service and long-term care insurance.

services.name: Home-Based Childcare Program
services.description: Contact WHEDco’s Home-Based Childcare Program (HBCC) at 347-708-7800. They work with families to help them explore options, determine their eligibility for childcare subsidies, and provide orientation on how to select the right caregiver for their needs. Also offer support services to licensed, registered, and legally-exempt service providers through the Home-Based Childcare Training Program.

services.name: Homebase: Support for housing stability to avoid shelter entry
services.description:
Call 311 or visit nyc.gov/homebase to learn more about housing resources provided by the city of New York. Services include eviction prevention, assistance obtaining public benefits, employment search and assistance, financial counseling, relocation resources, and short-term financial assistance. This program is especially intended for individuals at imminent risk of entering the NYC shelter system/experiencing homelessness. 

Homebase is a homelessness prevention network with 26 locations across NYC’s five boroughs. Use the homebase locator to find the location in your borough.

This resource is currently only available over the phone. To access the hotline, call 311 and ask for homebase services. This service is specifically for people at risk of eviction/houselessness, and may not be useful for individuals already experiencing houselessness. 

A government ID is required.

services.name: Homeless Services for Individuals and Families in NYC
services.description: Works to provide a a steady and growing pipeline of permanent low-income housing, and other services such as eviction support.

services.name: Homeownership assistance for low-to-moderate income families in Queens
services.description: Non-profit offering a variety of free and low-cost counseling and seminars to aid people in achieving and maintaining homeownership.

services.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Immigrants
services.description: Call the MinKwon Center at 718-460-5600 for help with benefits enrollment, setting up vaccination appointments, immigration services, food, medicine, and rental assistance.

services.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Jewish Victims of Domestic Abuse
services.description: Call/text/Whatsapp 888.883.2323 to speak to someone confidentially to talk about a domestic abuse situation. Shalom Task Force’s Legal Department also provides free, confidential legal services to victim-survivors of domestic and dating abuse, specializing in the Jewish community.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Hotline for LGBTQ and HIV-affected Survivors of Violence
services.description: Call 212-714-1141 to reach a free, bilingual (English/Spanish), 24-hour, 365-day-a-year crisis intervention hotline that offers support to LGBTQ & HIV-affected survivors of any type of violence, as well as to those who love and support survivors, including those who have lost a loved one to violence.

services.name: Hotline for Substance Use Disorder and Mental Health Care Resources
services.description: Call 888-614-5400 for assistance in accessing treatment and insurance coverage for substance use disorders and mental health treatment. Hotline is confidential.

services.name: Housing Court Hotline
services.description: Call (212) 962-4795 Monday-Friday 9-5 for information about housing court procedures, landlord & tenant rules and regulations, enforcement of housing code violations, and referrals for free legal help and other community organizations.

services.name: Housing Workshops to Learn About Housing Lottery Application Process
services.description:
See website for locations to book an appointment. Receive step-by-step advice on what to expect through the housing lottery application process, including a review of the application and other required documents; information on financial empowerment and managing credit and debt portfolios; and additional support through the selection and interview process. 

In addition to larger workshops, CUFFH also provides One-on-One Application Assistance including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

services.name: Housing and Homelessness Prevention
services.description: Tenants can call 718-592-5757 ext. 243, email skhan@qchnyc.org, or email mmoore@qchnyc.org to access housing counseling and tenants rights workshops and receive help with applying for rental subsidies, negotiating lease renewals, and obtaining apartment unit repairs. Low-income individuals and families who at risk of eviction can access: household risk assessment, application assistance, access to government benefits, budget counseling and advocacy, including referrals to Food Access, Health Care, Public Assistance, legal and other supportive services to help people remain housed and stable.

services.name: How to Set Up a Mutual Aid Fund
services.description: A September 2020 essay about how the STL Mutual Aid Fund was set up, with tips for other mutual aid organizers.

services.name: How to Start and Run a Bulk Buying Club With Your Community
services.description:
A guide to starting and running a bulk food buying club. This covers: food sourcing, organizing members, running operation, and logistics. Also includes information about different student-run
bulk buying clubs in the CoFED network to learn about their strategies.

services.name: Immigrant Legal Support for Survivors of Violence and Abuse
services.description: We help immigrant survivors of violence and abuse obtain status and protection, enabling them to live and work safely in the United States. Our work focuses on humanitarian-based relief created specifically for immigrant survivors, such as U-visas, VAWA self-petitions and asylum, as well as “green card” applications, naturalization, and removal defense. We work with people from around the world who have experienced trauma and offer services in any language.

services.name: Residential Services and Support for People with Developmental Disabilities
services.description:
To apply, contact the referral and information center. Call 212-780-4491 to get more information on making referrals or contact the Referral and Information Center online at https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/. 

Residential supports fall under three models:
1. Individualized Residential Alternatives (IRAs)
Supervised IRAs are traditional family-style group homes, providing 24-hour staff support and supervision for up to 14 residents.
Supportive IRAs provide need-based supports and services for those who are living in their own homes or apartments but do not require 24-hour staff support and supervision. Supportive IRAs are limited to 3 or fewer residents.
2. Supervised Apartments
3. Residential settings for people who are medically fragile (with 24/7 Nursing Care) AHRC NYC operates two residences for aging individuals who require full-time nursing oversight.  Support staff are comprised of nurse practitioners and supervising registered nurses, who are on-site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  Residents also have access to speech, physical, and occupational therapies as needed, as well as a day habilitation program operated within the residence.
