services.name: Rights Recorder and Chatbot: Report Housing Discrimination
services.description: Turned down by a landlord or broker because of your housing voucher? Record a call and/or report it using the Unlock NYC chatbot and they'll help hold them accountable.

services.name: RiseBoro HSE/ESL Program (English and Spanish)
services.description:
Fill out the form to access free HSE Adult Education classes at RiseBoro (English and Spanish). Classes are designed to prepare students for the Test Assessing Secondary Completion (TASC) that will provide them with a High School Equivalency Diploma. Students will receive instruction in reading comprehension, writing, social studies, science and math. 
The Free English as a Second Language (ESL) classes (Level I - Level IV) are for non-native English speakers to improve listening, speaking, reading and writing.

services.name: SAG-AFTRA Emergency Financial Assistance
services.description: See website for application and eligibility details. Emergency financial assistance is available for SAG-ASTRA members who are in urgent financial need due to an unexpected life crisis such as a natural disaster, accident, health crisis creating a financial burden, loss of work due to an illness, loss of housing due to an eviction, death in the family, or other emergency crisis situations covered under IRS guidelines which pertain to granting tax-free monies to individuals.

services.name: SNAP Enrollment Assistance
services.description: Call 347-880-2922 to speak to local Met Council Nutrition Outreach and Education Program (NOEP) coordinator to help to determine if you are eligible to apply for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and help you complete and submit your application. Free and confidential.

services.name: Safe Homes Project - Domestic Violence Programs
services.description:
24-Hour Hotline 718-499-2151

Good Shepherd Services’ Safe Homes Project provides an array of free services, which include a hotline, counseling, safety-planning, as well as a 20-bed shelter for survivors and their children. It also provides targeted services for special populations, including Spanish-speakers, youth, and LGBTQ survivors of partner violence.

All services are offered in both English and Spanish.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Sakhi for South Asian Women Helpline for Gender-Based Violence
services.description:
Call (212) 868-6741, text (305) 204-1809, or email advocate@sakhi.org Monday through Friday, 10am-10pm, for assistance with gender-based violence in the South Asian diaspora.

The helpline is able to assist in English, Hindi, Urdu, and Bengali. In addition, they also have an over-the-phone interpretation service if needed for another language.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: School & Student Rights Legal Support
services.description:
If The Legal Aid Society represents you or your child in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can reach out to the attorney to be directed to help with education issues.

If you are not involved in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can ask for help with your child’s education needs by calling The Legal Aid’s Civil Access to Benefits helpline at 888-663-6880.

If your child needs representation for an upcoming Superintendent’s Suspension Hearing, please call our Suspension Hotline at 718-250-4510.

services.name: Self-Sufficiency Grants
services.description: Emergency grant funding to assist individuals and families who, because they are working and live just above the poverty level, are ineligible for most types of conventional social assistance. Grants are typically between $750 and $1250. Grants come through donors to the national non-profit charity organization Modest Needs.

services.name: Senior Planet Virtual Events
services.description: A listing of free virtual events and activities including fitness classes and discussions. For tech questions, call the Senior Planet NYC hotline at (917) 936-4410.

services.name: Services for immigration questions, or help with citizenship, green card, DACA, or TPS applications
services.description:
Fill out the form on the website to request a call back. Get help with green card renewals, citizenship, DACA, and TPS. Includes support for checking eligibility for benefits, help with forms, and guidance on required documents and process. Priority to CUNY students, but all New Yorkers are supported.

Text: 929-334-3784
Call: 646-664-9400 or 212-652-2071

services.name: Services to support older adults in Brooklyn
services.description: Call 718-596-8789 to access case management and caregiver services for older adults living in Brooklyn. Services support aging in place and can assist with meal prep, grocery shopping, housekeeping and other chores.

services.name: Shelter-Based Clinics for Homeless People
services.description: The shelter-based clinics located in Third Street, Fort Washington, New Providence, and Williams Avenue serve homeless adults from all over New York City. No one is turned away, regardless of their ability to pay. Services include primary care, diabetes testing, depression and substance abuse screening, HIV testing and viral load suppression, tobacco cessation, and detox treatments.

services.name: Silver Corps Volunteer Assignments for Older Adults
services.description:
An AmeriCorps program that provides older adults with volunteer assignments at a partner organization, training, and/or credentialing to secure employment. 

Must be at least 55 years of age, an NYC resident, currently unemployed or underemployed, and commit to volunteering 15 hours per week in a nonprofit or government agency.

Attend a virtual information session by completing the Silver Corps Interest Form linked on the website.

services.name: Sliding Scale Therapy in NY
services.description: Request sliding scale therapy through Liberation-Based Therapy. LBT provides culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and liberation-centered therapy for individuals, couples, families, and groups. Services are primarily virtual, with limited in-person availability in New York City. Sliding scale options may be available based on financial need, therapist availability, and fit. Complete the appointment request form to get connected with the intake team.

services.name: Sliding-scale Bicycles and Bike Repair in Brooklyn
services.description: If you are in need of a complete bicycle, email bikeplantnyc@gmail.com with your height, what you will use the bike for, and your phone number, and you will be added to our list. If you're in need of repair, bring your bike to the shop during our regular business hours.

services.name: Small Claims Court Action Center
services.description:
Get free help with consumer problems and complaints in small claims court, such as the purchase of defective goods, shoddy services, unreturned security deposits, property damage or falling victim to deceptive business practices. 
While the Action Centers don’t provide legal advice or courtroom representation, they can help you resolve consumer problems and boost your chances of success in the small claims courts and with collecting a judgment.

services.name: Social Service Support at Community Benefits Assistance Centers - Brownsville
services.description:
Walk-in Tuesdays: 10am-3:30pm or call the office.

Community Benefits Assistance (CBA) provides individuals and families with hands-on assistance in applying for public benefits. At our centers, we offer easy access to public services in one place, connecting people to the resources to attain higher education, jobs, and financial stability, legal counseling, help with financial planning, immigration services and referrals to other community-based organizations, as needed.

services.name: Social Services on the Upper West Side
services.description: Email socialservices@wscah.org or call 212-362-3662 ext. 126 to be connected with the Social Services department. Benefits include referrals to access shelter, substance abuse treatment, mental health services, financial counseling and tax preparation, educational programs, immigration legal assistance, and sign ups for health insurance, SNAP, SCRIE, and DRIE

services.name: Soporte y ayuda Legal para new yorkers de bajos recursos en Manhattan
services.description: Ayuda legal sin costo para Newyorkers de bajos recursos en la ciudad de New York. Ayuda legal para resolver problemas en las areas de Vivienda, juicio hipotecario, faltas civiles, discapacidad y derechos para la tercera edad; bancarrota, impuestos, consumidores, empleo, beneficios proporcionados por el govierno, immigración, y cuidado legal de menores.

services.name: Source of Income Discrimination (SOI) Mapping Tool
services.description: Explore the crowdsourced map to see how widespread discrimination based on housing vouchers is in a specific NYC neighborhood.

services.name: Substance Use and Mental Health 24-Hour Helpline
services.description: Call (800) 662-4357 (HELP) for individuals and families facing mental and/or substance use disorders. Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) runs a 24-hour mental health hotline that provides education, support, and connections to treatment. The helpline is confidential; they collect no information. In English and  Spanish. Can also text your zip code to 435748 (HELP4U) to find treatment centers in your area.

services.name: Support Groups for Gender-Expansive Children, Transgender Adolescents, Their Families & Communities
services.description: The Gender & Family Project (GFP) of the Ackerman Institute offers a variety of support groups in addition to other services. There are groups for children 5-10 years old, for gender expansive and transgender adolescents, for siblings, and for caregivers and family members. Support groups take place once per month with no obligation to attend consecutively, and they cost from $5 up on a sliding scale.

services.name: Support for Formerly Incarcerated People
services.description:
New clients call 212-691-7554 for services including intakes and enrollment, counseling, case management, access to benefits, job readiness training and employment services, education, mental health, treatment services, and food distribution.

Hours Monday-Thursday: 8 AM – 8 PM and Friday: 8 AM – 5 PM

services.name: Support for mothers impacted by the criminal legal system
services.description: Support services for mothers who have been incarcerated including food pantries, thrift shops, supportive housing, job training, educational opportunities, and programming for children and teens.

services.name: Supportive Network for Caregivers for People with Special Healthcare Needs
services.description: Call 1-800-405-8818 if you are working with a parent of a child with disabilities or special health care needs looking for information about support groups and available resources.

services.name: Supportive housing for adults, seniors, and veterans living with serious mental illness and/or substance use disorders
services.description:
Call 212-663-3000.
Supportive housing. The Bridge houses 1500+ people in the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Manhattan, and offers a range of on-site services based on client level of need, including case management, advocacy, therapeutic activities, and linkages to community-based treatment and services.

services.name: Talkin’ It Out - Phone Chat for Older Adults
services.description: Call to learn more. Older adults 60+ can "chat” confidentially by phone for free with a bilingual (Spanish/English) licensed Master’s Level Social Worker, to discuss issues and concerns outside of formal psychotherapy.

services.name: Temporary Financial Assistance for Families and Individuals
services.description: Temporary Assistance (TA) is temporary financial help for people who are unable to work, can’t find a job, or whose job does not pay enough. The two types of TA are Family Assistance and Safety Net Assistance. Apply via https://mybenefits.ny.gov or file an application at your local department of Social Services. Government ID is required. Call the OTDA Hotline for more information: 1-800-342-3009

services.name: Temporary Shelter and Help for Muslim Women and Families Facing Domestic Violence, Eviction, or Homelessness
services.description: Call the Helpline at 718-833-2425. They provide shelter, legal and immigration services, help navigating public or government assistance, managing medical needs and mental health resources, assisting in securing long-term housing, and finding employment.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Tenants’ Rights Telephone Hotline: 212-979-0611
services.description:
Call the free Tenants' Rights Telephone Hotline at 212-979-0611 to ask questions about:
Getting repairs from negligent landlords, getting adequate heat in the winter months, dealing with the threat of eviction, questions about leases and lease renewals, and legal rent increases for rent-regulated apartments.

services.name: Therapy and Advocacy for Survivors of Sexual Violence
services.description: Call 212-423-2140. Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI) works with survivors who have experienced sexual assault and intimate partner violence. Provide therapy support and advocate for the safety of clients. Located at East Harlem, the Upper East Side, and Queens.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

services.name: Trans Lifeline Hotline
services.description: Trans and questioning people can call (877) 565-8860 from 1 PM-9 PM Eastern and speak to a trans/nonbinary peer operator. Full anonymity and confidentiality, and no nonconsensual active rescue (calling 911, emergency services, or law enforcement).

services.name: Trans Needle Exchange
services.description: Trans Needle Exchange is a non-profit mail-based service providing free HRT needle supplies for trans folk who cannot access or afford their own.

services.name: Tuition free access to youth dance company (ages 7-18)
services.description: Opportunity for year-long free dance and performance training for youth ages 7-18 at Dancewave (located in Gowanus, Brooklyn). Scholarship application available on the website. Please email school@dancewave.org with questions.

services.name: VOCAL-NY Syringe Exchange
services.description: Access sterile injection equipment and other supplies for safer injection, fentanyl testing strips, and hygiene supplies. VOCAL-NY is a New York State-licensed Syringe Exchange Program (SEP). Find the Syringe Exchange Team at Douglass St between 3rd & 4th Aves in Brooklyn. May be able to deliver supplies to you through the Peer-Delivered Syringe Exchange (email paula@vocal-ny.org).

services.name: Veteran Housing and Employment Services
services.description: For housing services, reach out to the supportive services arm of the organization (631-227-0777 or ssvfintakes@sus.org). For employment, contact 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

services.name: Virtual 12-Step meetings for people who use crystal meth
services.description: A calendar of online and in-person (socially distant) meetings and social activities. Call the 24 hour helpline at 1-855-638-4373.

services.name: Virtual Recovery Meetings
services.description: An aggregated calendar of online recovery meetings. Create an account with an email address to access live virtual meetings for both support and socialization. Listed meetings include Alcoholics Anonymous, Al-Anon, Narcotics Anonymous, Overeaters Anonymous, and Coronavirus Support groups.

services.name: Volunteer Program for New Yorkers
services.description: On the website, Bright Light offers volunteering events throughout the city.

services.name: Wellness Gatherings for Undocumented People
services.description: Register for 6-week virtual Wellness Support Groups led by trained mental health providers or registered clinicians, designed to help undocumented people feel less alone and more understood.

services.name: Woodside Community Fridge
services.description: Access or drop off free food at the Woodside Community fridge at 41-26 58th St in Woodside, Queens.

services.name: Workforce Training and Supportive Housing for Homeless Men
services.description:
Call Brooklyn: 646-672-2973 | Harlem: 718-417-2538 for more information.
Ready, Willing, and Able is a 12-month residential program with paid work—complemented by holistic social services, career training, education, and sobriety support. If you’re already in the New York City shelter system and would like to join Ready, Willing & Able, talk to your case manager or parole officer about a transfer to a Doe Fund facility. The Ready, Willing & Able program is open to all men able to work and maintain sobriety, ages 18 and up.

services.name: Workshops and Programming for Youth
services.description: A calendar of workshops and programming for youth in their late teens to early 20s with the goal of improving the quality of education, health care and life-skills training for underserved adolescents and young adults.

services.name: Writing Workshops for Teens
services.description: Writing workshops for youth, with free and low-cost options for families who meet income requirements.

services.name: Youth Mentoring for Children Ages 7 to 16
services.description: Children between the ages of 7 and 16 will be matched with an adult mentor who will offer friendship, guidance, and advice. There's no cost for mentoring, but each child should be committed to this program for 8 hours per month, for a minimum of one year. Visit the website to enroll.

recTa2S4B7dP40wEc.name: 24-hour Drop-In Center offering free medical and mental health care and services to homeless LGBTQ+ youth
recTa2S4B7dP40wEc.description: Call 212.206.0574 ext. 100, or stop by the Drop-In Center at 307 West 38th Street, 3rd floor New York, NY 10018. Open for new intakes Monday-Friday from 8 AM - 8 PM and Saturday and Sunday from 10 AM - 6 PM, except closed Wed 2-4pm.

recoRoyOyXdLYJbV7.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
recoRoyOyXdLYJbV7.description: Call 988. The Lifeline provides 24/7, free and confidential support for people in distress, prevention and crisis resources for you or your loved ones, and best practices for professionals. Also available via text and online chat.

recXckAJjElkd0u9M.name: AARP Social Isolation Prevention for Adults 65 and Older
recXckAJjElkd0u9M.description: Take the AARP three-minute assessment to help you understand your risk level for social isolation and receive helpful information and local recommendations based on your results.

recVPECIhW9B9OCmk.name: Access to Health Services and Other Benefits
recVPECIhW9B9OCmk.description: Call (718) 321-7929 or email sacss@sacssny.org to get help accessing both private and public healthcare coverage, as well as help getting public benefits. This service is open to all, including South Asian and other immigrants.
recVPECIhW9B9OCmk.group_name: South Asian Council for Social Services

rec2MFiCeK8WUm4wY.name: Activities for Individuals with a Traumatic Brain Injury
rec2MFiCeK8WUm4wY.description:
Comprehensive range of interest-based activities. Participants have the opportunity to engage in social groups, art projects, community volunteering, cooking and financial literacy. Provide comprehensive psychological services that address the unique needs of each person supported. 

Apply through email form: https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recmdZOdzCYt5BfYW.name: Advocacy for Unaccompanied Immigrant Minors
recmdZOdzCYt5BfYW.description: The Young Center accepts referrals for the appointment of Child Advocates. Fill out the form linked on the website.

recv9jeeYK8KOVG7D.name: Affordable Community-Owned Internet
recv9jeeYK8KOVG7D.description: Fill in the join form to get connected to secure, affordable community-powered NYC Mesh internet

recHiDHE6ra7EnKUj.name: Affordable Housing Resources and Tenant Advocacy
recHiDHE6ra7EnKUj.description: Chhaya is a HUD-certified counseling agency providing pre-purchase and post-purchase counseling services, as well as a tenant advocacy team. Needs addressed include: First-time Homebuyer Program, Foreclosure Prevention Program, and Tenant Advocacy Program

recI03JvN7m6gBhig.name: Affordable Housing through Breaking Ground
recI03JvN7m6gBhig.description:
Offers affordable housing for low-income working professionals and the formerly homeless, some of whom live with HIV/AIDS, mental illness, or physical disabilities.

Call the Central Intake Hotline at 800-324-7055 to request an application, or fill one out online. Fill out a separate and specific application for each building to which you are applying.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

rec0h7AxrxqEk3uvl.name: Affordable locally-grown produce in Queens
rec0h7AxrxqEk3uvl.description: A Food Box Program offering weekly boxed collections of locally grown produce that can be purchased affordably. See website for information on Community Garden, Food Justice programs, and Quarterly Potlucks!

recMPxH0CkqzUgbJJ.name: AfterCare Resource Center for Long COVID
recMPxH0CkqzUgbJJ.description: The AfterCare Resource Center provides information and tools related to Long COVID, and connects New Yorkers recovering from COVID-19 or living with Long COVID to the health and social resources to support them in their recovery. Support provided regardless of one’s ability to pay or immigration status.

recuJJvye3CFJDtnA.name: Arrest and Policing - Contact a Criminal Defense Attorney
recuJJvye3CFJDtnA.description:
If you, or someone you know, has been arrested and you have questions about a pending criminal case, contact your attorney or call the Criminal Defense Office in your borough to find out how to get help.

Criminal Defense Offices:
Bronx: 718-579-3000
Brooklyn: 718-237-2000
Manhattan: 212-732-5000
Queens: 718-286-2000
Staten Island: 347-422-5333

Juvenile Trial Offices:
Bronx: 718-579-7900
Brooklyn: 718-237-3100
Manhattan: 212-312-2260
Queens: 718-298-8900
Staten Island: 347-422-5333

recZDPJIqadMCqHaT.name: Assistance Fund financial assistance for health-related expenses
recZDPJIqadMCqHaT.description: The Assistance Fund is an independent nonprofit organization that helps patients and families facing high medical out-of-pocket costs by providing financial assistance for their copayments, coinsurance, deductibles, and other health-related expenses for over 70 medical conditions (some are waitlist, some are open for application). Find eligibility and more info on the website.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recRp1SNromlOQVar.name: Assistance with Supportive Housing
recRp1SNromlOQVar.description:
Call 718-538-3344, Monday-Friday.
Housing advocacy in the areas of evictions, complaints, housing code violations, landlord/tenant and tenant/tenant mediation, and dispossession’s and foreclosures preventions. Also provide legal assistance, advocacy on behalf of the client should they be denied, rejected, and/or terminated for the following: housing application forms of HPD/NYCHA section 8, tenancy forms, NYC FEPS application, OTDA FEPS, SNAP, DRIE, LINK, SCRIE, homeowner’s loan program and rent stabilization forms.

recMf6ANOYzHZhP0Y.name: Behavioral Health Services for People Struggling with Mental Health and Substance Use
recMf6ANOYzHZhP0Y.description: Reach out via their phone or email for direction to applicable behavioral health services including care coordination, treatment, and recovery: 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

rectlhZAOFgJw1U7l.name: Benefits Access Counseling and Enrollment Assistance
rectlhZAOFgJw1U7l.description: Provides free counseling on entitlements, health insurance, financial guidance, social services, and legal services. On-site health insurance and SNAP enrollment are available. These services are open to the community for people of all ages, with or without children. Locations in Jamaica, NY and Flushing, NY.

recXyJwlLqkT0lT9y.name: Benefits Access for SNAP and WIC
recXyJwlLqkT0lT9y.description:
Call (646) 355-1475 to set up a free, confidential consultation for assistance applying for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program for Women, Infants and Children). Hunger Free NYC will go over income eligibility requirements, check to see that you qualify, and then help you gather necessary documents. They also help with the re-certification process. Service in additional languages is available:
Spanish: (347) 599-1510
Mandarin/Cantonese: (646) 935-3513 
Russian: (332) 600-5425

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recIiEOG7jd66auf2.name: Benefits Enrollment Assistance and Case Management Services in the Rockaways
recIiEOG7jd66auf2.description: Call to connect with services, including a large kosher food warehouse, Medicaid assistance, Medicare enrollment and troubleshooting, SNAP enrollment and troubleshooting, housing assistance, Holocaust survivor services, crisis intervention, support for single mother families, holiday programs and much more.
recIiEOG7jd66auf2.group_name: Jewish Community Council of the Rockaway Peninsula

recw9DPUiuzodl8uM.name: Benefits and Social Service Guidance
recw9DPUiuzodl8uM.description:
Contact customer service at 718-636-6994 or walk in to schedule an appointment at Restoration Plaza at the Financial Empowerment Center.

Restoration provides a continuum of services from case managers, licensed lawyers, financial counselors, housing ambassadors, and social workers including a free benefit screening, on-site food stamp and Medicaid enrollment, financial and legal counseling, social services referrals, and one-on-one case management.

recDkSZvXGwNIiuoV.name: Benefits assistance, senior and youth programs, and family services
recDkSZvXGwNIiuoV.description: Connect with Grand St. Settlement to access financial resources, opportunities for education, counseling, training, and support. Services include one-on-one appointments with Grand St. Settlement staff for financial and insurance support, access to job training and placement programs, and assistance in connecting with and navigating social services. They also offer early childhood and youth programs and services.

rec9E1Zg4qwdhQoLA.name: Benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and other services
rec9E1Zg4qwdhQoLA.description: Call 212-234-3481 on weekdays to make an appointment for the Resource Center, which provides benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and support services for individuals and families.

rect3LSL3d7rvnh2g.name: Black Trans Travel Fund
rect3LSL3d7rvnh2g.description: The Black Trans Travel Fund helps to cover monetary expenses for Black transgender women in New York and New Jersey states in need of money for transportation, in order for them to be able to self-determine, and have access to, their safest transportation options. There is a bi-weekly cap of 75 applicants.

reciVRTzRVg5hdi6s.name: Bronx Community Fridge and Food Hub
reciVRTzRVg5hdi6s.description:
Take food from the Friendly Fridge Bronx around the corner from the last stop on the 1 train at 242nd St, or leave fresh food to feed our neighbors and use up food unused food. Available for anyone.

Food Hub Hours: Tues, Thurs & Fri at 2 pm

rec7X67OmPCMQGBUa.name: BronxWorks Economic and Social Services and Programs
rec7X67OmPCMQGBUa.description:
BronxWorks provides a range of programs and services including help obtaining health insurance; family and adult shelter; eviction and prevention services; foster care prevention, senior homelessness prevention; chronic illness and health management such as HIV/AIDS; education and youth development; SNAP assistance; food pantry;  immigration and legal services; and workforce development. 

Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities.
TTY: 1-800-662-1220
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recK1Tv1U7Ijjuzyt.name: BronxWorks Programs for Elementary School Aged Children
recK1Tv1U7Ijjuzyt.description: Access directory of childcare resources including after-school programs, summer camps, and community-center based recreational and education activities for children 5-12 years old operated by BronxWorks.

recrEJLYqEqk5yatM.name: Brooklyn Grange CSA
recrEJLYqEqk5yatM.description:
A Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program that offers a sliding scale for locally grown vegetables. Runs for 22 weeks from late May through October.

Accepts SNAP benefits.

recoyGFH2YCTN9Ndt.name: Bushwick Free Store
recoyGFH2YCTN9Ndt.description: Tuesdays, 3-5pm at Maria Hernandez Park: Suydam St and Knickerbocker Ave. Share what you have, take what you need. Check Facebook or Instagram (@bushwickfreestore) for weekly updates and/or cancellations for weather.

recuGfNg24l9phvW2.name: CERF+ Emergency Assistance
recuGfNg24l9phvW2.description:
CERF+ offers $3,000 Emergency Relief Grants to craft artists with a public-facing practice who experienced a recent and substantially disruptive emergency or disaster. Applicants must be at least 18 years old and reside or work in the United States or U.S. territories.

To apply, visit the website and complete the online application with supporting documentation.

reczNb2edwZzPpSPq.name: Call or Chat to Get Connected with Social Services and Support in NYC
reczNb2edwZzPpSPq.description:
CUCS Benefit Centers provide individuals and families with coordinated access to resources, including income support, health insurance enrollment, legal support, and financial coaching. 

Email or call to make an in-person appointment.

recEOm6eTnOlWvxAj.name: CaringKind Helpline for Support with Dementia
recEOm6eTnOlWvxAj.description: Call (646) 744-2900, fill out an online form, or email helpline@caringkindnyc.org for resources for caregivers of those diagnosed with Alzheimer's or dementia. Social workers can meet, by appointment, in person in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and The Bronx or by phone and email.

recPprJacapUJPjto.name: Case Management Program for Older Adults in Brooklyn
recPprJacapUJPjto.description: Case management program to help adults over the age of 60 in Brooklyn stay in their homes and communities as they age. Email info@heightsandhills.org to learn more and schedule a home visit.

reckOcnFAfJ787dVo.name: Case Management Program for Older New Yorkers
reckOcnFAfJ787dVo.description: Call (718) 892-5520 to access the R.A.I.N. Case Management Program, which serves home bound seniors 60 years of age and over residing in Bronx Community Districts 7,8,11, and 12. Case Managers can assess and link seniors to a wide range of services such as transportation, housekeeping, home care, home delivered meals and assistance with entitlements and benefits.

rec09M1zDy0rNWMoL.name: Catholic Charities Help Line
rec09M1zDy0rNWMoL.description: Call 888-744-7900 8:30am-5:30pm to get connected with Catholic Charities' wide range of services for New Yorkers of all religions, including food pantries, housing resources, and services for immigrants and refugees.

recqGX5HVTyxB4JF5.name: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic
recqGX5HVTyxB4JF5.description: Provides a single, comprehensive hub for "clients" seeking treatment for their mental health and/or substance use issues. The Bridge partners with Ryan Health, a licensed health clinic, to offer behavioral and primary health care under one roof. Includes outpatient treatment and substance use treatment.

recsE5oVXPDDGBWXH.name: Child Care Vouchers for Children 6 Weeks - 13 Years Old
recsE5oVXPDDGBWXH.description: Apply for vouchers from the city to help cover the cost of child care for children 6 weeks to 13 years old at home-based and center-based providers across NYC. Most families are required to pay part of the costs based on their income and family size, but your voucher will cover all of the costs if you are: a family on cash assistance, a family experiencing homelessness, or a foster care parent. Visit the website for eligibility and application details.

recuOn5fIF7l7orBt.name: Childcare for Babies and Toddlers: EarlyLearn Program
recuOn5fIF7l7orBt.description:
EarlyLearn NYC is free or low-cost child care and education for children six weeks to four years old available for families who qualify for free or low-cost care.

Visit the link to review application process. Must provide proof of address, income, and your citizenship or immigration status.
recuOn5fIF7l7orBt.group_name: New York City Department of Education (NYCDOE)

rec9WQAgOEvPc8Lu4.name: Children Wellbeing Programs for Underserved New Yorkers
rec9WQAgOEvPc8Lu4.description: Call to connect to educational, health and wellbeing, and family support resources. Visit the website to search for specific programs by age group and neighborhood. Program areas are focused on academic and social-emotional learning, health and nutrition, and support to parents and guardians.

recHBnfN1y5Ccc8Yc.name: Circle of Care - Support for Caregivers of People with Chronic Illness or Memory Loss
recHBnfN1y5Ccc8Yc.description: If you care for someone who is frail, chronically ill or has memory loss call (866) 665-1713 or fill out an online form to get free personalized support from a Care Consultant. Services include telechat support groups, webinars, and temporary (paid) respite. All New Yorkers are eligible at all income levels.

rec64vZu52VbkiWcY.name: City Harvest Map of Food Distribution Sites
rec64vZu52VbkiWcY.description: Map of locations that are currently distributing free food throughout NYC. Location sites include soup kitchens, food pantries, City Harvest Mobile Markets, and City Harvest Community Partner Distributions.

recfpYffNkzmLvAVB.name: Citywide Doula Initiative to Find Free Doula Services
recfpYffNkzmLvAVB.description:
Find professional, no-cost doula services. Check website for contact information for specific doula services by borough. Care is provided depending on zip codes.  To enroll, you must live in one of the neighborhoods shown on the website and be income-eligible for Medicaid. 

The program prioritizes people who: live in a shelter, are in foster care, have no other labor support, are giving birth for the first time, had a previous traumatic birth experience, or have a high-risk medical condition
recfpYffNkzmLvAVB.group_name: New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

recRhIWavvuy7W0Ol.name: Clases de inglés y educación cívica
recRhIWavvuy7W0Ol.description: Un tercio de los adultos neoyorqinos—más de dos millones de personas—carecen del conocimiento del idioma inglés o un diploma de educación secundaria, pero como resultado de una falta de fondos solo el 3% de ellos pueden acceder a las clases necesarias. Make the Road New York responde a esta necesidad ofreciendo clases de inglés, computación, preparación para la ciudadanía, y cursos de Bridge to Health Careers (Puente a Carreras de Salud) a más de 1,300 adultos al año. Aliados con varias instituciones de la ciudad y el estado, luchamos para aumentar los fondos para la educación de todos los adultos en New York.
recRhIWavvuy7W0Ol.application_process:
Llame a nuestra oficina de Brooklyn al (718) 418-7690 para obtener más información sobre nuestros siguientes servicios:

- Acceso a la Universidad Dirigido por Jóvenes y Aplicaciones de Ayuda Financiera
- Servicios Integrales Para Estudiantes en Escuelas Comunitarias

reclQyIsCYog06yJ6.name: Clinical Supports, Services, & Treatment for Children and Adults
reclQyIsCYog06yJ6.description:
Provides services on a sliding scale fee basis. Services include: Psychological Assessment, Psychosocial Evaluation, Sexuality Assessment, and Additional Assessments, to assess and assist in determining needs for individuals with developmental disabilities. Additional clinical services include: Psychotherapy/Counseling, Crisis Intervention Services, Recovery Supports and Wellness Services, OT, PT, & Speech Services, Nutritional Counseling, and Family Reimbursement.

Clinical Services are available to people with developmental disabilities, ages 5 and up. Additionally, certain support services can be provided to other family members who do not themselves have a disability.

Clinics are in Manhattan (Financial District) and the Bronx (Fordham Heights) and open by appointment only; please no walk-ins.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

reckRqQBUfEOr2c4s.name: College Programs for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
reckRqQBUfEOr2c4s.description: Individuals aged 21 or older with intellectual disabilities who reside in New York City can apply for admission to the Melissa Riggio Higher Education Program at the participating CUNY campus in their borough of residence. To be eligible, applicants must qualify for services from the New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), be enrolled in the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver, and have a Care Manager from a Care Coordination Organization.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recF784FDKUsFa1k7.name: Community Cupboard in Hell's Kitchen
recF784FDKUsFa1k7.description: Free food pantry in Hell's Kitchen, open 24/7. Take what you need, leave what you can.

recN0qEIa5b0kkqC4.name: Community Dining Room for Free Meals
recN0qEIa5b0kkqC4.description:
Enjoy a healthy meal served to your table.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue
12:30 PM - 3:00 PM Monday-Saturday.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

rec0a1S5pxhKtuwFc.name: Community Economic Development Program for Community Groups and Nonprofit Legal Support
rec0a1S5pxhKtuwFc.description: Attorneys provide both short-term legal advice and ongoing representation for community groups and nonprofits, offering a full range of transactional services including corporate formation, contract drafting and negotiation, employment matters, commercial leases, regulatory issues, and real estate transactions.

rec3UxY3qFXg7aMJ2.name: Community Fridge Finder
rec3UxY3qFXg7aMJ2.description: Find community fridges containing free food near you. Go to the site and click the "Find A Fridge" button for the full map and list of fridges. Update the status of fridges in your own community.

recIrWKZyZRpu2IRI.name: Community Fridge at Hart and Myrtle
recIrWKZyZRpu2IRI.description: Community fridge in Bushwick always accepting food donations 24 hours /day. DIY don't ask just go.

recm4uPw2bJrKlrWh.name: Community Fridge in Brooklyn
recm4uPw2bJrKlrWh.description: Access the Classon Community Fridge, a refrigerator and pantry, on the street outside of Dean Crossfit that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access.

recEPA3r6bROgPIcd.name: Community Fridge in Ridgewood
recEPA3r6bROgPIcd.description: Visit the community fridge at 586 Seneca Ave in Ridgewood. There is free food distribution for those in need every Friday at 5pm.

recIk897rHj6qlFn2.name: Community Fridge in Washington Heights
recIk897rHj6qlFn2.description: Community Fridge in Washington Heights at 181st St & Fort Washington Ave. Take what you need, give what you can. Open 24/7.

recJUux0yfkDhGdti.name: Community Health Access to Addiction & Mental Healthcare Project (CHAMP)
recJUux0yfkDhGdti.description:
Call the CHAMP live-answer Helpline for free and confidential assistance accessing mental health and substance use disorder care.   Monday-Friday 9am-4pm. Supports multiple languages and all insurance types (including uninsured folks).

CHAMP assistance includes help finding a mental health or substance use disorder provider, appealing an insurer’s denial of care, and understanding your rights to mental health and substance use disorder care.

CHAMP is a partnership among specialist organizations, community based organizations, and the New York State Offices of Addiction Services and Supports (OASAS) and Mental Health.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recJUux0yfkDhGdti.group_name: New York State Office of Addiction Services and Support (OASES)

recnQDCbHlZQzZ4mc.name: Community Services for Tenants, Immigrants, Seniors, and Youth
recnQDCbHlZQzZ4mc.description: Asian Americans for Equality (AAFE) works with clients one-on-one to ensure their rights to safe and decent housing, to secure and extend appropriate government housing subsidies, to make sure they have access to social support programs, such as food stamps and Medicaid, and to provide assistance with immigration matters.  Counselors are available in storefront offices in Manhattan’s Chinatown; the Lower East Side; Flushing, Queens; and Sunset Park, Brooklyn. Contact by phone or fill out contact form on website.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recLL0WaVfJvLgr0n.name: Community and Family Services Counseling and Support
recLL0WaVfJvLgr0n.description: SCO Family of Services provides a range of community, family, and children's services in Brooklyn and Long Island including access to counseling, community centers, literacy, after school, and employment services.

recHliIfdMRVurIh0.name: Connections 2026: A Guide for Formerly Incarcerated People in NYC
recHliIfdMRVurIh0.description: A collection of resources for formally incarcerated people. The guide includes resources related to education, money, housing, mental and physical health, substance use, and more.

recwNnR0qRyDBrEkG.name: Consumer Debt, Tax & Small Business Help
recwNnR0qRyDBrEkG.description:
For help with new and existing small businesses and not-for-profit organizations or existing HDFCs contact the Community Development Project at 212-298-3340, CommunityDevProject@legal-aid.org, or reserve a spot in our virtual clinic by completing our online questionnaire.

Visit website to access forms and questionnaires.

recEV10hQpWMKruKJ.name: Cost saving programs and resources for HDFC co-op members
recEV10hQpWMKruKJ.description: Call 212 479 3337 to learn more about resources for HDFC  co-ops (Housing Development Fund Corporation co-ops), including free classes, cost savings on fuel and insurance, and more.

recrGjsNdlOppnAvK.name: Counseling, Legal, and other Resources for People Experiencing Domestic Abuse
recrGjsNdlOppnAvK.description: All free & confidential services: 24/7 domestic violence crisis hotline at (631)329-2200, individual and group counseling, legal advocacy, a residential shelter for adults and children, and violence prevention and education programs for children, teenagers and adults, taught in local schools and community-wide.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recOHPDoetQAMzYkE.name: Covenant House crisis shelter and resources for youth experiencing homelessness
recOHPDoetQAMzYkE.description: Any youth 16-21 and their minor child(ren) may go 24/7 to Covenant House NY crisis shelter at 460 West 41st near the Port Authority Bus Terminal. They have beds, clothes, food, showers, laundry, chargers, toiletries, and holistic services. No referral and no immigration status restrictions. States they are a LGBTQ safe space.

recM5JeSwhGYRuyRO.name: Criminal-Immigration Helpline
recM5JeSwhGYRuyRO.description:
Immigrants and their loved ones who are affected by the criminal system, including immigrants who have been arrested, ticketed, or convicted of a crime: call the helpline for limited immigration legal advice and information, referrals for free immigration legal services, and referrals for private immigration attorneys. 

The helpline is not live. Leave a voicemail with your name and number at any time and a staff member or volunteer will contact you .

recjReRaK9Ip1L0TU.name: Crisis Intervention Hotline for Shelter Services
recjReRaK9Ip1L0TU.description: Call the Crisis Intervention Emergency Hotline at 1-888-358-2384 with questions about accessing shelter or other services, including if you have been denied access to shelter. Leave a detailed message, including your phone number. The Intervention Program is based in NYC and only able to respond to questions regarding NYC services.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recpv6SHVMm1Vo0fR.name: Crisis Shelter for Women Survivors of Domestic Violence with Disabilities
recpv6SHVMm1Vo0fR.description: Freedom House is a safe, confidential and fully accessible shelter that offers private living spaces of various sizes to accommodate both singles and larger families. They are also equipped to serve all survivors and their children with disabilities including (but not limited to) wheelchair users, people who are D/deaf or hard of hearing and blind or visually impaired. Call (212) 400-6470 for more information and availability or email info@bflnyc.org.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recitUIHoF1jCYFSR.name: Crisis Text line: Free text-based crisis counseling
recitUIHoF1jCYFSR.description: In the United States, text HOME to 741741 at anytime 24/7 to reach a volunteer crisis counselor.

recIJ0AJQbCKfNOuM.name: Crisis Toolkit
recIJ0AJQbCKfNOuM.description: An assortment of resources that may provide perspective, comfort, and/or tools that could be of assistance to people experiencing various sorts of tough times. Includes links to informational guides, online peer support, and more.

recXbB4EfW5YWRaaB.name: Day Habilitation Program for People with Developmental Disabilities
recXbB4EfW5YWRaaB.description:
NYC’s Day Habilitation programs are tailored to adults 18 and over. Programs provide diverse services that cater to people’s individual preferences.​

Day Habilitation is available to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are over the age of 18, in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx. 

To enroll the participant must have Medicaid, Care manager enrolled in CCO (Care Coordination Organization).
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recpJNeaY4FDQA1LQ.name: Developmental Disabilities Services
recpJNeaY4FDQA1LQ.description: Offers housing, employment, and other support for both children and adults. See each type of support for the best person to contact.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recJ2tXlhumpwcWEn.name: Dial-A-Teacher Homework Help
recJ2tXlhumpwcWEn.description:
What: Homework help line for students and their parents, run by classroom teachers
Where: Call (212) 777-3380
Who: Students in K-12
Hours: Monday through Thursday, 4 to 7 p.m. when school is in session.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recnPqp3VWYNxtuLX.name: Diaper Assistance Program
recnPqp3VWYNxtuLX.description:
Call 718-402-1212 Mondays between 9:30am-5pm to schedule an appointment for free diapers (walk-ins cannot be accepted at this time). Distribution is in the Bronx. 

To qualify, you must reside with a child 2 years or younger or be expecting (proof of sonogram or official doctors note required), live in the New York City area, and receive WIC and/or SNAP (food stamps). 

Required documents include:
- Photo ID
- Proof of address (no more than 90 days old-electricity bill/light bill/doctors letter/note with client’s name and address)
- Birth certificate(s) for baby or hospital discharge papers for newborn
- WIC proof (WIC app on cellphone or WIC card with a letter/note from WIC office) or Food Stamps/SNAP proof (recent budget letter)

recH7dENUNGhhE5X9.name: Digital Resource Map by and for Transgender, Non-binary and/or Intersex People
recH7dENUNGhhE5X9.description:
TransAtlas is a map-based guide to community organizations, agencies and spaces across the 5 boroughs of New York City, made by and for people of transgender, non-binary and/or intersex experience. 

Drawn from Callen-Lorde’s Transgender Resource guide and Surgeon guide, and made by a team of transgender folks, TransAtlas maps hundreds of services and organizations across the 5 boroughs where TGNB folks can find trans-competent and friendly resources to help with anything from primary care to hair removal, addiction support, and religious institutions. You can search through dozens of surgeons, therapists, dentists, lawyers, barbers, case managers and more.

recDOdMuAw8IEUIz0.name: Directory to find access, information, and funding to people seeking an abortion
recDOdMuAw8IEUIz0.description: A national searchable directory to find abortion care providers, funding, and support. Does not provide direct referrals or actual procedures, but instead connects you to information about places that do.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recSBeGs56x9e7Ew5.name: Domestic Violence Help
recSBeGs56x9e7Ew5.description: Call 212-568-6616 9am-5pm to access individual counseling, shelter services or help obtaining an order of protection.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recjs89JVLJxeIptS.name: Domestic Violence Hotline
recjs89JVLJxeIptS.description: Call 1-800-621-HOPE (4673) for assistance in domestic violence situations, including crisis counseling, safety planning, assistance with finding domestic violence shelters, and information about resources.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recAuOGip2OhuM4aL.name: Doula Access and Care for Black and Low Income Patients
recAuOGip2OhuM4aL.description: A reimbursement service that covers doula care under Medicaid. For New Yorkers who seek support through pregnancy and post partum.

recK7KKeRivElf37Z.name: Drive Change
recK7KKeRivElf37Z.description:
Drive Change runs an 3-month paid fellowship for formerly incarcerated youth ages 18-25 that focuses on hospitality/restaurant industry training and professional development. Apply online.

To apply, you must be between 18-25, and prove you have 8th grade or higher math and reading level (TABE, GED/TASC or HS DIPLOMA preferred but not necessary).

recGn3Qxixq1EzF19.name: Education for families of people with developmental disabilities to obtain services
recGn3Qxixq1EzF19.description:
AHRC's Family Educational Series includes workshops and informational sessions for families in obtaining services for their family member with a developmental disability and help families to come with challenges that may arise as they care for their loved one. 

Join AHRC's mailing list to receive invitation to their education workshops via email.

recvVbNbO8EGMYgnX.name: Emergency Financial Aid for Professional Visual Artists
recvVbNbO8EGMYgnX.description:
The Artists’ Fellowship provides one-time emergency aid to professional visual fine artists and their families in times of sickness, natural disaster, bereavement or unexpected extreme hardship that can be documented through paid or unpaid invoices, bills, or contracts.

Eligibility: please note that “Professional” is defined as those visual artists who make their livelihood through sales as reported on a Schedule C with a U.S. Federal tax return. An active exhibition history is also an important part of documenting “professional.”

recfdXk3XEKypO3q4.name: Emergency Grant for Burials
recfdXk3XEKypO3q4.description: Apply online or call 718-557-1399 for funds to meet funeral expenses for a deceased low-income New York City resident.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recgekeuBrsZ9PyQd.name: Emergency Meal Delivery for Homebound Elderly New Yorkers
recgekeuBrsZ9PyQd.description:
This resource is only accessible through a case management agency. If eligible, enter address to get the phone number for the Case Management Agency of your district. The Case Management Agency will guide you through the process of getting meals. 

To qualify, you:
-Must be 60 years of age or older
-Must be physically or mentally incapacitated and in need of some assistance
-Must be unable to prepare nutritious meals or have no one to do so for you
-Must be able to live safely at home if services are provided for you
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recqRqCFnm30dnZuP.name: Emergency Rental Assistance Program
recqRqCFnm30dnZuP.description: New York State Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) will provide economic relief to help low and moderate-income households at risk of experiencing homelessness or housing instability by providing rental arrears, temporary rental assistance and utility arrears assistance. No immigration status requirements to apply. See website for eligibility and application requirements. Funds are not always available, so check website to see if applications are currently being accepted.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recqRqCFnm30dnZuP.group_name: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance

recX4NHtoMh7hvA4q.name: Emotional Support and Crisis Response Hotline
recX4NHtoMh7hvA4q.description: Call 212-673-3000 to reach The Samaritans of New York completely confidential 24-hour emotional support and crisis response hotline. It's available on an immediate and ongoing basis for individuals who are dealing with every kind of problem, situation, illness, trauma or loss and need someone to talk to who will listen and take you seriously.

rec2sbQBEsUUosNUk.name: Employment Opportunities for the Long-Term Unemployed
rec2sbQBEsUUosNUk.description:
The Doe Fund offers employment opportunities for people who have experienced long-term unemployment but who are not homeless. To learn more, call one of the facilities or email info@doe.org: 
Brooklyn: 646-672-2973
Harlem: 718-417-2538

recNqFPndhQ5IWhfv.name: Employment Services: Job Readiness, Training, and Counseling
recNqFPndhQ5IWhfv.description: Urban Upbound’s Employment Services team provides job readiness training and one-on-one counseling to help community members gain and retain meaningful employment. Includes job readiness assistance, 1:1 counseling, job training, and computer labs.

reciC0rYvfbuZ1JFr.name: Empowered NYC: Financial Counseling and Coaching
reciC0rYvfbuZ1JFr.description: Fill out the online form to schedule free one-on-one financial counseling. Help with debt reduction, credit scores, savings, budgeting, opening a bank account, and preparing income information for housing applications. Appointment options may be in-person or by phone.
reciC0rYvfbuZ1JFr.group_name: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection

recc2ABaPIdH97pVE.name: English, Citizenship Prep, and Community Health Worker Training Classes
recc2ABaPIdH97pVE.description:
Complete the online form to apply to Make the Road adult education programs, including: 
- English classes for speakers of other languages 
- Citizenship preparation
- Community health worker training program (Brooklyn only)

For more information, call your preferred location in Bushwick, Jackson Heights, Port Richmond, Brentwood, or White Plains.

recjRtUfRnSPD1ecI.name: Entertainment Community Fund Emergency Financial Assistance & List of Additional Funds
recjRtUfRnSPD1ecI.description: Emergency Financial Assistance is available to eligible performing arts and entertainment professionals in times of unexpected critical need and to assist towards basic living expenses such as health care, housing and utilities to prevent eviction or shut-offs. Multiple funds in the entertainment industries are available to apply to, covering a variety of eligibility restrictions.

recvs2Ss9ikmPHel6.name: Episcopal Actors Guild Fund for Performers in Financial Crisis
recvs2Ss9ikmPHel6.description: You must live in one of the five NYC boroughs and have an established career working as a performer for at least five consecutive years. Call (212)-685-2927 if you think you may be eligible for the program. EAG's programs and services focus primarily on sustaining and supporting the careers of working performers. At the heart of EAG's charitable outreach is the EARP. Through this program, we give grants to qualified performers in financial crisis regardless of religion, race, national origin or ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental ability, political ideology/affiliations, or language. Through EARP we address critical issues like eviction, housing court stipulations, utility shutoffs, emergency medical and dental costs, and sustenance needs like food and transportation.

recYh4epv2mW8V6PA.name: Eviction Prevention Program
recYh4epv2mW8V6PA.description: People in danger of being evicted can call the Eviction Prevention Hotline at 888-850-2712 on Wednesday mornings beginning at 9:30 am. Appointments are limited and first-come, first-serve. To qualify for a one-time payment of $1000 (on average), you must be in court, have a signed court stipulation, and have future ability to pay your ongoing rent.

recTWI22ndpP0KhKJ.name: Exchange childcare with people you trust
recTWI22ndpP0KhKJ.description: Carefully is a free playdate and childcare exchange platform to build a network of parents you know and trust to share care, redefining the traditional 'care circle' model for the digital age (available for iOS and Android).

rec87GdB8CxD3Hekt.name: Family Support Program and Benefits Counseling in the Bronx
rec87GdB8CxD3Hekt.description: Call 718-839-1100 to learn more about WHEDco's Family Support Services or to ask for an appointment. Family support services include public benefits counseling for benefits such as: SNAP, WIC referrals, cash assistance (PA, TANF, SafetyNet), Safelink and Assurance cell phones, social security, health insurance, citizenship and green card applications and renewals (plus fee waiver assistance), housing applications, Senior Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE), and childcare.
rec87GdB8CxD3Hekt.group_name: Women’s Housing and Economic Development Corporation (WHEDco)

recJrO7I220nCe0jf.name: Financial Counseling and Workshops for South Asian Small Businesses
recJrO7I220nCe0jf.description:
To apply for services, fill out survey on the website. 

Chhaya is a community development corporation with the mission to build the power, housing stability, and economic well-being of South Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities. Chhaya executes this work by providing free direct services in the areas of housing counseling and homeownership, asset building and financial empowerment, policy and advocacy, and community organizing.

recB7en0awPaDToR3.name: Financial Support for Black Transgender People
recB7en0awPaDToR3.description:
A Black, trans-led collective that curates parties to fundraise money to help Black transgender people pay for their rent, gender-affirming surgeries, smaller co-pays for medicines/doctor’s visits, and travel assistance. Visit website to view currently available applications and to apply for assistance programs. 

Only open to Black transgender people. Application through website. Depending on services, social media access might be necessary.

recoJKhacXQ4eEfJe.name: Financial guidance, marketing, and planning support for small businesses
recoJKhacXQ4eEfJe.description: Small Business Support Specialists offer businesses that are opening or reopening support with applying for grants and loans, digital marketing, getting online, lease negotiations, and business planning.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

rec7lljBwAYZr92m4.name: Find Food Assistance By Address
rec7lljBwAYZr92m4.description: Enter an address to find a directory of nearby food assistance resources, including pantries and meal programs.

recsPpnzM9GOf2kEK.name: Find a Food Pantry Map
recsPpnzM9GOf2kEK.description:
Visit the link to view a map of food banks operating in New York City. 

NOTE: Hours vary - call ahead to confirm when a food bank will be open.

recSXx0FNQ9PoEjS3.description: Find a Health Center the receives government Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) funding by location. Primary care health services should be available at a reduced cost or free of charge depending on your economic status.

reci98WLhv53yGm8t.name: Fiscal Hosting for Mutual Aid Groups in New York City
reci98WLhv53yGm8t.description: NYC Mutual Aid Groups looking for a fiscal sponsor can get in touch at pactbk@gmail.com. A fiscal sponsor is an entity that holds money on behalf of a collective, and takes care of accounting, taxes, and invoices.

recQiDBEzVoRFpDOU.name: Food Career Training Program
recQiDBEzVoRFpDOU.description: Apply for this free program on the "career programs" page. This resource is available for women and nonbinary people over 18 who are looking to find a job in food and restaurant services. Must be able to actively take courses for 5 weeks.

recSNJC4fwSDlE925.name: Food Distribution Tuesdays in Washington Square Park
recSNJC4fwSDlE925.description: Weekly distro of food, hot coffee, and more on Tuesdays 12:30pm-2:30pm in Washington Square Park across from Holley Statue. Take what you want, leave what you can.

rec7f7wKZ3OSVbjAA.name: Free & Confidential Mental Health Support via Call Or Text
rec7f7wKZ3OSVbjAA.description:
Text or call 988 for Free & Confidential Mental Health + Substance Use Support open 24/7. A chat service is also available on the website.

Interpreters are available for 200+ languages. Stay on the line, and you will be connected with a counselor who can connect you to translator services.

recnTHOzJAPmlLHLC.name: Free & Low-Cost Primary Care, Behavioral Health Services, Dental and Podiatry for the Homeless
recnTHOzJAPmlLHLC.description: Call (833) 423-4273 24/7 for information or a same-day appointment. Find walk-in locations on the website. You will be treated regardless of your ability to pay.

recCgg4LnKlmYmXdk.name: Free Abortion Clinic and Pill Directory
recCgg4LnKlmYmXdk.description: Search the database to find verified abortion clinics near you that keeps your information private.

rec74MrdsXkXXqhOS.name: Free Adult English Classes
rec74MrdsXkXXqhOS.description:
A 10-month program to help improve  listening, reading, speaking and writing skills. Textbooks are provided. We offer English for Speakers of Other Language (ESOL) classes at a variety of levels to adult immigrant students during the daytime, evenings, and weekends, free of charge.

Requirements: 
- Must be at least 18 years old
- Must be a NYC resident and provide proof of address
- Must be able to attend 10 months of in-person classes

recR1v0emdqPNweBa.name: Free Assistance with Health Insurance, Healthcare, Medicaid
recR1v0emdqPNweBa.description: Call (888) 614-5400 or email cha@cssny.org for assistance with understanding how to use your health insurance, resolving medical billing and debt issues, disputing coverage denials and eligibility determinations, getting the most from your coverage (get prior authorizations, access specialists, and out-of-network services when needed), accessing affordable health care services, and hospital and prescription financial assistance program.

rec7qZIGyTKZ1QGS5.name: Free Baby Formula Exchange
rec7qZIGyTKZ1QGS5.description: Submit an online form to offer or request baby formula on this nationwide platform. You can also search for available formula by location and contact donors directly.

recJsZWPayBtRp0Le.description:
Call 1-844-862-7930 to reach counselors available 9 am until 5 pm, Monday through Friday. You can also request to be contacted by a counselor by filling out the form at https://www.cidny.org/getnyconnects
Support includes SNAP, Unemployment Insurance, Social Security, Medicaid, etc. for people with disabilities and older adults; help getting connected with various resources including food, toiletries, mental health, etc.
recJsZWPayBtRp0Le.group_name: Center for Independence of the Disabled
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recUb1ToyewpVmMle.name: Free Bikes for Fellow New Yorkers
recUb1ToyewpVmMle.description: Donate a spare bike or apply for a free one at bikematch.nyc. Fill out a form, get paired with a neighbor of about the same height, and arrange a time to meet up and exchange the bike.

recge9MwZoAmlDRHM.name: Free Clinic Directory
recge9MwZoAmlDRHM.description: Free Clinic Directory is a directory of medical and dental clinics and community health centers that can help low-income and uninsured people by offering free and discounted rates for medical and/or dental care. Search by location, name, or phone number.

recZxjSFYN1wSS2jo.name: Free Counseling and Assistance with Medicare
recZxjSFYN1wSS2jo.description: Call 1-800-333-4114 to get assistance with understanding Medicare benefits, making enrollment decisions, coordinating Medicare with other insurance, appealing denials of care, determining eligibility for Medicare cost-saving programs, or another topic.

rec2r11RD9g5g4lIm.name: Free Daily Showers
rec2r11RD9g5g4lIm.description:
Hot showers, fresh towels and toiletries are available.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Ave
8:30-11:30 a.m. / 12:30-2:20 p.m.
Monday-Friday

recY540c4z4cnl6Eu.name: Free Dating Abuse and Domestic Violence Services and Resources for Youth Under 24 Years Old
recY540c4z4cnl6Eu.description: For youth experiencing dating abuse and domestic violence, access the helpline by calling 800-214-4150 or texting 646-535-DAY1 (3291). Access prevention and know-your-rights resources on the website.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

rec3JlBzEIHVE1ICu.name: Free Diapers and Wipes for Brooklyn Families
rec3JlBzEIHVE1ICu.description: ​Visit Rain or Shine Diaper Fund every Monday at The Living Gallery in Brooklyn, NY, to receive free diapers and wipes. Get a number at 8am, and distribution is at 1pm. No ID or sign-up required.

rec24ElrgQjZm0LXO.name: Free Digital Mental Health Resources
rec24ElrgQjZm0LXO.description: Library of apps and online services offering mental health support, including for depression, anxiety, and addiction.

recmuaS4sX5Knpcdr.name: Free Downloadable Deportation Defense Manual
recmuaS4sX5Knpcdr.description: Read this to familiarize yourself with how to respond to ICE.  Broken into three sections: Know Your Rights, Rapid Response to Raids, and Deportation Defense.

recsp1RGxQ38RygZi.name: Free Educational Courses, SAT and AP Prep
recsp1RGxQ38RygZi.description: Access Khan Academy’s library of practice and lessons covering math K-12 through early college, grammar, science, history, AP®, SAT®, and more. Free for learners and teachers.

recN3m8TLbk3aYIaD.name: Free Food Delivery for East Asian Elders throughout NYC
recN3m8TLbk3aYIaD.description:
Deliver weekly hot lunches, fresh produce, and bulk ingredients to East Asian elders while supporting local small businesses.

Fill out the form to join the waitlist. During the next onboarding cycle, they will review your eligibility for receiving Heart of Dinner care packages for free. The criteria:

1. Be a local NYC Asian American person aged 60 or above.
2. Have a gross monthly income as a single elderly at or below $1,869; or have a gross monthly income as an elderly couple at or below $2,518.
3. Unable to prepare meals because of the lack of money to purchase food, inability to shop or cook, or lack of facilities.
4. Isolated due to lack of family, friend or neighbor support.

recO4Af4mthwMPJGI.name: Free Food Distribution Mondays and Saturdays in Astoria
recO4Af4mthwMPJGI.description: Pick up a pre-packaged bag of groceries Mondays 8am-10:30am and Saturdays 1-1:30pm. No sign-up, id, or name required. 25-82 Steinway St in Queens.

recSBZZJApQrik213.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays at Woodside Houses
recSBZZJApQrik213.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays 1:30pm at the Woodside Houses at 49th St & Broadway

recETCDMo12NfQksC.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Tompkins Square Park
recETCDMo12NfQksC.description: Free food distribution Saturdays, 11am at Tompkins Square Park at the corner of East 7th Street & Avenue B. Dropoff donations of food and goods can be received at the distro 10:45-noon.

recQcF8SGZr11bp9w.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Woodside at the 61st St-Woodside Station
recQcF8SGZr11bp9w.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays at 1:30pm at the 61st St-Woodside MTA Station in Queens.

recLfjponzuxvrQuO.name: Free Food Distribution Second Saturdays in Jamaica
recLfjponzuxvrQuO.description: Free food and produce distribution at 12pm every 2nd Saturday of the month at the corner of Jamaica Ave and Parsons Blvd, outside of the old Jamaica Multiplex.

recvBlHWA02Tmbcpg.name: Free Food Distribution Sundays in Lower Manhattan
recvBlHWA02Tmbcpg.description: Free food distribution Sundays, 12-2pm at the NE corner of Houston and LaGuardia Place.
