recP1caKMmWlmdekF.name: Free Food Distribution Sundays in Tompkins Square Park
recP1caKMmWlmdekF.description: Free food distribution Sundays, 12-2pm in the SW corner of Tompkins Square park at Ave A and East 7th St.

recJVj10RMUeBT1JV.name: Free Food Distribution Thursdays in Sunnyside
recJVj10RMUeBT1JV.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Sunnyside on Thursdays at 1:15pm at Bliss Plaza on Queens Blvd & 46th St.

recvVd1ShCk7eR2wo.name: Free Food Distribution, Clothing, & Community Care on Saturdays in the Bronx
recvVd1ShCk7eR2wo.description: Pick up free produce, hot food, clothing, books, and toiletries every Saturday from 1 - 2pm @ St. Mary's Park 601 E. 149th St, Bronx, NY.

rec1fRbfE2gWjp9GC.name: Free Food and Clothing Distribution in Brooklyn
rec1fRbfE2gWjp9GC.description: Tuesdays, 12-2pm at 1046 Broadway in Brooklyn. Free food distribution available to anyone.

rece38Cknmkk4gi9t.name: Free Gender-Affirming Clothes and Resources - Marsha's Closet
rece38Cknmkk4gi9t.description: Give what you can, take what you need! Pull up every 3rd Monday of the month on 135th and St Nick to drop off/pick up Clothing Donations for our queer and unhoused community in Harlem & beyond.

recbxxxclArEf6RTj.name: Free Grocery and Supply Delivery
recbxxxclArEf6RTj.description: Free grocery and supply delivery to elderly, disabled, and/or immunocompromised New Yorkers. Call (732) 639-1579 (open seven days a week) or fill out the form on the website to request a delivery.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recaCDVOHWvfZ3TkH.name: Free Haircuts
recaCDVOHWvfZ3TkH.description:
Free haircuts for the first 30 clients (with ticket - given at POTS) of all ages.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue. Starts at 8:30 am – First 30 Clients Tuesday and Thursday.

recq0ZO3PqOF3eC7m.name: Free Health Clinic for Sex Workers
recq0ZO3PqOF3eC7m.description: Sex workers can call 212-271-8134 to schedule an appointment with COIN, a free healthcare program through Callen-Lorde for sex workers in an affirming, supportive environment. The clinic offers primary medical care, sexual health, HIV treatment & prevention, transgender health, GYN care, and more.

recrGbUc9vZpixVjv.name: Free Healthcare for Ages 10-26, Including Primary Care
recrGbUc9vZpixVjv.description: Call (212) 423-3000 for free and confidential care for young people ages 10-26. Fundamental care for all patients includes primary care, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, social services, optical, health education and prescriptions, plus specialized services for LGBTQ young people, teen parents, young people living with HIV, and young people dealing with trauma.

recnDnEiWVuLrNHv8.name: Free Housing Legal Services & Eviction Prevention Program
recnDnEiWVuLrNHv8.description:
Call 718-538-3344 Ext. 100 or 117, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm.
NAICA's primary focus is geared towards providing legal eviction prevention services to families and individuals who are working, receiving public assistance, or that meet the low-income eligibility and are at risk of losing their homes.

recmh44TTQJopglhF.name: Free Legal Hotline for People with Limited Income
recmh44TTQJopglhF.description:
Call the Legal Hotline or fill out an online application to connect with staff attorneys who assist callers of limited income on a range of civil legal issues, including matrimonial and family law, housing law, domestic violence, bankruptcy, and debt collection and benefits. Our staff includes bilingual attorneys who speak English and Spanish, and we can accept calls in any language through interpreting services.

The Hotline is open Monday through Thursday from 10am-12pm and 2pm-4pm, and Friday from 9am-12pm.

recwj2qK9NK3JIIIR.name: Free Legal Support for New Yorkers
recwj2qK9NK3JIIIR.description:
Call 917-661-4500 for the Access Line to speak to an intake specialist in any language.

The website also includes FAQs for common legal questions including topics related to immigration and asylum, LGBTQ+ rights, health and disability rights, housing and foreclosure, and more.

recRX8zh2mmrZcB9D.name: Free Legal Support for People Experiencing Poverty or In Crisis
recRX8zh2mmrZcB9D.description: For legal assistance or financial counseling, contact the office by either filling out the online intake form or calling and leaving a message with full name, contact info, and description of legal or financial counseling needs. Legal support focuses on helping immigrants, survivors of violence and discrimination, and people who need support securing access to health care and essential benefits, demanding safe and affordable housing , and protecting their economic rights.
recRX8zh2mmrZcB9D.group_name: New York Legal Assistance Group - NYLAG

recuVxxjY3Y1AHkZK.name: Free Legal and Social Services Support for Low Income People in the Bronx
recuVxxjY3Y1AHkZK.description:
Call 718-838-7878 (Mon-Fri 9am-4pm) for free legal and social services for immigration, housing, criminal, and family defense, as well as social work support and advocacy. Legal Emergency Hotline: 347-778-1266 (Available 24/7)
Housing Hotline: 347-842-1122 (Available two Mondays* every month, from 9:00AM to 5:00PM)

recpjWN4CoYn0arvp.name: Free Meal Distribution Saturdays in Greenpoint
recpjWN4CoYn0arvp.description: Visit Greenpoint Community Kitchen at 155 Milton Street every Saturday from 11 am to 1 pm to receive hot meals and coffee. Meals can be enjoyed on-site or taken to go. Bread is packaged and available to take home as well.

recwxvYTavY8gxdmz.name: Free Meals in Park Slope
recwxvYTavY8gxdmz.description: CHiPS serves breakfast (9-10:30am) and lunch (11:30am-1pm) Monday-Saturday at 200 4th Avenue in Park Slope Brooklyn. Meals are available to anyone who is in need.

recGR8pfTIt8zVI0Z.name: Free Mediation Services for Brooklyn and Manhattan
recGR8pfTIt8zVI0Z.description: New York Peace Institute offers free in-person mediation for Brooklyn and Manhattan residents. Also offers conflict coaching and restorative processes to help you resolve your conflict.

recqP5HnH2TKIO5AR.name: Free Medical and Dental Clinic
recqP5HnH2TKIO5AR.description: Free Clinic operated by Care for the Homeless at our POTS 2759 Webster Avenue location.

recz60v2tnc15tSfA.name: Free Mental Health Crisis Intervention for LGBTQ Youth via Phone Hotline, Text, or Chat
recz60v2tnc15tSfA.description: Call 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678-678 if you are thinking about harming yourself. Get immediate crisis support, connect to a crisis counselor 24/7, 365 days a year, from anywhere in the U.S via text, chat, or phone. Confidential and free.

recyLTDNpfig9PqKa.name: Free Mental Health Support for Parents
recyLTDNpfig9PqKa.description: State-wide help line to support parents before and after having a baby. Call 7 days a week, 9am-5pm to access non-judgmental and confidential emotional support, educational information, healthcare and support group resources, and to connect to parental mental health peer support groups.
recyLTDNpfig9PqKa.group_name: Postpartum Resource Center of New York

recmqpSH032fC7QBq.name: Free Monthly Grocery Distribution in Brooklyn
recmqpSH032fC7QBq.description: Grocery distributions at 641 Classon Avenue on the second Monday of each month.

recwYkan3nvMaZFqp.name: Free National Mental Health HelpLine
recwYkan3nvMaZFqp.description: Call 1-800-950-6264 (NAMI) or email info@nami.org, Monday-Friday, 10am to 10pm. Operators can provide information about mental illness and refer callers to treatment, support groups, family support, and legal support, if needed.

rec8VmbXZCDr7xFNa.name: Free Phone Caption Service
rec8VmbXZCDr7xFNa.description: Caption service for phone calls. Can be used on internet phones, landlines, and mobile phones. You must be a U.S. resident and certify that your hearing loss inhibits your ability to use the phone.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

reci5URT2omE4o5ez.name: Free Programs and Services for Young People Ages 12 to 24
reci5URT2omE4o5ez.description: The Door offers a variety of services in health, mental health, legal, education, arts, housing, and more for youth and young people ages 12 through 24.

rec1WiHloM8QwSq3D.name: Free Rapid PCR Testing in Brooklyn
rec1WiHloM8QwSq3D.description:
Periodic free Rapid PCR tests for COVID, Flu A + B, and RSV. If you are positive for any of them, G-REBELS will provide you with a care kit and discuss support services so you can focus on rest and recovery. 

Tests, kits, and support services are completely free of charge to community members, but are limited to the uninsured to prioritize those who need it most. 

Find upcoming appointment times and locations on Instagram or the sign-up form.

rec39cIDRQMYgXz5q.name: Free Resources - Children's Mental Health and Learning Challenges
rec39cIDRQMYgXz5q.description: Visit the Family Resource Center to find information to help support children who are struggling with mental health, behavior or learning challenges. Resources available in English and Spanish.

rec5fz6J28wPgoBUM.name: Free Services for Residents of Upper Manhattan and the Bronx
rec5fz6J28wPgoBUM.description: Call the hotline at 929-415-8970 to get assistance in a number of areas including a food pantry, tax preparation, unemployment insurance, benefits, housing, or immigration needs.

rec6gNfCpTF1VPGmy.name: Free Showers and Personal Hygiene
rec6gNfCpTF1VPGmy.description: Get free showers, toiletries, clean clothes, snacks, and water with Shower Power NYC’s Fresh City program in Harlem (Mon/Fri at Harlem United) and Ridgewood (Tues at Ridgewood Presbyterian Church), 10am–2pm. No ID or appointment needed.

rec0a8CGFDGWijFVN.name: Free Store in Greenpoint
rec0a8CGFDGWijFVN.description: Free store open 24/7 at the corner of Adelphi St and Greene Ave in Greenpoint. Anyone can come anytime to donate or take items from the store’s shelves, from clothing and linens to toys and home decor. Please no large items, make sure things are suitable for redistribution, and help keep things tidy.

recWLYx4feoU7GJ73.name: Free Vegan Meal Distribution Sundays in the Lower East Side
recWLYx4feoU7GJ73.description: Free vegan meals served every Sunday at 4:30pm inside the SW corner of Tompkins Square Park (E 7th st & Ave A).
recWLYx4feoU7GJ73.group_name: Lower East Side Food Not Bombs

recnElyfdsVGeTdRa.name: Free Vegetable Distribution Sundays in Queens
recnElyfdsVGeTdRa.description: Free veggie distro every Sunday, ~2:30pm at Roosevelt Ave & 58th St in Woodside, Queens until November 2026.

recx9HrD7EFlDPzCq.name: Free Virtual Support Groups for Eating Disorders
recx9HrD7EFlDPzCq.description:
Communities of Healing virtual support groups are free and open to anyone with an eating disorder. Each group is facilitated by someone who has personally experienced and recovered from an eating disorder. Groups meet weekly to share with and learn from other people who understand what it means to fight for recovery.

To join, fill out the information request form, and ANAD will contact you with more information and joining info.

rec1jR53kqRtNehPe.name: Free Virtual Tutoring for NYC Public School Students
rec1jR53kqRtNehPe.description: EduMate NYC provides free virtual tutoring from volunteer college students for K-12 students enrolled in the NYC public school system. Priority will be given to students who are on free and reduced-price meal programs. Our tutoring covers all traditional school subjects, standardized test prep, and the college application process!

recwTiPZOFvDSE4Jy.name: Free Water Testing Kits for Lead
recwTiPZOFvDSE4Jy.description: Fill out the request form to receive a free kit to test your drinking water for lead. The kit comes with a pre-paid label to send it to a laboratory for lead analysis, and the results will be mailed to you within 30 days of the sample being tested. Limited to one per household at a time.
recwTiPZOFvDSE4Jy.group_name: New York City Department of Environmental Protection

rec2qB8xxoNqWotUR.name: Free confidential anti-violence chat & hotline in multiple languages
rec2qB8xxoNqWotUR.description:
Highly trained helpline advocates can answer general questions about domestic violence, human trafficking, and sexual violence across the lifespan, provide crisis counseling and help develop safety plans, and/or make referrals for ongoing support. Womankind also provides emergency safety shelter.

Online chat & text available Mon-Fri 10am-6pm (English, Chinese)
Text Womankind for help in: English 1.929.207.5907, Chinese 1.929.207.5901
24-Hour Multilingual Helpline: 1.888.888.7702 (English, Spanish and 18+ Asian languages and dialects, including Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Tagalog, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, and Vietnamese)

recz3bKwZ0nb1Jf2e.name: Free dancing lessons, group exercise, and interactive activities
recz3bKwZ0nb1Jf2e.description: The Y @ Home includes free programs for all ages and populations open to the wider community, including exercise activities, congregate lunches, dance classes, and more.
recz3bKwZ0nb1Jf2e.group_name: YM & YWHA of Inwood and Washington Heights

recv2Po1V5pmDTzq1.name: Free diabetes supplies/medication, insurance/PAP help
recv2Po1V5pmDTzq1.description:
Mutual Aid Diabetes (MAD) is available to help anyone with any type of diabetes to access free or low cost supplies and medication as well as assist with insurance coverage and patient assistance programs. To request aid, please fill out our intake form here: https://airtable.com/shrr0XQLbZXNn1oGv.

Aid hotline (text or call): 646-780-9571
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recI4XW5qdXAxVCKA.name: Free food, clothes and supplies in Washington Square Park
recI4XW5qdXAxVCKA.description: WSP Mutual Aid collects and distributes free food, clothes, and supplies in Washington Square Park every Friday starting at 5pm.

rec9JPwfSlALIdnQV.name: Free healthcare access application for people with HIV/AIDS
rec9JPwfSlALIdnQV.description: The Uninsured Care Programs provide access to free health care (Drugs, Outpatient Primary Care, Home Care, Insurance Premium Payments, and Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to prevent HIV infection) for New York State residents who are uninsured or underinsured. The Uninsured Care Programs are committed to working closely with providers and individuals to support access to the wide range of options for payment for health care services and medications for persons living with or at risk of acquiring HIV/AIDS.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recFcslKR72fRPAll.name: Free job training and placements
recFcslKR72fRPAll.description: The HOPE Program is a non-profit organization that offers 5 different job training programs: job readiness training, construction training, industry certifications such as OSHA-30 internships, HSE prep, job placement, and more. Virtual Info sessions every Tuesday and Thursday at 1pm, as well as in-person info sessions every Wednesday at 1pm at both HOPE locations. Call 347-7730-4623 to learn how to apply. Government ID required.

rece1DuXfr6YOMVht.name: Free legal services for immigrant New Yorkers
rece1DuXfr6YOMVht.description:
Call the city-funded, free, and safe MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365, or call 311 and say, "Immigration Legal," between 9:00am to 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, to get help in any language:

Get answers to immigration policy questions and information on how and where to find help at Legal Support Centers across the City, housed in community sites, public health facilities, public schools, and libraries. Must be a New York City resident and making 200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

rece1DuXfr6YOMVht.group_name: The Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs

recpP7ilx5nr3MOjY.name: Free meal delivery for people with severe or chronic illness
recpP7ilx5nr3MOjY.description:
If you or someone you know is living with a severe or chronic illness and having trouble shopping or cooking, visit our website to confirm eligibility and apply for free, medically-tailored meals delivered to your door.

To be eligible, you must be living with a serious illness and have an ADL (Activities of Daily Living) limitation that prevents you from shopping or cooking for yourself which must be verified by a healthcare provider. Application forms and supporting documentation are available on the website and can be submitted electronically or mailed.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recIZpG3Q8Oo5pRjo.name: Free mental health resources for BIPOC in NYC
recIZpG3Q8Oo5pRjo.description: Visit the website to get connected to free resources and tools including "Find Me a Therapist", a Black Mental Health Resource Packet, and a Black Mental Health Provider Database.

rec2zhKDL8W7sd0Wt.name: Free weekly grocery distribution in Bedstuy and Long Island
rec2zhKDL8W7sd0Wt.description:
Find a Food Share location and weekly date/time on the website: Bedstuy, Farmingville, Wyandanch, Hemstead, and Huntington

Anyone can come to a Community Solidarity Food Share and get most, if not all, of the groceries they need for the week. Each Food Share is a free supermarket where community members share instead of pay for what they need. There are no prerequisites, there is no paperwork, all are welcome and everyone will be helped. We also share clothing, books, toys, school supplies, and other necessities.

rec31CTxaY2bTx6sN.name: Friendly VOICES Program
rec31CTxaY2bTx6sN.description: The Friendly VOICES program builds friendships and limits social isolation for older adults who are isolated for reasons such as COVID-19. Volunteers can do virtual or in-person visits. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or apply online.
rec31CTxaY2bTx6sN.group_name: New York City Department for the Aging

rechZVwtgKbkZCjpU.name: From Shelter to Apartment: A Guide to New York City's Department of Homeless Services
rechZVwtgKbkZCjpU.description: A foldout poster (English and Spanish versions) that breaks down people’s rights in homeless shelters and the different programs available to help them leave shelter and find affordable permanent housing. It also provides resources on other services shelter residents may have access to, like transportation benefits and storage grants, and what to do when your rights have been violated.

rec60a5a3fWA6k16s.name: Gay Men’s Health Crisis (GMHC) Hotline
rec60a5a3fWA6k16s.description: Call 1-800-243-7692 for a safe space to discuss a wide range of concerns. They provide information about topics such as HIV/AIDS, STDs, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), sexual health, and resources such as testing, healthcare, benefits, and counseling.

rec7Sk0zb9fYmluWv.name: Generation Q, at Queens Community House
rec7Sk0zb9fYmluWv.description: An after-school youth center for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer youth and allies, between the ages of 13 and 21. They offer a wide variety of educational and recreational opportunities, as well as social and emotional support. Open Tuesday through Friday 3-7pm.

recoUORRt1T87wGGV.name: Get Someone to Accompany You During an ICE Checkin Date
recoUORRt1T87wGGV.description: Got an upcoming ICE check-in date? Fill out the form linked on the website with your name, email, and ICE check-in date, and Families for Freedom staff will reach out to accompany you during the process.

recEZWl80yT59xEEw.name: Growing Up Healthy Hotline for Families with Children
recEZWl80yT59xEEw.description:
Call the hotline anytime at 1-800-522-5006. We're open 24/7. TTY 1-800-655-1789.

Help is available for health care, nutrition, pregnancy, family planning, children's needs, and more.

recJ8JEY9nRLzrmTM.name: Guidance on Applying for WIC for Families with Children
recJ8JEY9nRLzrmTM.description: Information on how to apply for WIC. The WIC program provides support with accessing food, nutrition education, and resources for expecting parents and caregivers. Government ID required.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recq2xs9YLxxBdOHJ.name: Guide to Reduced-Cost Veterinary Care
recq2xs9YLxxBdOHJ.description: An informational guide to programs offering financial assistance to help pay for veterinary care for your companion animals in the New York City area.

rec0CBifNE3B1tOWs.name: Harlem Community Fridge at 155th St
rec0CBifNE3B1tOWs.description: Harlem community fridge open 24/7 at 155th St and Bradhurst. Fresh produce on Saturdays 11 AM-1pm, and hot meals on Sundays 3-5pm.

reccpaRzLwimnd0Ui.name: Health Insurance Enrollment Assistance
reccpaRzLwimnd0Ui.description:
Free or inexpensive public health insurance is available for those meeting financial eligibility requirements.
Call 1-855-355-5777 to enroll directly or call the Medicaid Helpline (800) 541-2831 for assistance.
Free enrollment assistance through city - call 311 or text CoveredNYC (SeguroNYC en Español) to 877877.
For assistance enrolling through a local community-based organization: call (888) 614-5400 or email enroll@cssny.org.
All NYC Health + Hospitals centers will provide healthcare regardless of insurance coverage, and can help with insurance enrollment: call 1-844-NYC-4NYC.

recq1A7iaEarr8lEj.name: Health Insurance Information, Counseling and Assistance Program
recq1A7iaEarr8lEj.description: Call 1-800-701-0501 Monday - Friday, 8:30am-5pm to get answers to questions about Medicare, Medicare Advantage programs (managed care), Medicare prescription drug coverage, Medigap, and other health and long-term care insurance issues
recq1A7iaEarr8lEj.group_name: New York State Office For the Aging

rec8VEYuDG1uHSzTM.name: Health Services for Indigenous New Yorkers
rec8VEYuDG1uHSzTM.description: Call 718-215-8417 or enroll online to schedule health services or receive referrals at no charge. Services include urgent and emergency care, preventive care, primary and specialty care, behavioral health & recovery support, and transportation assistance. Note that we are only able to cover services arranged or referred by NYIC in advance. NYIC cannot reimburse members for services they book or receive independently (i.e. without prior approval).

recJzaGPsdlKRhrmM.name: Health and Disability Benefits support for People Living with HIV/AIDS

Or enroll in the Daily Money Management program to help seniors with day-to-day financial tasks.

recBCXinmZZ37seF6.name: Help with Eviction Prevention and Other Issues at POTS Legal Clinic
recBCXinmZZ37seF6.description: Speak with an attorney or legal advocate if you are behind on your rent or otherwise in danger of eviction, or for help accessing public benefits. POTS can also offer brief advice and referrals on other legal issues. Call 718-220-4892, ext. 101 and leave a message or send an email to legalclinc@potsbronx.org.

recn4TFhrkzlzKiAZ.name: Help with Moving Expenses
recn4TFhrkzlzKiAZ.description: Assistance for HRA clients related to moving, including help with moving expenses, broker's fees, and NYCHA security deposits. See Special Grant Document Guide webpage for specific forms.

recBbI21IrbGFzdJm.name: Helpline For Education-Related Information in New York City
recBbI21IrbGFzdJm.description:
Call (866) 427-6033 Monday through Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm to speak to an education specialist. 

Advocates for Children’s Jill Chaifetz Education Helpline is a resource for information and guidance on all education-related matters in New York City. If your child is struggling in school or experiencing school discrimination of any kind, specialists will assess the problem and provide free assistance, ranging from information you can use to advocate on your own, or assign you an education specialist or attorney to work with you directly.
recBbI21IrbGFzdJm.group_name: Advocates for Children of New York (AFC)
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recyEs7DC55Q15aia.name: Hire Harm-Reduction Medics with Sliding-Scale Rates for Events
recyEs7DC55Q15aia.description:
Hire harm-reduction medics from PartySafe Medics on a sliding-scale for events. Message on SMS, Signal, or WhatsApp, or visit the website or Instagram @partysafemedics. 

Services include safer drug use education, first aid, and overdose prevention. Medics are supplied with Naloxone, drug testing strips, safer drug use supplies, sexual health and hygiene products, oxygen tanks, and more.

rec3785Is8r49Byty.name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP): Money for Heat, Cooling, and Utility Expenses
rec3785Is8r49Byty.description: Apply for money to pay for fuel, your utility source, equipment and/or repairs through the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP). Apply online or call the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance at 800-692-0557 for assistance. A government ID is required.

recZExkHmZeULDCDu.name: Home Health Care Services and Assistance
recZExkHmZeULDCDu.description:
A range of home health care services to meet the needs of eligible persons with and without disabilities, including home health aides, personal care aides / companions, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapies, respiratory therapy, and social work services

To contact or ask questions about home health care services, contact the referral and information center, available 24/7, or visit the office Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

Fill out the form to contact the referral and information center. Additionally, they accept fee-for-service and long-term care insurance.

recbKjpkYou0SGMEZ.name: Home-Based Childcare Program
recbKjpkYou0SGMEZ.description: Contact WHEDco’s Home-Based Childcare Program (HBCC) at 347-708-7800. They work with families to help them explore options, determine their eligibility for childcare subsidies, and provide orientation on how to select the right caregiver for their needs. Also offer support services to licensed, registered, and legally-exempt service providers through the Home-Based Childcare Training Program.
recbKjpkYou0SGMEZ.group_name: Women’s Housing and Economic Development Corporation (WHEDco)

recGI0DCUAfxG20Jn.name: Homebase: Support for housing stability to avoid shelter entry
recGI0DCUAfxG20Jn.description:
Call 311 or visit nyc.gov/homebase to learn more about housing resources provided by the city of New York. Services include eviction prevention, assistance obtaining public benefits, employment search and assistance, financial counseling, relocation resources, and short-term financial assistance. This program is especially intended for individuals at imminent risk of entering the NYC shelter system/experiencing homelessness. 

Homebase is a homelessness prevention network with 26 locations across NYC’s five boroughs. Use the homebase locator to find the location in your borough.

This resource is currently only available over the phone. To access the hotline, call 311 and ask for homebase services. This service is specifically for people at risk of eviction/houselessness, and may not be useful for individuals already experiencing houselessness. 

A government ID is required.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recTHHG1sFCb6SJwE.name: Homeless Services for Individuals and Families in NYC
recTHHG1sFCb6SJwE.description: Works to provide a a steady and growing pipeline of permanent low-income housing, and other services such as eviction support.

recDeNzfu5eMHJtaV.name: Homeownership assistance for low-to-moderate income families in Queens
recDeNzfu5eMHJtaV.description: Non-profit offering a variety of free and low-cost counseling and seminars to aid people in achieving and maintaining homeownership.
recDeNzfu5eMHJtaV.group_name: Neighborhood Housing Services of Queens CDC

recta1Oxq06G9ZoaP.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Immigrants
recta1Oxq06G9ZoaP.description: Call the MinKwon Center at 718-460-5600 for help with benefits enrollment, setting up vaccination appointments, immigration services, food, medicine, and rental assistance.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recx6Iba82yVWfNfM.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Jewish Victims of Domestic Abuse
recx6Iba82yVWfNfM.description: Call/text/Whatsapp 888.883.2323 to speak to someone confidentially to talk about a domestic abuse situation. Shalom Task Force’s Legal Department also provides free, confidential legal services to victim-survivors of domestic and dating abuse, specializing in the Jewish community.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

reciKxXIR8O8EfQH5.name: Hotline for LGBTQ and HIV-affected Survivors of Violence
reciKxXIR8O8EfQH5.description: Call 212-714-1141 to reach a free, bilingual (English/Spanish), 24-hour, 365-day-a-year crisis intervention hotline that offers support to LGBTQ & HIV-affected survivors of any type of violence, as well as to those who love and support survivors, including those who have lost a loved one to violence.

recEh8dg39iatPcOg.name: Hotline for Substance Use Disorder and Mental Health Care Resources
recEh8dg39iatPcOg.description: Call 888-614-5400 for assistance in accessing treatment and insurance coverage for substance use disorders and mental health treatment. Hotline is confidential.

rec129bcshHg5pq7y.name: Housing Court Hotline
rec129bcshHg5pq7y.description: Call (212) 962-4795 Monday-Friday 9-5 for information about housing court procedures, landlord & tenant rules and regulations, enforcement of housing code violations, and referrals for free legal help and other community organizations.

reclDnkioaBOPfVLB.name: Housing Workshops to Learn About Housing Lottery Application Process
reclDnkioaBOPfVLB.description:
See website for locations to book an appointment. Receive step-by-step advice on what to expect through the housing lottery application process, including a review of the application and other required documents; information on financial empowerment and managing credit and debt portfolios; and additional support through the selection and interview process. 

In addition to larger workshops, CUFFH also provides One-on-One Application Assistance including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

recBGj87QRBMZeVXd.name: Housing and Homelessness Prevention
recBGj87QRBMZeVXd.description: Tenants can call 718-592-5757 ext. 243, email skhan@qchnyc.org, or email mmoore@qchnyc.org to access housing counseling and tenants rights workshops and receive help with applying for rental subsidies, negotiating lease renewals, and obtaining apartment unit repairs. Low-income individuals and families who at risk of eviction can access: household risk assessment, application assistance, access to government benefits, budget counseling and advocacy, including referrals to Food Access, Health Care, Public Assistance, legal and other supportive services to help people remain housed and stable.

recfJ43vtcggBE3bq.name: How to Set Up a Mutual Aid Fund
recfJ43vtcggBE3bq.description: A September 2020 essay about how the STL Mutual Aid Fund was set up, with tips for other mutual aid organizers.

recD3cNjNBZKiL1xn.name: How to Start and Run a Bulk Buying Club With Your Community
recD3cNjNBZKiL1xn.description:
A guide to starting and running a bulk food buying club. This covers: food sourcing, organizing members, running operation, and logistics. Also includes information about different student-run
bulk buying clubs in the CoFED network to learn about their strategies.

recfcyxqjecWoZzjY.name: Immigrant Legal Support for Survivors of Violence and Abuse
recfcyxqjecWoZzjY.description: We help immigrant survivors of violence and abuse obtain status and protection, enabling them to live and work safely in the United States. Our work focuses on humanitarian-based relief created specifically for immigrant survivors, such as U-visas, VAWA self-petitions and asylum, as well as “green card” applications, naturalization, and removal defense. We work with people from around the world who have experienced trauma and offer services in any language.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recHB7jm2cuH0bCTs.name: Improving Access to Healthcare for Immigrants
recHB7jm2cuH0bCTs.description: Call (718) 418-7690. Make the Road New York works to guarantee equal rights, access, and improved healthcare for the 2.5 million New Yorkers with limited English proficiency. Provides one-on-one assistance with health insurance and food stamp enrollment, hospital bill negotiation, health system navigation, nutrition education and emergency food services, Community Health Worker training and services, and HIV testing referrals.

rechi3OvqdYEPjqV2.name: In-Home Respite for People With Developmental Disabilities
rechi3OvqdYEPjqV2.description:
For people with developmental disabilities who reside at home with their families, AHRC New York City provides out-of-home and in-home respite opportunities, ranging from a period of a few hours to a few days.

To apply for respite services, contact the referral and information center on AHRCNYC's website.

recKnZLrxEgx7JJZb.name: Information About Housing Rights For City Residents
recKnZLrxEgx7JJZb.description: Information from the NYC Commission on Human Rights about what NYC Human Rights law covers in relation to housing discrimination including specific scenarios in which a complaint might be filed.

recOURnuOT9GTNkhB.name: Informational Guides for Immigrants
recOURnuOT9GTNkhB.description: Find information and links to organizations covering topics including DACA, TPS, mental health, education, and employment for undocumented and other immigrants.

recQEK6FPY4qHWyUE.name: Interest Free Loans for New Yorkers Seeking Immediate Financial Help
recQEK6FPY4qHWyUE.description: Hebrew Free Loan Society offers interest free loans for needs such as medical, addiction treatment, higher education, vocational training, and housing. Applicants must be defined as low to moderate income as a household. A government id is required.

rec2zbruiRz11KUvx.name: Job Application Platform for People with Disabilities & Chronic Illness
rec2zbruiRz11KUvx.description: A job application platform specifically designed to connect folks with disabilities and chronic illness to employers who have committed to offering flexibility and support of these employees' personal needs to ensure their success in the job.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recBBL64AWDethlGh.name: Know Your Rights Information, Legal Resources, and Trainings for Immigrant Communities
recBBL64AWDethlGh.description: Know Your Rights information, trainings, legal resources, and FAQs for communities impacted by ICE stops and raids.

recqJqm8QaFhY2NK3.description: Informative guides on the NYC shelter system, disability accommodations, and finding permanent housing.

rech2Wx9KsehRYtJJ.name: LGBT National Youth Hotline
rech2Wx9KsehRYtJJ.description: Call 800.246.7743 for volunteer LGBTQIA+ youth peer support hotline. Visit website for hours and one-on-one chat and chatroom options.

recHRmMey7ydRqK46.name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Mental Health Services
recHRmMey7ydRqK46.description: Fill out the pre-intake form on the website to learn more and get connected to 1:1 short-term counseling services available to individuals ages 18 and over who reside in New York State. Sessions are provided in person and virtually.
recHRmMey7ydRqK46.group_name: The Center - The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual & Transgender Community Center

recWnV93H1uhMIuRW.name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Peer Counseling Services: Walk-in clinic, short-term counseling, support groups
recWnV93H1uhMIuRW.description:
Walk-in center open Wednesdays 7pm – 9pm and Saturdays 6pm – 8pm. We also offer virtual sessions by appointment on Sunday evenings. Free (or $25 donation /session for those who can afford id) and open to all adults struggling with questions about sexual orientation and gender identity & expression, including alienation, relationships, and family. 

Counselors can provide resource information and referrals to short-term peer counseling or professional therapists after the walk-in clinic session.

Find information about groups at https://identityhouse.org/groups/.

rec7PdaltPXcNjTeT.name: Latinx LGBTQ+ Community Health Services: STI Testing, HIV Care, and Support
rec7PdaltPXcNjTeT.description: Call 212-675-3288 or make an appointment online. For the Latinx LGBTIA+ community to access free testing, workshops, enrollment into programs that allow you to access clinical services, and large scale social events. Services include both in-person and virtual resources including STI testing, HIV prevention and treatment, and substance use support.

recutSnPReUgYHn6y.name: Legal Advocacy and Services for Low-Income New Yorkers
recutSnPReUgYHn6y.description: Free legal assistance to low-income New Yorkers throughout New York City to resolve legal problems in the areas of housing; foreclosure; civil, disability and aging rights; bankruptcy, tax, consumer, employment, government benefits, immigration, and kinship care.

Port Richmond: (718) 727-1222

recxl09mPp3U1PkHS.name: Legal Help for LGBTQ and HIV-Positive Immigrants
recxl09mPp3U1PkHS.description: Find resource guides on topics including asylum, detention, family reunification, and visas. If your question isn't answered, fill out an online form to set up an appointment with a legal expert.

recfi6F6btGsjp1sF.description: A collection of resources for immigrants, including: A community toolkit, Know Your Rights information as printable posters and wallet cards, Know Your Rights curriculum with presentation and facilitator materials, immigration detention support information, family preparedness guides, and more. recLVGOjLeYf1F3pD.name: Legal Issues in Mutual Aid Operations: A Preliminary Guide
recLVGOjLeYf1F3pD.description: A June 2020 article by Michael Haber about legal issues that impact groups engaged in mutual aid, with a focus on New York. It gives legal information on topics including: risk of liability; questions around governance and incorporation; safety policies, liability waivers, and insurance; banking and mutual aid; funding mutual aid and taxation of mutual aid; crowdfunding regulations; and food storage and safety rules.

recP1MD3WdMrMwN9D.name: Legal Support Services for LGBTQIA, Polyamorous, and Underserved Families
recP1MD3WdMrMwN9D.description: Call (732) 639-1657 or fill out an intake form on the website to access legal support services, including: name and gender marker changes on identity documents, will and estate documents, known donor agreements, family formation such as cohabitation and coparenting agreements, parentage petitions, and nuptial agreements. Requires documentation of residency and income.

rec2Jz6R7tsjbBqCs.name: Legal services for individuals who face domestic violence
rec2Jz6R7tsjbBqCs.description: For domestic violence-related inquiries, please reach out to our office by phone or email and request the Domestic Violence Program. In-person meetings are by appointment only.

recaWkU6yFhVDo4fh.name: Legal support for discrimination for people with conviction records
recaWkU6yFhVDo4fh.description: The Worker Justice Project combats discrimination faced by workers with arrest or conviction records living in New York City. If you have been denied a job or a license because of your arrest or conviction record and you live in New York City, email the Worker Justice Project at WorkerJustice@legal-aid.org or call 888-663-6880 Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

recVNMdHXs4Lg65qR.name: Lemontree Food Helpline / La línea de ayuda alimentaria de Lemontree
recVNMdHXs4Lg65qR.description:
Need food? Submit a webform with your phone number to get help from a real person 10a-6p every day. We can help you find the closest food pantry, apply for SNAP, and more.
¿Necesitas comida? Llena un formulario en línea con tu número de teléfono para conectar con una persona verdadera 10a-6p cada día quien puede ayudarte a encontrar comida gratis, aplicar para SNAP, y más.

recnUWRb6LRrQFXzs.name: Lifeline Grocery Packages
recnUWRb6LRrQFXzs.description: Sign-up online for this community initiative that delivers groceries free to families in Queens, NYC, but note that there is often a waitlist. recEZ4Yajy0aakn6U.name: Live 24 Hour Domestic Violence Hotline
recEZ4Yajy0aakn6U.description: Call 800-664-5880 24/7 to reach Violence Intervention Program (VIP), a Latina-led organization that provides healing, housing, and economic justice to thousands of survivors of domestic and sexual violence in NYC each year.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recZ5TizaPu6wMgQZ.name: Low and No Cost Healthcare through NYC Health + Hospitals
recZ5TizaPu6wMgQZ.description: Visit NYCCare.nyc or call 1-646-NYC-CARE (1-646-692-2273) to enroll in the NYC Care program and access low- and no-cost healthcare from NYC Health + Hospitals, regardless of immigration status. Proof of identity, proof of income, proof of address, and insurance eligibility determination are required. Even if you are unable to provide the required documents, you may still be able to enroll.

recjQ4OC7sQdg4xqo.name: Low to No Cost Sexual Health Care, Immunizations, and TB Care
recjQ4OC7sQdg4xqo.description:
The DOHMH Public Health Clinics provide sexual health, immunization, and TB services- regardless of insurance or immigration status. We’re especially focused on making sure care is accessible, LGBTQ+ inclusive, and welcoming for all. If anyone doesn't have health insurance, we offer services on a sliding scale based on income and family size. No income proof is required and no one is ever turned away due to inability to pay.

Clinics are located in Central Harlem, Morrisania, Chelsea, Fort Greene, Jamaica, and Corona

Monday-Saturday 9am-5pm (syringe exchange 9-4:30).

recKUoPhwLNcUVA38.name: Mejorando el acceso al servicio médico para los inmigrantes

recKUoPhwLNcUVA38.application_process: Para todos los Servicios de Salud llame: 1-866-365-2724. Escuche las opciones y deje un mensaje de voz. Un miembro del Equipo de Salud le devolverá su llamada dentro de unos días.

reczIacXCcrqQgM5S.name: Mental Health Resource Directory for Black/African-American Communities
reczIacXCcrqQgM5S.description: A Directory of Mental Health Providers and Programs serving the African-American community.

rec7oDQrGpKaZlCXP.name: Mental Health Resources for LGBTQ+ Community
rec7oDQrGpKaZlCXP.description: Free membership-based community of LGBT adults living with a mental illness. Services include peer support groups and social activities.

rec7jqZigqBz9wkfP.name: Mentoring and Advocacy for Disadvantaged Girls, Femmes, and Gender-Expansive Youth
rec7jqZigqBz9wkfP.description: Call 347-918-8723 Monday-Friday 10am-6pm or email info@girlvow.org for mentoring and other support such as advocacy.

rec05Xf2dIdu7NrjE.name: Mentors and Educators for Students in NYC Shelters
rec05Xf2dIdu7NrjE.description: Register and enroll a student, 5-21 years of age, living in an NYC shelter with educational programs and tutors that can assist them in strengthening their academic skills and achieving their educational goals.

recRpgSUZkCrpjaJT.name: Mercadito Solidario Project
recRpgSUZkCrpjaJT.description: Community initiative that provides fresh and free food to the TransGNB community every Wednesday 3-6pm at 3763 83rd St Suite #1B, Jackson Heights, NY 11372.

recoyjzkKc08k2Nxl.description: Emergency grant to help pay for rent or mortgage that you owe. Must provide documentation showing how future rent payments will be made, including a statement from a third party who will help you pay your rent.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recT0xScmWVzt2fgV.name: Mood Disorder Support Groups
recT0xScmWVzt2fgV.description:
MDSG is a bi-weekly free support group network for people dealing with a mood disorder. Meetings are Wednesday and Friday 7:30-9:15 over zoom. Groups available include Bipolar, Unipolar, Under 30, and Friends and Family.

A donation is requested, but no one is turned away.

recN67ddQsprR88kj.name: Mouse Create: educator resource for free STEM, Design & CS Courses for school groups
recN67ddQsprR88kj.description: An online learning platform designed for young people to build the tech & design skills. Educators from schools, community centers, and afterschool providers can partner with Mouse to integrate Mouse project curricula into their programs and classes, choosing from courses that cover circuitry, game design, web literacy, coding, green technology, and more.

recbXml8nC8jeZWP6.name: Mutual Aid + Sisterhood Centering Young Black Women

reci4dEpLewIddMX3.name: Mutual Aid 101 Toolkit #WeGotOurBlock

recTCJPiCbrnDtpNc.name: My Bronx Impact: Find Free or Cost-based Resources by Zipcode

recMc378afAbGuhGR.name: NYC Affordable Housing Lottery Application Process Info and Training

recHaJ149g4dzDfIi.description: A collection of resources for harm reduction, offering information about sites for safe syringes and Narcan access, as well as toolkits, fact sheets, and training materials.

recccfqFBLGVVtMUS.description:

recd75FKKJmLMSAnQ.description: 1-800-985-5990, is a 24/7, 365-day-a-year. A National hotline dedicated to providing year-round disaster crisis counseling. recCPRX5cCYSNYWan.name: Neighbors Together Empowerment Program
recCPRX5cCYSNYWan.description:
The Neighbors Together Empowerment Program connects its members to important resources such as housing, public benefits, job training, health and mental health care, legal services, income tax filing, and other resources needed by our members. They offer regular on-site clinics to provide specialized support to members. Please call 718.498.7256 for more information or to schedule an appointment.

reckzZM3AO5gOhUA6.description: A list of organizations offering family legal aid and pro bono services in New York City.

rec7makS5sLYBLv6Y.name: Residential Services and Support for People with Developmental Disabilities
rec7makS5sLYBLv6Y.description:
To apply, contact the referral and information center. Call 212-780-4491 to get more information on making referrals or contact the Referral and Information Center online at https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/. 

Residential supports fall under three models:
1. Individualized Residential Alternatives (IRAs)
Supervised IRAs are traditional family-style group homes, providing 24-hour staff support and supervision for up to 14 residents.
Supportive IRAs provide need-based supports and services for those who are living in their own homes or apartments but do not require 24-hour staff support and supervision. Supportive IRAs are limited to 3 or fewer residents.
2. Supervised Apartments
3. Residential settings for people who are medically fragile (with 24/7 Nursing Care) AHRC NYC operates two residences for aging individuals who require full-time nursing oversight.  Support staff are comprised of nurse practitioners and supervising registered nurses, who are on-site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  Residents also have access to speech, physical, and occupational therapies as needed, as well as a day habilitation program operated within the residence.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

Classes are designed to prepare students for the Test Assessing Secondary Completion (TASC) that will provide them with a High School Equivalency Diploma. The Free English as a Second Language (ESL) classes (Level I - Level IV) are for non-native English speakers to improve listening, speaking, reading and writing.

reccuRqBPcW6w1DCo.description: See website for application and eligibility details. Emergency financial assistance is available for SAG-ASTRA members who are in urgent financial need due to an unexpected life crisis such as a natural disaster, accident, health crisis creating a financial burden, loss of work due to an illness, loss of housing due to an eviction, death in the family, or other emergency crisis situations covered under IRS guidelines which pertain to granting tax-free monies to individuals.

recSAnGUptOxct8um.name: SNAP Enrollment Assistance
recSAnGUptOxct8um.description: Call 347-880-2922 to speak to local Met Council Nutrition Outreach and Education Program (NOEP) coordinator to help to determine if you are eligible to apply for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and help you complete and submit your application. Free and confidential.

rec6zBlhkXBFn58KP.name: Safe Homes Project - Domestic Violence Programs
rec6zBlhkXBFn58KP.description:
24-Hour Hotline 718-499-2151

Good Shepherd Services’ Safe Homes Project provides an array of free services, which include a hotline, counseling, safety-planning, as well as a 20-bed shelter for survivors and their children. It also provides targeted services for special populations, including Spanish-speakers, youth, and LGBTQ survivors of partner violence.

All services are offered in both English and Spanish.

recQ18c4vnnMyVxuh.name: Sakhi for South Asian Women Helpline for Gender-Based Violence
recQ18c4vnnMyVxuh.description:

The helpline is able to assist in English, Hindi, Urdu, and Bengali. In addition, they also have an over-the-phone interpretation service if needed for another language.

recLwZ7Baf2n48Xsz.name: School & Student Rights Legal Support
recLwZ7Baf2n48Xsz.description:
If The Legal Aid Society represents you or your child in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can reach out to the attorney to be directed to help with education issues.

If you are not involved in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can ask for help with your child’s education needs by calling The Legal Aid’s Civil Access to Benefits helpline at 888-663-6880.

recVnW4MzSYHjXhlk.description: A listing of free virtual events and activities including fitness classes and discussions. For tech questions, call the Senior Planet NYC hotline at (917) 936-4410.

rec51ntJXmv35aaeZ.name: Services to support older adults in Brooklyn

Must be at least 55 years of age, an NYC resident, currently unemployed or underemployed, and commit to volunteering 15 hours per week in a nonprofit or government agency.

recK0Grhtinj1J7SV.name: Sliding Scale Therapy in NY

recHLAK8rbcrGKlkG.name: Sliding-scale Bicycles and Bike Repair in Brooklyn
recHLAK8rbcrGKlkG.description: If you are in need of a complete bicycle, email bikeplantnyc@gmail.com with your height, what you will use the bike for, and your phone number, and you will be added to our list. recJd3sVUxuWYxcCF.name: Small Claims Court Action Center

Get free help with consumer problems and complaints in small claims court, such as the purchase of defective goods, shoddy services, unreturned security deposits, property damage or falling victim to deceptive business practices. 
While the Action Centers don’t provide legal advice or courtroom representation, they can help you resolve consumer problems and boost your chances of success in the small claims courts and with collecting a judgment.

recjCl7q3XLnVt6nk.description:
Walk-in Tuesdays: 10am-3:30pm or call the office.

Community Benefits Assistance (CBA) provides individuals and families with hands-on assistance in applying for public benefits. At our centers, we offer easy access to public services in one place, connecting people to the resources to attain higher education, jobs, and financial stability, legal counseling, help with financial planning, immigration services and referrals to other community-based organizations, as needed.

recDwaNsFD4Tsc6zI.name: Social Services on the Upper West Side
recDwaNsFD4Tsc6zI.description: Email socialservices@wscah.org or call 212-362-3662 ext. 126 to be connected with the Social Services department. Benefits include referrals to access shelter, substance abuse treatment, mental health services, financial counseling and tax preparation, educational programs, immigration legal assistance, and sign ups for health insurance, SNAP, SCRIE, and DRIE

recwVqJsIR00j88lw.name: Soporte y ayuda Legal para new yorkers de bajos recursos en Manhattan
recwVqJsIR00j88lw.description: Ayuda legal sin costo para Newyorkers de bajos recursos en la ciudad de New York. Ayuda legal para resolver problemas en las areas de Vivienda, juicio hipotecario, faltas civiles, discapacidad y derechos para la tercera edad; bancarrota, impuestos, consumidores, empleo, beneficios proporcionados por el govierno, immigración, y cuidado legal de menores.

languages.name: Chinese (Mandarin): 简体中文 / 繁體中文

recdLPlOSrHaNKSww.name: Source of Income Discrimination (SOI) Mapping Tool
recdLPlOSrHaNKSww.description: Explore the crowdsourced map to see how widespread discrimination based on housing vouchers is in a specific NYC neighborhood.

recD2IdyGSaXQIzXu.name: Substance Use and Mental Health 24-Hour Helpline
recD2IdyGSaXQIzXu.description: Call (800) 662-4357 (HELP) for individuals and families facing mental and/or substance use disorders. Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) runs a 24-hour mental health hotline that provides education, support, and connections to treatment. The helpline is confidential; they collect no information. In English and  Spanish. Can also text your zip code to 435748 (HELP4U) to find treatment centers in your area.
recD2IdyGSaXQIzXu.group_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

rec50qwOANGmGmfkA.name: Support Groups for Gender-Expansive Children, Transgender Adolescents, Their Families & Communities
rec50qwOANGmGmfkA.description: The Gender & Family Project (GFP) of the Ackerman Institute offers a variety of support groups in addition to other services. There are groups for children 5-10 years old, for gender expansive and transgender adolescents, for siblings, and for caregivers and family members. Support groups take place once per month with no obligation to attend consecutively, and they cost from $5 up on a sliding scale.

recA84AuwXtzy0dj3.name: Support for Formerly Incarcerated People
recA84AuwXtzy0dj3.description:
New clients call 212-691-7554 for services including intakes and enrollment, counseling, case management, access to benefits, job readiness training and employment services, education, mental health, treatment services, and food distribution.

Hours Monday-Thursday: 8 AM – 8 PM and Friday: 8 AM – 5 PM

recfcdrBGDydLq5Uv.name: Support for mothers impacted by the criminal legal system
recfcdrBGDydLq5Uv.description: Support services for mothers who have been incarcerated including food pantries, thrift shops, supportive housing, job training, educational opportunities, and programming for children and teens.

recKaPOtuMeTM5Y4c.name: Supportive Network for Caregivers for People with Special Healthcare Needs
recKaPOtuMeTM5Y4c.description: Call 1-800-405-8818 if you are working with a parent of a child with disabilities or special health care needs looking for information about support groups and available resources.
recKaPOtuMeTM5Y4c.group_name: Parent to Parent New York State

recdc6LUXP2BFpcTG.name: Supportive housing for adults, seniors, and veterans living with serious mental illness and/or substance use disorders
recdc6LUXP2BFpcTG.description:
Call 212-663-3000.
Supportive housing. The Bridge houses 1500+ people in the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Manhattan, and offers a range of on-site services based on client level of need, including case management, advocacy, therapeutic activities, and linkages to community-based treatment and services.

recOuDlfHBsRcP7A7.name: Talkin’ It Out - Phone Chat for Older Adults
recOuDlfHBsRcP7A7.description: Call to learn more. Older adults 60+ can "chat” confidentially by phone for free with a bilingual (Spanish/English) licensed Master’s Level Social Worker, to discuss issues and concerns outside of formal psychotherapy.

recX49zOvzw80TrKo.name: Temporary Financial Assistance for Families and Individuals
recX49zOvzw80TrKo.description: Temporary Assistance (TA) is temporary financial help for people who are unable to work, can’t find a job, or whose job does not pay enough. The two types of TA are Family Assistance and Safety Net Assistance. Apply via https://mybenefits.ny.gov or file an application at your local department of Social Services. Government ID is required. Call the OTDA Hotline for more information: 1-800-342-3009
recX49zOvzw80TrKo.group_name: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance

recdHXl50fwHaFCkb.name: Temporary Shelter and Help for Muslim Women and Families Facing Domestic Violence, Eviction, or Homelessness
recdHXl50fwHaFCkb.description: Call the Helpline at 718-833-2425. They provide shelter, legal and immigration services, help navigating public or government assistance, managing medical needs and mental health resources, assisting in securing long-term housing, and finding employment.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recyiPpV0rpJ3aKgj.name: Tenants’ Rights Telephone Hotline: 212-979-0611
recyiPpV0rpJ3aKgj.description:
Call the free Tenants' Rights Telephone Hotline at 212-979-0611 to ask questions about:
Getting repairs from negligent landlords, getting adequate heat in the winter months, dealing with the threat of eviction, questions about leases and lease renewals, and legal rent increases for rent-regulated apartments.

recV1Hz3hTAzKG1W4.name: Therapy and Advocacy for Survivors of Sexual Violence
recV1Hz3hTAzKG1W4.description: Call 212-423-2140. Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI) works with survivors who have experienced sexual assault and intimate partner violence. Provide therapy support and advocate for the safety of clients. Located at East Harlem, the Upper East Side, and Queens.
recV1Hz3hTAzKG1W4.group_name: Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI)
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recQd6IcDhBraO6p8.name: Trans Lifeline Hotline
recQd6IcDhBraO6p8.description: Trans and questioning people can call (877) 565-8860 from 1 PM-9 PM Eastern and speak to a trans/nonbinary peer operator. Full anonymity and confidentiality, and no nonconsensual active rescue (calling 911, emergency services, or law enforcement).

rec5H5vw8uGvIzUGc.name: Trans Needle Exchange
rec5H5vw8uGvIzUGc.description: Trans Needle Exchange is a non-profit mail-based service providing free HRT needle supplies for trans folk who cannot access or afford their own.

recUkf8uRtCKPHXhO.name: Tuition free access to youth dance company (ages 7-18)
recUkf8uRtCKPHXhO.description: Opportunity for year-long free dance and performance training for youth ages 7-18 at Dancewave (located in Gowanus, Brooklyn). Scholarship application available on the website. Please email school@dancewave.org with questions.

recjlrO8YQpCitbjs.name: VOCAL-NY Syringe Exchange
recjlrO8YQpCitbjs.description: Access sterile injection equipment and other supplies for safer injection, fentanyl testing strips, and hygiene supplies. VOCAL-NY is a New York State-licensed Syringe Exchange Program (SEP). Find the Syringe Exchange Team at Douglass St between 3rd & 4th Aves in Brooklyn. May be able to deliver supplies to you through the Peer-Delivered Syringe Exchange (email paula@vocal-ny.org).

recRgyXuBCXicrXM8.name: Veteran Housing and Employment Services
recRgyXuBCXicrXM8.description: For housing services, reach out to the supportive services arm of the organization (631-227-0777 or ssvfintakes@sus.org). For employment, contact 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

recRXDcM6RFdFJ942.name: Virtual 12-Step meetings for people who use crystal meth
recRXDcM6RFdFJ942.description: A calendar of online and in-person (socially distant) meetings and social activities. Call the 24 hour helpline at 1-855-638-4373.
recRXDcM6RFdFJ942.group_name: New York Crystal Meth Anonymous Intergroup (NYCMA)

recxHubFM0ta9eiAl.name: Virtual Recovery Meetings
recxHubFM0ta9eiAl.description: An aggregated calendar of online recovery meetings. Create an account with an email address to access live virtual meetings for both support and socialization. Listed meetings include Alcoholics Anonymous, Al-Anon, Narcotics Anonymous, Overeaters Anonymous, and Coronavirus Support groups.

recIIh4XRv2Nqehem.name: Volunteer Program for New Yorkers
recIIh4XRv2Nqehem.description: On the website, Bright Light offers volunteering events throughout the city.

rec9nG3Kjj0dmNG5K.name: Wellness Gatherings for Undocumented People
rec9nG3Kjj0dmNG5K.description: Register for 6-week virtual Wellness Support Groups led by trained mental health providers or registered clinicians, designed to help undocumented people feel less alone and more understood.

recWwuvmPGtotfihE.name: Woodside Community Fridge
recWwuvmPGtotfihE.description: Access or drop off free food at the Woodside Community fridge at 41-26 58th St in Woodside, Queens.

recKc2oQmXw4k8W9W.name: Workforce Training and Supportive Housing for Homeless Men
recKc2oQmXw4k8W9W.description:
Call Brooklyn: 646-672-2973 | Harlem: 718-417-2538 for more information.
Ready, Willing, and Able is a 12-month residential program with paid work—complemented by holistic social services, career training, education, and sobriety support. If you’re already in the New York City shelter system and would like to join Ready, Willing & Able, talk to your case manager or parole officer about a transfer to a Doe Fund facility. The Ready, Willing & Able program is open to all men able to work and maintain sobriety, ages 18 and up.

recQ7ImXtzBHbF5Cn.name: Workshops and Programming for Youth
recQ7ImXtzBHbF5Cn.description: A calendar of workshops and programming for youth in their late teens to early 20s with the goal of improving the quality of education, health care and life-skills training for underserved adolescents and young adults.

recg8padt5791dFK2.name: Writing Workshops for Teens
recg8padt5791dFK2.description: Writing workshops for youth, with free and low-cost options for families who meet income requirements.

rec1xCueVrw2nu1H6.name: Youth Mentoring for Children Ages 7 to 16
rec1xCueVrw2nu1H6.description: Children between the ages of 7 and 16 will be matched with an adult mentor who will offer friendship, guidance, and advice. There's no cost for mentoring, but each child should be committed to this program for 8 hours per month, for a minimum of one year. Visit the website to enroll.
rec1xCueVrw2nu1H6.group_name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of NYC

organizations.name: -No Associated Group
organizations.description: Resources provided by individuals or other efforts not affiliated with an existing group.

organizations.name: 826nyc
organizations.description: 826nyc's mission is to help young people build creative writing skills through support and engagement.

organizations.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
organizations.description: The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is a national network of local crisis centers that provides free and confidential emotional support to people in suicidal crisis or emotional distress 24 hours a day, 7 days a week in the United States.

organizations.name: AARP
organizations.description: AARP is a nonprofit that advocates for older Americans, including for health and fiscal issues at the state and local level.

organizations.name: Abortion Finder
organizations.description: Provides clear, up-to-date information about the availability of abortion care across the country.

organizations.name: Ackerman Institute
organizations.description: A nonprofit that offers couple & family therapy services, trains mental health professionals, and conducts research.

organizations.name: Adelphi Free Store
organizations.description: We are a small collective of neighbors who have built and maintain the store on the corner of Adelphi St and Greene Ave in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. You can reach out to us and get involved!. You can reach out to us and get involved! Open 24/7 and accessible to anyone and everyone, our free store is a place for community members to stop by anytime and drop off donations directly onto the store’s shelves, from clothing and linens to toys and home decor. Please donate in moderation and with consideration.

organizations.name: Advocates for Children of New York (AFC)
organizations.description: Advocates for Children of New York works on behalf of children who are at greatest risk for school-based discrimination and/or academic failure due to poverty, disability, race, ethnicity, immigrant or English Language Learner status, sexual orientation, gender identity, homelessness, or involvement in the foster care or juvenile justice systems.

organizations.name: AHRCNYC
organizations.description: AHRCNYC advocates for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities to lead full and equitable lives.

organizations.name: Ali Forney Center
organizations.description: 24-hour drop-in center offering medical and mental health services, housing support, and linkage to other programs for homeless LGBTQ+ youth.

organizations.name: ANAD
organizations.description: ANAD is a nonprofit in the U.S. that provides free, peer support services to anyone struggling with an eating disorder, regardless of age, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, or background.

organizations.name: Animal Medical Center
organizations.description: The Animal Medical Center is the world’s largest non-profit animal hospital with 100+ veterinarians providing medical care across more than 20 specialties and services.

organizations.name: Artists Fellowship Emergency Financial Aid
organizations.description: The Artists’ Fellowship provides emergency aid to professional fine artists and their families in times of sickness, natural disaster, bereavement or unexpected extreme hardship.

organizations.name: Asian Americans For Equality (AAFE)
organizations.description: Through community development, Asian Americans for Equality (AAFE) advances racial, social and economic justice for Asian Americans and other systematically disadvantaged communities, guided by our experiences as Asian Americans and a commitment to civil rights.

organizations.name: Astoria Food Pantry
organizations.description: We are a neighbor-to-neighbor pantry, entirely donation based and volunteer run. We distribute FREE groceries twice a week, run a FREE store, host FREE social and educational events, offer FREE language classes, and maintain a space for ALL neighbors to come together under the common goal of bettering each other's lives.

organizations.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of NYC
organizations.description: A youth mentoring organization that does one-to-one mentoring, Workplace Mentoring Program (corporate engagement), affinity groups, College & Career Success Program, Bigs in Blue, and other community partner programs.

organizations.name: Bike Plant
organizations.description: Bike Plant is a bicycle repair shop located in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn.

organizations.name: Black Trans Travel Fund
organizations.description:
Our mission as a Black trans led collective 
​is to provide Black trans women with financial and material resources towards
education, community, safety and removing travel barriers.

organizations.name: Boris Lawrence Henson Foundation
organizations.description: BLHF provides culturally competent therapy referrals and wellness resources. It actively promotes mental wellness and strives to eradicate stigmatizing language surrounding mental illness through impactful programs, awareness campaigns, and educational initiatives.

organizations.name: Breaking Ground
organizations.description: Breaking Ground’s mission is to strengthen individuals, families and communities by developing and sustaining exceptional supportive and affordable housing as well as programs for homeless and other vulnerable New Yorkers.

organizations.name: Bright Light
organizations.description: At Bright Light, we believe in making volunteerism easy and impactful for young professionals. Our mission is to empower individuals by providing flexible, accessible, and well-organized volunteer opportunities that seamlessly fit into busy schedules. We are a community driven by the core values of empowerment, inclusivity, and collaboration—where everyone has the chance to shine their light and make a difference.

organizations.name: Bronx Impact
organizations.description: Bronx Impact is a collective-impact initiative based in the Bronx that brings together community organizations, government agencies, businesses, and residents to reduce poverty and promote social and economic mobility.

organizations.name: Bronx Mutual Aid
organizations.description: Bronx Mutual Aid (BXMA) is a grassroots mutual aid organization based in the South Bronx. Founded in 2026, BXMA provides free produce, hot meals, clothing, toiletries, books, and other essential supplies to neighborhood residents every Saturday. In addition to meeting immediate material needs, BXMA organizes political education programs and activities for children, with a focus on building community power and collective care.

organizations.name: BronxWorks
organizations.description: BronxWorks helps individuals and families improve their economic and social well-being. From toddlers to seniors, we feed, shelter, teach, and support our neighbors to build a stronger community.

organizations.name: Brooklyn Community Kitchen
organizations.description: Brooklyn Community Kitchen prepares and serves hot meals for the Brooklyn community every Saturday from 11 am to 1 pm. The kitchen partners with local organizations and restaurants to gather food that would otherwise go to waste.

organizations.name: Brooklyn Grange
organizations.description: Brooklyn Grange farms rooftops, builds green spaces, and promotes sustainable living and local ecology through food, education, and events.

organizations.name: Build Up Justice NYC
organizations.description: Build Up Justice NYC advances economic and racial justice by providing community-centered free civil legal services to low-income New Yorkers across all five boroughs.

organizations.name: Bushwick Community Fridge
organizations.description: Bushwick Community Fridge on Hart and Myrtle. Started during COVID by volunteers with Food Not Bombs Bed Stuy, Community Solidarity, and In Our Hearts NYC.

organizations.name: Bushwick Mutual Aid
organizations.description: Neighbors helping neighbors in Bushwick. Run the Bushwick Free Store, Tuesdays 3-5pm at Maria Hernandez Park.

organizations.name: Callen-Lorde
organizations.description: Callen-Lorde Community Health Center provides sensitive, quality health care and related services targeted to New York’s lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities — in all their diversity — regardless of ability to pay. To further this mission, Callen-Lorde promotes health education and wellness, and advocates for LGBTQ health issues.

organizations.name: Care for the Homeless
organizations.description: Care for the Homeless coordinates health care at 30 service sites where homeless people congregate and without regard to their ability to pay. Our service sites include shelters for single adults, family shelters, soup kitchens, drop-in centers, SROs, and a street outreach program to the mentally ill in four of New York City’s five boroughs.

organizations.name: Carefully
organizations.description: Carefully's mission is to make the world better through community, care, and mutualism (the idea that giving and receiving creates a stronger community). By building a strong network of co-ops, family networks, and childcare swaps, they work to help families save money, get back to work, and have more time for the things that matter.

organizations.name: CaringKind
organizations.description: CaringKind works with community partners to develop information, tools, and training to support individuals and families affected by Alzheimer's and dementia.

organizations.name: Catholic Charities
organizations.description: The Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of New York provides a number of services - including for the hungry, for children, for the homeless, and for immigrants and refugees - throughout the city for people of all religions.

organizations.name: Center for Independence of the Disabled
organizations.description: CIDNY is a nonprofit organization founded in 1978. We are part of the Independent Living Centers movement: a national network of grassroots and community-based organizations that enhance opportunities for all people with disabilities to direct their own lives.

organizations.name: Center for Urban Pedagogy
organizations.description: Our mission is to use the power of art and design to increase meaningful civic engagement in partnership with marginalized communities.

organizations.name: CERF+
organizations.description: CERF+ serves artists who work in craft disciplines by providing a safety net to support strong and sustainable careers. CERF+’s core services are education programs, advocacy, network building and emergency relief.

organizations.name: Chhaya CDC
organizations.description: Chhaya CDC was founded in 2000 to advocate for the housing needs of New York City’s South Asian community. Our mission is to work with New Yorkers of South Asian origin to advocate for and build economically stable, sustainable, and thriving communities.

organizations.name: Child Center of NY
organizations.description: The Child Center of NY has more than 50 locations and 100 programs in NYC’s most under-served communities. They serve children, adults, and whole families and communities with programs in six areas: early childhood education, behavioral health, health homes & integrated care, prevention and family support, residential services, and youth development.

organizations.name: Children's Aid
organizations.description: Children's Aid helps children in poverty to succeed and thrive by providing comprehensive supports to children, youth, and their families in targeted high-needs New York City neighborhoods.

organizations.name: CHiPS
organizations.description: We feed the hungry in our soup kitchen, and shelter homeless young women & their infants in our Frances Residence.

organizations.name: Chosen Family Law Center
organizations.description: The Chosen Family Law Center is building the legal framework to support dignity and justice for all family types. We pursue our mission through advocacy and education, legislative development, and direct legal services for those in need.

organizations.name: Chronically Capable
organizations.description: A platform that connects people with chronic illnesses or disabilities to flexible and remote employment opportunities, and provides a community and support around employment.

organizations.name: Churches United for Fair Housing (CUFFH)
organizations.description: CUFFH is a grassroots organization that works towards community empowerment through community organizing, youth engagement and by providing social services.

organizations.name: City Bar Justice Center
organizations.description: The City Bar Justice Center furthers access to justice by addressing unmet civil legal needs of New Yorkers struggling with poverty and other systemic socioeconomic barriers. The Justice Center mobilizes law firms, corporate legal departments, and other legal institutions to provide pro bono legal services; educates the public on pertinent legal issues; fosters strategic community relationships; and impacts public policy.

organizations.name: City Harvest
organizations.description: City Harvest rescues perfectly good, nutritious food that would otherwise go to waste and delivers it for free to New Yorkers experiencing hunger. Delivers soon-to-expire produce to food banks and agencies. Produce comes from wholesalers, other food banks, and major retailers.

organizations.name: Citymeals on Wheels
organizations.description: A nonprofit organization that partners with the City of New York to deliver meals to homebound elderly New Yorkers.

organizations.name: Claim Our Space NOW
organizations.description:
Claim Our Space Now is a Black, Queer, and immigrant led nonprofit organization based in Harlem, New York. Our mission to ritualize intersectional community care and action to dismantle white supremacy and save the lives of all Black and oppressed identities. 

Our work is brought to life by activating our sizable volunteer base across our four active programs that seek to address both immediate and long-term community needs. We are one of the few completely volunteer-based coalitions founded in 2020 following George Floyd’s lynching that is still doing the life-saving work of meeting fundamental needs of Black and Brown communities in New York and beyond.

organizations.name: Classon Community Fridge
organizations.description: Classon Community Fridge is a community-run resource and mutual aid group. We manage a refrigerator and pantry on the street outside of Dean Crossfit (543 Grand Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238) that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access. We also host grocery distributions at 641 Classon Avenue on the second Monday of each month. Our motto is "take what you need, leave what you can."

organizations.name: Clear Captions
organizations.description: A real-time phone captioning service for people experiencing hearing loss.

organizations.name: Coalition for the Homeless
organizations.description: The Coalition for the Homeless is the nation’s oldest advocacy and direct service organization helping homeless men, women and children. We believe that affordable housing, sufficient food and the chance to work for a living wage are fundamental rights in a civilized society.

organizations.name: Colectivo Intercultural TRANSgrediendo
organizations.description: The TRANSgrediendo Intercultural Collective is nationally recognized as a bilingual and multicultural movement that defends and promotes the human rights of the diverse Trans* and gender-diversity identity populations in the United States.

organizations.name: Collective Focus Resource Hub
organizations.description: Collective Focus is a Women, POC and LGBTQIA+-led organization fostering resourcefulness and empowerment at our Brooklyn-based Resource Hub. Our community-based approaches confront the challenges of food insecurity and food waste, racial and economic inequality & mental health by building access to food, clothing, creative and wellness.

organizations.name: Community Care Collective (ccc)
organizations.description: A collective of young people in NYC working to build community and hold institutions accountable through mutual aid and political education. Distro Tuesdays 12:30-2:30pm in Washington Square Park.

organizations.name: Community Health Advocates
organizations.description: Provides assistance and answers questions on health insurance, Medicaid, legal issues, and can help with healthcare benefit enrollment.

organizations.name: Community Service Society (CSS)
organizations.description: The Community Service Society of New York (CSS) has worked with and for New Yorkers since 1843 to promote economic opportunity and champion an equitable city and state. Through a strategic combination of data-driven research, direct services, and people-driven advocacy, we ensure New Yorkers have the power to create change in their lives and the life of our city and state. Our programs, policy analysis, legal advocacy, and campaigns expand access to health care, safe and affordable housing, employment, opportunities for individuals with conviction histories, consumer debt assistance, and more—making a tangible difference in the lives of millions.

organizations.name: Community Solidarity
organizations.description: Community Solidarity shares free vegetarian groceries, clothing, book, and toys.

organizations.name: Cooperative Food Empowerment Directive (CoFED)
