The Justice Center mobilizes law firms, corporate legal departments, and other legal institutions to provide pro bono legal services; educates the public on pertinent legal issues; fosters strategic community relationships; and impacts public policy.

rec7QDun6J2YmNBsg.name: City Harvest
rec7QDun6J2YmNBsg.description: City Harvest rescues perfectly good, nutritious food that would otherwise go to waste and delivers it for free to New Yorkers experiencing hunger. Delivers soon-to-expire produce to food banks and agencies. Produce comes from wholesalers, other food banks, and major retailers.

recPTUBNSANTcPMuH.name: Claim Our Space NOW
recPTUBNSANTcPMuH.description:
Claim Our Space Now is a Black, Queer, and immigrant led nonprofit organization based in Harlem, New York. Our mission to ritualize intersectional community care and action to dismantle white supremacy and save the lives of all Black and oppressed identities. 

Our work is brought to life by activating our sizable volunteer base across our four active programs that seek to address both immediate and long-term community needs. We are one of the few completely volunteer-based coalitions founded in 2020 following George Floyd’s lynching that is still doing the life-saving work of meeting fundamental needs of Black and Brown communities in New York and beyond.

receiFlcUx1MtCHqW.name: Citymeals on Wheels
receiFlcUx1MtCHqW.description: A nonprofit organization that partners with the City of New York to deliver meals to homebound elderly New Yorkers.

recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.name: Classon Community Fridge
recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.description: Classon Community Fridge is a community-run resource and mutual aid group. We manage a refrigerator and pantry on the street outside of Dean Crossfit (543 Grand Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238) that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access. We also host grocery distributions at 641 Classon Avenue on the second Monday of each month. Our motto is "take what you need, leave what you can."

recDvVLiCoHx3BOiD.name: Clear Captions
recDvVLiCoHx3BOiD.description: A real-time phone captioning service for people experiencing hearing loss.

recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.name: Coalition for the Homeless
recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.description: The Coalition for the Homeless is the nation’s oldest advocacy and direct service organization helping homeless men, women and children. We believe that affordable housing, sufficient food and the chance to work for a living wage are fundamental rights in a civilized society.

recpgQyo3TpdNpYTz.name: Colectivo Intercultural TRANSgrediendo
recpgQyo3TpdNpYTz.description: The TRANSgrediendo Intercultural Collective is nationally recognized as a bilingual and multicultural movement that defends and promotes the human rights of the diverse Trans* and gender-diversity identity populations in the United States.

recJIcDMIK2kiMELF.name: Community Care Collective (ccc)
recJIcDMIK2kiMELF.description: A collective of young people in NYC working to build community and hold institutions accountable through mutual aid and political education. Distro Tuesdays 12:30-2:30pm in Washington Square Park.

recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.name: Collective Focus Resource Hub
recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.description: Collective Focus is a Women, POC and LGBTQIA+-led organization fostering resourcefulness and empowerment at our Brooklyn-based Resource Hub. Our community-based approaches confront the challenges of food insecurity and food waste, racial and economic inequality & mental health by building access to food, clothing, creative and wellness.

recVUclk7MmyiDLn9.name: Community Service Society (CSS)
recVUclk7MmyiDLn9.description: The Community Service Society of New York (CSS) has worked with and for New Yorkers since 1843 to promote economic opportunity and champion an equitable city and state. Through a strategic combination of data-driven research, direct services, and people-driven advocacy, we ensure New Yorkers have the power to create change in their lives and the life of our city and state. Our programs, policy analysis, legal advocacy, and campaigns expand access to health care, safe and affordable housing, employment, opportunities for individuals with conviction histories, consumer debt assistance, and more—making a tangible difference in the lives of millions.

recwXdBrHgvhJqFeK.name: Community Health Advocates
recwXdBrHgvhJqFeK.description: Provides assistance and answers questions on health insurance, Medicaid, legal issues, and can help with healthcare benefit enrollment.

recAOFy8P6p8w4iDR.name: Community Solidarity
recAOFy8P6p8w4iDR.description: Community Solidarity shares free vegetarian groceries, clothing, book, and toys.

rec3ggacriV3pGPhH.name: Cooperative Food Empowerment Directive (CoFED)
rec3ggacriV3pGPhH.description: Building a cooperative food economy, powered by the leadership of young people of color! We partner with food and land co-ops across the US and Canada to embody cooperative values + economics.

recUOyGsehgZmmcuS.name: Covenant House NY
recUOyGsehgZmmcuS.description: Covenant House New York’s mission is to help each young person find safety and refuge from the dangers of living on the streets. We do this through compassion, unconditional love and absolute respect.

rec7TI5mVAAPmwlh4.name: Crisis Text Line
rec7TI5mVAAPmwlh4.description: Connect with a Crisis Counselor. Text us. Get free, confidential, 24/7 support.

recDiMg0pHyatodZn.name: CUCS
recDiMg0pHyatodZn.description: Nonprofit committed to developing affordable housing and providing integrated programs that link housing, health and social services for New York’s homeless and most vulnerable people.

rec7Ozef2M8fhqHXU.name: CUNY Citizenship Now!
rec7Ozef2M8fhqHXU.description: We offer free, high-quality, and confidential immigration law services to help you and your family on your path to U.S. citizenship. Our attorneys and paralegals will assess your eligibility for legal benefits and help you apply if you qualify.

recdDyGw23pYlUquA.name: Dancewave
recdDyGw23pYlUquA.description: Dancewave provides access to supportive and empowering dance experiences that center social, emotional and cognitive development through movement. Developing programs to meet community needs, we use dance as a vehicle for transformation, expression, active citizenship and self reflection. Dancewave fosters a culture where dance is celebrated as a healing and inclusive art form.

recEirZnAFofbZsoq.name: Damayan Migrant Worker Center
recEirZnAFofbZsoq.description: Damayan is a grassroots organization that serves and empowers low-wage Filipino migrant workers living and working in New York City and New Jersey, especially domestic workers and labor trafficking survivors or modern day slaves.

recAai2YaRhnnO1mi.name: Darkness Rising Project
recAai2YaRhnnO1mi.description: Abolitionist BIPOC-operated mental health organization providing free mental health resources, wellness workshops, and video series.

recUyJ2OfpWgDioJ3.name: Day One NYC
recUyJ2OfpWgDioJ3.description: A nonprofit serving youth (24 and under) in NYC to prevent dating abuse and domestic violence, through legal advocacy, counseling, education, leadership programs.

recg8RNoOjGSGRKyg.name: Drive Change
recg8RNoOjGSGRKyg.description: At Drive Change, our mission is to equip young people with the tools to succeed in the food service industry and become leaders in their community.

rec3g1OG4UVRpKGMN.name: Dominican Women's Development Center
rec3g1OG4UVRpKGMN.description: Founded in 1988, the DWDC’s mission is to empower women and communities to achieve gender equality and social justice. The DWDC provides direct services and programs for all women and families that are affected by any for of oppression including racism, sexism, classism,  domestic and other forms of violence (such as sexual assault, sexual harassment, incest, and human trafficking).

recKN0wWKnaLi6THO.name: EduMate NYC
recKN0wWKnaLi6THO.description: Edumate is a free tutoring service for students in K-12.  Students are matched with college students to provide academic support primarily for kids who are of low income, homeless, undocumented, or have special needs.

recMwIaNp1bFoPqm4.name: Emma's Torch
recMwIaNp1bFoPqm4.description: We provide refugees with culinary training, ESL classes and interview preparation. We set them up for successful employment in an industry in which their cultural heritage and cuisine can be celebrated. What’s more, we provide a community in which they can build supportive relationships.

reczOXbRyW8IwldSN.name: Entertainment Community Fund
reczOXbRyW8IwldSN.description: The Entertainment Community Fund fosters stability and resiliency, and provides a safety net for performing arts and entertainment professionals over their lifespan.

receyKSu1Fg1xB5s6.name: Episcopal Actors Guild
receyKSu1Fg1xB5s6.description: For 95 years, the Episcopal Actors’ Guild has been a community that celebrates and supports the talent and dedication needed to sustain a career in the performing arts. Your gift will ensure that the services of EAG will always be available for our city’s amazing performers "of all faiths, and none" when they experience financial crisis.

rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.name: EVLovesNYC
rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.description: We are a volunteer-powered 501(c)3 mutual aid focused on combatting food insecurity in NYC, and helping recent migrants to our city by providing food, job training, advocacy, and resources.

recBB7h77e9niD19C.name: Families For Freedom
recBB7h77e9niD19C.description: Families for Freedom is a New York-based multi-ethnic human rights organization by and for families facing deportation.

recfUWygymsr0l522.name: Fenix Community Fridge
recfUWygymsr0l522.description: Established in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, a community fridge at 586 Seneca Ave in Ridgewood. Free food distribution every Friday at 5pm.

recuz5P52xiJZOlAK.name: Fireweed Collective
recuz5P52xiJZOlAK.description: Fireweed Collective provides mental health education and mutual aid through a Healing Justice lens, centering the needs of those most marginalized by our society.

recIPF1mALNR5kMIf.name: Food Bank for New York City
recIPF1mALNR5kMIf.description: With food donated from partners such as Baldor, Duane Reade, Hood, Target, etc., Food Bank for New York City is a nonprofit organization that distributes food and provides meals for people who cannot afford to buy food.

recaFoKbv5zeTWnqN.name: For The Gworls
recaFoKbv5zeTWnqN.description: We are a Black, trans-led collective that curates parties to fundraise money to help Black transgender people pay for their rent, gender-affirming surgeries, smaller co-pays for medicines/doctor’s visits, and travel assistance.

reci4hOr3GsyP8TK3.name: Free Clinic Directory
reci4hOr3GsyP8TK3.description: Directory of free clinics in the U.S.

recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.name: G-REBELS
recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.description: G-REBELS is a grassroots, Brooklyn based org aimed at promoting solidarity through community action. They facilitate peer-to-peer food distribution and regularly provide COVID, Flu A + B, and RSV rapid PCR tests, care kits, and associated resources for the community.

rec4gUhmL3kofpo9c.name: Freedom House
rec4gUhmL3kofpo9c.description:
pened in 2006 in New York City, Freedom House is a domestic violence shelter (90-180 day stay) for women, men and children. We serve both families and single individuals with or without disabilities. We have worked with people from 40 states and internationally and we welcome all members of the LGBTQ community.

Our safe, confidential and fully accessible shelter (the first in the nation) offers private living spaces of various sizes to accommodate both singles and larger families. We are equipped to serve all survivors and their children with disabilities including (but not limited to) wheelchair users, people who are D/deaf or hard of hearing and blind or visually impaired.

recFExVAL1FofyRBh.name: Girl Vow, Inc.
recFExVAL1FofyRBh.description: Girl Vow, Inc. is a non-profit organization that offers mentoring and other support to disadvantaged girls, femmes, and gender-expansive youth in New York City. They support all girls who identify as a member of the LGBTQ+ community.

recD0VDY2OZn9cTMr.name: GMHC
recD0VDY2OZn9cTMr.description: As the world’s first HIV/AIDS service organization, GMHC is working to end the AIDS epidemic and uplift the lives of all affected.

recVjbIafzytYIbLE.name: God's Love We Deliver
recVjbIafzytYIbLE.description: The mission of God’s Love We Deliver is to improve the health and well-being of people living with HIV/AIDS, cancer and other serious illnesses by alleviating hunger and malnutrition. We prepare and deliver nutritious, high-quality meals to people who, because of their illness, are unable to provide or prepare meals for themselves. We also provide illness-specific nutrition education and counseling to our clients, families, care providers and other service organizations. All of our services are provided free to clients without regard to income.

recOgoobH1wpOdE6k.name: Goddard Riverside
recOgoobH1wpOdE6k.description: A multi-service organization based on the Upper West Side, with roots in the settlement house movement. Resources include supportive housing, mental health services, youth enrichment programs, and community arts initiatives.

recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.name: Good Shepherd Services
recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.description: A multi-service organization working to expand opportunities for children, youth, and families in historically underinvested NYC communities through academic enrichment, supportive housing, career development, and family well-being services.

reczijceHgFZEBcsF.name: Grand St. Settlement
reczijceHgFZEBcsF.description: Grand St. Settlement provides vital services to families throughout the Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn. Programs include early childhood programs, youth after school and summer camp programs, senior housing, job training, benefits assistance, senior programs, and services for the whole family.

rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.name: Gratis Grove
rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.description: Gratis Grove maintains the Woodside Community Fridge at 41-26 58th St and organizes free store events and fresh food distros in Woodside, Queens.

recJXLPJ1fAiF726y.name: Greenwich House
recJXLPJ1fAiF726y.description: At its founding in the early 1900s, Greenwich House was tasked with helping immigrants settle into their new lives in New York City. Greenwich House remains a "first responder" resource for the underserved, helping children who have survived physical and sexual abuse and domestic violence, supporting adults working to overcome addiction, providing psychiatric and case management services to seniors who suffer from mental health challenges related to aging and providing cultural enrichment to New Yorkers of all ages and backgrounds. The mission of Greenwich House is to help individuals and families lead more fulfilling lives by offering social and health services, cultural and educational programs and opportunities for civic involvement to New Yorkers of all ages and backgrounds.

recwVmrMdwJY0WEk1.name: H.E.A.L.T.H for Youths
recwVmrMdwJY0WEk1.description:
H.E.A.L.T.H for Youths, Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit formed for the charitable and educational purposes of assisting youth. We strive to combat community deterioration and juvenile delinquency, improve the quality of education, health care and life-skills training offered to adolescence and young adults.

To further this purpose, we collaborate with non-profit organizations, schools, and community organizations to offer adolescence and young adults various programs and workshops in the areas of physical health, mental health, social/cultural education and life-skills.

recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.name: Harm Reduction Coalition
recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.description: Harm Reduction Coalition was founded in 1993 and incorporated in 1994 by a working group of needle exchange providers, advocates and drug users. Today, we are strengthened by an extensive and diverse network of allies who challenge the persistent stigma faced by people who use drugs and advocate for policy and public health reform.

recQgfLX22mKHmVEP.name: Health Leads
recQgfLX22mKHmVEP.description: Work locally and nationally to move racial health equity progress more effectively – in partnership and with communities taking the lead. We innovate and spread promising practices on the most complex health equity challenges of today –  from maternal health to housing to food security.

recK7rCT3Atvzj6Cf.name: Heart of Dinner
recK7rCT3Atvzj6Cf.description: Heart of Dinner addresses food insecurity, social isolation, and loneliness among Asian American seniors who live in under-resourced and underinvested communities. We do this by delivering care packages of nutritious prepared lunchboxes and fresh produce every Wednesday, lovingly paired with a handwritten and illustrated letter in their native language to bring warmth and comfort.

recUgIYFXOUuccnRg.name: Hebrew Free Loan Society NYC
recUgIYFXOUuccnRg.description: The Hebrew Free Loan Society advances economic stability and opportunity for lower income New Yorkers within and beyond the Jewish community by making safe, affordable interest-free loans.

rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.name: Heights and Hills
rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.description: Providing programs and services to support older Brooklynites to age in place as vital members of their communities.

reco3fOTxEWWHuP5j.name: Hell's Kitchen Community Cupboard
reco3fOTxEWWHuP5j.description: Free food pantry in Hell's Kitchen, open 24/7. Take what you need, leave what you can.

recTCv9sU5pt2448j.name: Henry Street Settlement
recTCv9sU5pt2448j.description:
Henry Street Settlement, a 127 year old social service agency situated on Manhattan’s Lower East Side. Each year, Henry Street opens doors of opportunity for more than 50,0000 LES residents and other New Yorkers through social services, arts, and health care programs.
 
Today, our community’s most vulnerable residents--individuals and families experiencing homelessness, unemployed and low-income workers, undocumented workers, seniors, and public housing residents--are at high risk of being severely affected by COVID-19. Henry Street has a long history of building trust and working with these residents and is able to pivot in real-time to offer solutions that address their needs during times of turbulence—including serving as a community first responder during major crises such as the 1918 flu pandemic, the Great Depression, 9/11, and Hurricane Sandy. In the midst of today’s pandemic, Henry Street is leveraging our capacity and community embeddedness to serve on the front lines once again.

rec4aLDskvPdFx8B1.name: Her Justice
rec4aLDskvPdFx8B1.description: Her Justice stands with women living in poverty in New York City by recruiting and mentoring volunteer lawyers to provide free legal help to address individual and systemic legal barriers. Her Justice pair pro bono attorneys with women who have legal needs in the areas of family, matrimonial and immigration law.

recW5tGM3telgpMVu.name: Hetrick-Martin Institute for LGBTQ+ Youth
recW5tGM3telgpMVu.description: HMI supports and empowers LGBTQIA+ youth by creating affirming spaces, providing vital services, and advocating for systems that allow young people to live healthy, authentic lives. Through direct support, community partnership, and education, we work to reduce harm, build resilience, and expand opportunity for queer and trans youth.

recVm9bMvU5vfjvXv.name: Hot Bread Kitchen
recVm9bMvU5vfjvXv.description: Since 2008, Hot Bread Kitchen has empowered New Yorkers who face barriers to economic opportunities through transformative careers in New York City’s food industry. We offer job skills training, customized job placement, food entrepreneurship programs, and an ecosystem of wraparound support, opening pathways to economic mobility for New Yorkers across the five boroughs who face barriers to employment. A growing and opportunity-rich sector, the food industry provides a desired and accessible entry point to the workforce for the communities we serve.

rec2gHjlzfUPZyBTs.name: Hour Children
rec2gHjlzfUPZyBTs.description: Hour Children supports women and their families during and after incarceration and equips them with the tools to build their futures by providing housing, childcare, job training, and mental health services

recnsQIYlt2P2LfXc.name: Housing Court Answers
recnsQIYlt2P2LfXc.description: Housing Court Answers educates and empowers NYC tenants and small homeowners through Information Tables and a hotline.

rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.name: Hunger Free America
rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.description: Hunger Free America (with the Hunger Free NYC affiliate) helps low-income New Yorkers by helping them access SNAP benefits, distributing guides on food and assistance, and advocating for food security policies.

recGfSfy1OiaZdXXY.name: Hunter College NYC Food Policy Center
recGfSfy1OiaZdXXY.description: Hunter College New York City Food Policy Center.

reczz8dmaa0sHOhKi.name: Hunter NYPIRG
reczz8dmaa0sHOhKi.description:
The New York Public Interest Research Group’s unique mission is to give students an array of extracurricular activities and opportunities to participate in important public policy discussions, through which they can learn a wide range of valuable skills, contributing to a well-rounded educational experience.

Students across the state at NYPIRG’s campus chapters, including NYPIRG’s Student Board of Directors, have made tangible contributions on the issues of civic engagement, higher education funding, consumer rights, environmental protection, mass transit, and homelessness. Since 1973, NYPIRG has provided a unique service of supplementary learning and provided countless students with an enriching and rewarding experience.

recl1b4wqGw1HdN5l.name: Identity House
recl1b4wqGw1HdN5l.description:
Identity House provides peer counseling in NYC – for LGBTQ+ folks, by LGBTQ+ folks. We run a walk-in center for one-time individual sessions, short-term counseling, and support groups focused on issues around sexual orientation and gender identity & expression, including alienation, relationships, and family.

Our volunteer peer counselors use active listening and share their own stories to help deepen perspectives on LGBTQ+ identity, address challenges, and develop community.

recdNcict1HRXlJbu.name: If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice
recdNcict1HRXlJbu.description: A national network of lawyers, law students, legal professionals, and movement organizers who are working to make reproductive freedom a reality for all.

rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.name: Immigrant Defense Project
rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.description: The Immigrant Defense Projects fights to end the current era of unprecedented mass criminalization, detention and deportation through a multipronged strategy including advocacy, litigation, legal advice and training, community defense, grassroots alliances, and strategic communications.

recuJfKaPUf0X9Nmt.name: Immigrants Rising
recuJfKaPUf0X9Nmt.description: A California-based group striving to increase educational access and opportunities for undocumented people through institutional policy changes and direct support to empower educators, students, and communities.

reckrD9pzaBFDYTZ3.name: Immigration Equality
reckrD9pzaBFDYTZ3.description: Immigration Equality is a non-profit organization that provides free information and legal services to people who have been persecuted on account of their sexual orientation, gender identity or HIV status or have other LGBTQ-related immigration issues.

rec2fCP9AJfCTF6Sk.name: In the Rooms
rec2fCP9AJfCTF6Sk.description: With a 12-step approach, aims to "give recovering addicts a place to meet and socialize when they’re not in face-to-face meetings. This basic concept has grown into a global online community with over 650,000 members who share their strength and experience with one another daily. Through live meetings, discussion groups, and all the other tools In the Rooms has to offer, people from around the world connect with one another and help each other along their recovery journeys."

rec3rpoNrZX7gFYHE.name: IncludeNYC
rec3rpoNrZX7gFYHE.description: INCLUDEnyc connects young people with disabilities to resources and helps them thrive in school, at work, and in the community.

recJx8PzBGDCM6I3m.name: Independent Consumer Advocacy Network
recJx8PzBGDCM6I3m.description: CSS is an informed, independent, and unwavering voice for positive action on behalf of more than 3 million low-income New Yorkers. CSS draws on a 170-year history of excellence in addressing the root causes of economic disparity through research, advocacy, litigation, and innovative program models that strengthen and benefit all New Yorkers. CSS is committed to the goal of increasing access to quality, affordable health coverage as a means to improve individual and community health outcomes, promote health equity, and alleviate barriers to employment.

recCV0V2u4rtoMlDb.name: Informed Immigrant
recCV0V2u4rtoMlDb.description: A digital hub and offline network offering up-to-date and accessible information and guidance for the undocumented immigrant community, compiled by immigrant rights leaders, service providers, lawyers, and technologists from across the country.

recAPyPWEI9VlGEQG.name: Invisible Hands Delivery
recAPyPWEI9VlGEQG.description: We are a group of thousands of volunteers delivering groceries and prescriptions to those most at-risk during this crisis, including the elderly, immunocompromised, sick, and disabled.

recWinJTyQd8PMBq3.name: Jewish Community Council of the Rockaway Peninsula
recWinJTyQd8PMBq3.description: JCCRP provides support for those in need through a wide range of comprehensive social services. The dedicated team is committed to serving everyone with compassion, integrity, and respect. All services are offered at no cost, making help accessible to all.

recGkx7ATJk7Jhs1J.name: Jamaica Center Distro (JCD)
recGkx7ATJk7Jhs1J.description:
Jamaica Center Distro is a leftist organization primarily structured around a food distribution in Jamaica Queens (corner of Parson Blvd and Jamaica Ave) every 2nd Saturday of the month. Food is free and available to all who want as long as supplies last. 

We hope to build the food distro into further acts of mutual aid, political organizing, and other forms of community based care.

We are working through Astoria Food Pantry because of our shared values and for ease of attaining funding.

recTtvii6mJWrofJg.name: Justia
recTtvii6mJWrofJg.description: Justia provides open and free access to the law, and a platform for the legal community to share their knowledge.

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Legal Aid Society
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description: Civil, Criminal Defense, Juvenile Rights, and Pro Bono practices in and out of the courtroom to defend clients and dismantle the hidden, systemic barriers that can prevent them from thriving in New York City. Provide comprehensive services, support, and advocacy that protect rights, keep families and communities together, and in many cases, saves lives.

recaupMLWXNkBJASc.name: Legal Services NYC
recaupMLWXNkBJASc.description: Legal Services NYC’s (LSNYC) mission is to fight poverty and seek racial, social, and economic justice for low-income New Yorkers. We help New Yorkers obtain the basic necessities of life, including housing, economic security, family and immigration stability, education, health care. We challenge systemic injustices that trap people in poverty.

recnaUuZBGUt7LqKS.name: Lemontree
recnaUuZBGUt7LqKS.description: We work with thousands of resources designed to help neighbors like you. Our team will match you with the options that make sense for you, whether that’s the closest food pantry, or a community kitchen open on Sundays.

rec0nCqutJdkYS2L7.name: LGBT National Help Center
rec0nCqutJdkYS2L7.description: Free & confidential peer support, information, and local resources through national hotlines and online programs staffed by volunteers who identify as part of the LGBTQIA+ family.

recF5VNzqAQ1WwePq.name: Liberation-Based Therapy
recF5VNzqAQ1WwePq.description: Liberation-Based Therapy is psychotherapeutic group practice supports mental health and wellness through the lens of liberation-based healing practices. The work offered is emotionally-focused, culturally affirming with a strengths-based perspective. We work with individuals, couples, families and groups in New York and New Jersey.

rectBt4wFpHYEsGnO.name: Lower East Side Food Not Bombs
rectBt4wFpHYEsGnO.description: Independently organized distribution of vegan/vegetarian meals, made of soon to expire food from local grocery stores, bakeries, food co-ops, farmer's markets, etc.

recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.name: Make the Road New York (MRNY)
recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.description: Make the Road New York builds the power of immigrant and working class communities to achieve dignity and justice.

recwgsKrHaWCYeUez.name: Mayor's Alliance for NYC's Animals
recwgsKrHaWCYeUez.description: A 501(c)(3) non-profit charity that accomplished a mission to make New York City a no-kill city and currently serves as a capacity-builder, connector, and hub for NYC animal welfare.

rechNE648bhCkjdHp.name: MDSG
rechNE648bhCkjdHp.description: MDSG is a bi weekly support group for people with mental health disorders or family/friend with mental health disorders. These groups now meet over zoom (wed & friday 7:30-9:15) and include Under 30, Bipolar, Friends and Family, Unipolar and I believe a LGTBQ+ group is underway.

recVbkL7FrTEZEcIk.name: Mentor A Promise
recVbkL7FrTEZEcIk.description: A nonprofit organization helping NYC youths and families break the cycle of homelessness by illuminating paths to education and success.

recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.name: Met Council on Housing
recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.description: The Metropolitan Council on Housing is a tenants’ rights membership organization made up of New York City tenants who believe in our motto of “housing for people, not profit.” We serve the one million NYC households who are rent stabilized or regulated, particularly those who most vulnerable to displacement – working class and low-income New Yorkers.

recGZkfFWaQ5qkRz6.name: MinKwon Center for Community Action
recGZkfFWaQ5qkRz6.description: The MinKwon Center for Community Action empowers the Korean American community and works with the wider Asian Pacific American (APA) and immigrant communities to achieve economic and social justice for all.

recXpQoushkEzeeGl.name: Mobilization for Justice
recXpQoushkEzeeGl.description: Mobilization for Justice, offers free legal assistance to low-income New Yorkers throughout New York City to resolve legal problems in the areas of housing; foreclosure; civil, disability and aging rights; bankruptcy, tax, consumer, employment, government benefits, immigration, and kinship care. Through these services we prevent homelessness, help seniors and people with disabilities live independently, stabilize families, maintain and increase income, and address racial disparities.

recqtNhvHuOhvzQA7.name: Modest Needs
recqtNhvHuOhvzQA7.description: Modest Needs is a tax-exempt charity where you can make small, emergency grants to low-income workers who're at risk of slipping into poverty and for whom no other source of immediate help is available.

reczvGWr85qo2tbv2.name: Mount Sinai Adolescent Health Center
reczvGWr85qo2tbv2.description: The Mount Sinai Adolescent Health Center in New York City offers a comprehensive array of medical, mental health, and reproductive health services, plus prevention education to young people aged 10 to 26 with no cost to patients.

recxIjHMkfwvjEj1m.name: Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI)

recGy1FOdnxoNLt7H.description: NHSQ CDC is a non-profit organization that helps low-to-moderate income families continue to live in Queens by sustainably achieving or preserving homeownership. for direct giving in a time of widespread financial insecurity.

recbrzpM04X4I3Mie.description: The Right to Counsel NYC Coalition led the campaign to make it a right for tenants to have a lawyer when facing eviction in NYC, inspiring a Right to Counsel movement across the country. recyzMGD05H7Kq61Z.name: Rise
recyzMGD05H7Kq61Z.description: Founded in 2005 and led by parents impacted by the child welfare system, Rise believes that parents have the answers for their families and communities. recawgSdcfEiFBIpo.name: RiseBoro Community Partnership
recawgSdcfEiFBIpo.description: Since 1973, we’ve offered services designed to support every generation and meet the needs of communities. Our unique model of holistic community revitalization works by developing neighborhood assets, like affordable housing, to create the foundation for a more vibrant and diverse community. recQhDRkVPzbBbav8.name: Rising Ground
recQhDRkVPzbBbav8.description: Rising Ground is a human services organization that supports individuals and families in New York City and lower Westchester County.

rect1prBH0YaVuQFe.name: South Asian Council for Social Services
rect1prBH0YaVuQFe.description: A multi-service, multilingual community-based organization with the mission to empower and integrate underserved South Asians and other immigrants into the civic and economic life of New York. recHOPdxMW9U3y2OT.description: A network of organizers, healers, artists, community leaders, and every day people coming together to deliver food and supplies, provide financial solidarity, offer emotional support, and connect people to their neighbors in St. Louis.

recDNCEa91hUR5rax.description: SAMHSA runs a 24-hour mental health hotline that provides education, support, and connections to treatment.

recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.description: We are neighbors in Queens, acting collectively to address community needs and take care of each other.

rec795pUt3p8Ho2ZF.description: NYC S&P is a grassroots prison abolition organization, dedicated to freeing criminalized survivors of gender violence held in prisons in New York. recPTgHSVcMWueXIL.name: The 155th Street Fridge

recmAx54SyWVSuX46.description: Sustainable Economies Law Center cultivates a new legal landscape that supports community resilience and grassroots economic empowerment. recylwtaZfYuNiFM7.name: The Center - The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual & Transgender Community Center

recV6gQsVrahEnhTO.description: The Coalition for Immigrant Freedom, also known as the Northern Manhattan Coalition for Immigrant Rights (NMCIR), is a non-profit organization founded in 1982 to educate, defend and protect the rights of immigrants. recVHiId4WdbLUrIa.description: The agency is a source of support for working parents and their children. They offer access to social services, childcare, and recreational activities including a daycare program, after-school care, special needs programs, youth, and adult programs

recyUJmxPLCM2vWVj.name: The HOPE Program
recyUJmxPLCM2vWVj.description: The HOPE Program empowers New Yorkers to build sustainable futures through comprehensive training, jobs, advancement, and lifelong career support. Our comprehensive approach combines training, adult basic education, industry certifications, work wellness services, internships, HSE prep, and job placement with long-term support.

recPercPqHTFMPWg3.name: The HopeLine
recPercPqHTFMPWg3.description: Bronx-based organization that works with families to become more self-sufficient and upwardly mobile. Services include a food pantry, a diaper center, SNAP enrollment, tax preparation, financial literacy workshops, and referral services.

recsC4ydBdD0fdjto.name: The Jewish Board of Family and Children’s Services
recsC4ydBdD0fdjto.description: The Jewish Board provides services to all New Yorkers in a number of areas including behavioral and physical health, family, employment, education, and housing.

recNM4g5QrmvQ9hF2.name: The Medicare Rights Center
recNM4g5QrmvQ9hF2.description: A non-profit organization that helps people solve Medicare related issues

recoKgtKGCZzRJ0Ew.name: The Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs
recoKgtKGCZzRJ0Ew.description: The Mayor's Office of Immigration Affairs's mission is to promote the well-being of immigrant communities in the City of New York.

recm0VO5FQSVVsTFe.name: The National Child Traumatic Stress Network
recm0VO5FQSVVsTFe.description: The National Child Traumatic Stress Network (NCTSN) was created by Congress in 2000 as part of the Children’s Health Act to raise the standard of care and increase access to services for children and families who experience or witness traumatic events. The NCTSN is administered by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) and coordinated by the UCLA-Duke University National Center for Child Traumatic Stress (NCCTS).

recxeuCdqZsMFb7Ea.name: The Retreat
recxeuCdqZsMFb7Ea.description: The Retreat provides safety, shelter and support for children, adults and families affected by domestic violence, abuse, sexual assault and human trafficking.

recEdPM9EUnKCfqKV.name: The Samaritans of New York
recEdPM9EUnKCfqKV.description: The Samaritans of New York, a member of the international humanitarian network, is a community-based organization devoted to suicide prevention in the NYC-Metropolitan area. Samaritans has been providing crisis response, prevention planning, professional development and training, suicide survivor support groups and related services to the people of the region for over 30 years.

recClVSLNBGB9N9Gc.name: The Trevor Project
recClVSLNBGB9N9Gc.description: Founded in 1998 by the creators of the Academy Award®-winning short film TREVOR, The Trevor Project is the leading national organization providing crisis intervention and suicide prevention services to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer & questioning (LGBTQ) young people under 25.

recBYGWua9aKnlEry.name: The Young Center
recBYGWua9aKnlEry.description: The Young Center is a champion for the best interests of children who arrive in the United States on their own, from all corners of the world. We serve as trusted allies for these children while they are in deportation proceedings, advocating for their best interests, and standing for the creation of a dedicated children’s immigrant justice system that ensures the safety and well-being of every child.

recrZzCIdgLxP26Q4.name: Tompkins Distro
recrZzCIdgLxP26Q4.description: Tompkins Distro organizes a free mutual aid food distribution in Tompkins Square Park every Saturday at 11am for asylum seekers, unhoused neighbors, and all in need.

recuMBjTe0b3n3Kpq.name: Trans Lifeline
recuMBjTe0b3n3Kpq.description: Trans Lifeline is a grassroots hotline and microgrants 501(c)(3) non-profit organization offering direct emotional and financial support to trans people in crisis – for the trans community, by the trans community.

recC2mgB67TAaxgNE.name: Transportation Alternatives
recC2mgB67TAaxgNE.description: Transportation Alternatives uses a combination of neighborhood-level grassroots organizing and citywide advocacy to push for changes in public policy, street design, enforcement, and resource allocation that transform our city’s streets for the better.

recas8VzgGzRzb1Zj.name: Trans Needle Exchange
recas8VzgGzRzb1Zj.description: A non-profit mail-based service providing free HRT needle supplies for trans folk who cannot access or afford their own.

reckuwuA4zsYEcYeR.name: UHAB (Urban Homesteading Assistance Board)
reckuwuA4zsYEcYeR.description: UHAB creates and sustains community-controlled affordable housing. We support over 1,200 affordable HDFC co-ops, a type of cooperative low-income homeownership. We also build power with rent-stabilized tenants in Eastern Brooklyn.

recvcjFQuiB7DdUrs.name: United Federation of Teachers
recvcjFQuiB7DdUrs.description: The UFT, which represents nearly 200,000 members, is the sole bargaining agent for most of the non-supervisory educators who work in the New York City public schools.

recQvzUArnjG7l5Fy.name: University Settlement
recQvzUArnjG7l5Fy.description: Focuses on creating partnerships and connection with communities in the Lower East Side and Brooklyn in order to improve peoples lives thought a diverse array of programs.

recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.name: Unlock NYC
recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.description: At Unlock NYC, we equip voucher holders with the paper trail, voice, and connections to create accountability when they’re facing housing discrimination. Through our direct services, data analysis, and advocacy, we’re creating a power shift where landlords and brokers fear the social and financial costs of discriminating against voucher holders.

rec4RGp1bPNWosJq7.name: US Department of Health and Human Services
rec4RGp1bPNWosJq7.description: U.S. government department focused on health and wellbeing, and advancing the sciences underlying medicine, public health, and social services.

rec6sXk7ng8dmt9Vt.name: Urban Upbound
rec6sXk7ng8dmt9Vt.description: Urban Upbound serves public housing residents and other low-income New Yorkers to break cycles of poverty.

recyl4z4wfIW9ix5l.name: Violence Intervention Program (VIP Mujeres)
recyl4z4wfIW9ix5l.description: Our mission is to lead Latina victims of domestic violence to safety, empower them to live free of violence and reach and sustain their full potential. We pursue our mission by raising community awareness, engaging in activism and providing culturally competent services.

recVMjdII9dMKJU5f.name: USDA Food and Nutrition Service
recVMjdII9dMKJU5f.description: USDA’s Food and Nutrition Service has 16 government nutrition assistance programs to work toward children, income eligible individuals, and families having access to healthy, safe, and affordable foods that promote optimal health and well-being.

recQBLS0vZ7IQIfoK.name: Virtual NA
recQBLS0vZ7IQIfoK.description: Virtual NA is a globally based collaborative service resource whose primary purpose is to provide a meeting search for both Online and Phone line meetings of Narcotics Anonymous hosted from different countries around the world.

reclRoz7ouIR0Fgp0.name: VOCAL-NY
reclRoz7ouIR0Fgp0.description: Voices Of Community Activists & Leaders (VOCAL-NY) is a statewide grassroots membership organization that builds power among low-income people affected by HIV/AIDS, the drug war, mass incarceration, and homelessness in order to create healthy and just communities. We accomplish this through community organizing, leadership development, advocacy, direct services, participatory research and direct action.

recOd8L5i1nuyOwOD.name: Washington Square Park Mutual Aid
recOd8L5i1nuyOwOD.description: Mutual Aid in Washington Square Park every Friday from 5 - 8 PM collecting and distributing free food, clothes, and supplies

recgVbYwhnUi8DIwe.name: West Side Campaign Against Hunger
recgVbYwhnUi8DIwe.description: West Side Campaign Against Hunger is on a mission to alleviate hunger by ensuring that all New Yorkers have access with dignity to a choice of healthy food and supportive services.

recvAb6TSyXLFOdbz.name: Womankind
recvAb6TSyXLFOdbz.description: Womankind works with survivors of gender-based violence to rise above trauma and build a path to healing. We bring critical resources and deep cultural competency to help survivors of all ages in Asian communities find refuge, recovery, and renewal from domestic violence, human trafficking, and sexual violence.

recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.name: Women’s Housing and Economic Development Corporation (WHEDco)
recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.description: WHEDco’s mission is to give the South Bronx access to all the resources that create thriving neighborhoods: from high-quality early education and after-school programs, to fresh, healthy food, cultural programming, and economic opportunity.

reczLMvOYciMOt2Gn.name: YM & YWHA of Inwood and Washington Heights
reczLMvOYciMOt2Gn.description:
Established in 1917, the YM&YWHA of Washington Heights & Inwood (the Y) is a  not-for-profit human services organization in Northern Manhattan. We provide educational, recreational, and social services and programs that focus on improving the quality of life for New Yorkers from preschool to seniors. During the current pandemic, we have launched a robust virtual program -- The Y @ Home -- with many fun and meaningful online events.

We are also providing help with access to food, mental health counseling, emergency cash assistance, guidance with benefit enrollment, medical care, or other emergency services at this time through our website.

recnqi4Jj9YpkQiB8.name: Young Black Queens NYC
recnqi4Jj9YpkQiB8.description: YBQ.NYC is a mutual aid collective + sisterhood dedicated to uplifting Black women and strengthening Black communities through care, joy, empowerment, & sharing of resources. Through distribution events & community-centered initiatives, we work to create spaces where Black women feel supported, protected, & free.

recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.name: Free Abortion Clinic and Pill Directory
recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.description: Search the database to find verified abortion clinics near you that keeps your information private.

recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.name: Legal Issues in Mutual Aid Operations: A Preliminary Guide
recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.description: A June 2020 article by Michael Haber about legal issues that impact groups engaged in mutual aid, with a focus on New York. It gives legal information on topics including: risk of liability; questions around governance and incorporation; safety policies, liability waivers, and insurance; banking and mutual aid; funding mutual aid and taxation of mutual aid; crowdfunding regulations; and food storage and safety rules.

recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.name: New York State Order of Parentage Guide
recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.description:
A DIY guide to help non-gestational parents using donor sperm petition Family Court to obtain legal parentage rights to protect their family following the NY Child-Parent Security Act (CPSA). This includes the steps to submit a court petition, example templates, and additional information and resources.

Compiled by a parent who successfully petitioned the court using this process.

recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.name: Mutual Aid 101 Toolkit #WeGotOurBlock
recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.description: This toolkit includes step by step instructions for how you can build your own mutual aid network. Created in 2020 at the height of the COVID-19 crisis, but contains useful information for other contexts.

recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.name: Refuse to Be Numb: A Free Support Space in Times of Unrest (Not Therapy)
recO88HEJjqZIJ6KY.description: Join a free virtual support group for NY residents processing political unrest and emotional overwhelm. For adults in NY | Not therapy | Respectful space only | Max 12 people

recokocub8pcyBRe7.name: Writing Workshops for Teens
recokocub8pcyBRe7.description: Writing workshops for youth, with free and low-cost options for families who meet income requirements.

recunoQJauUDoRSvh.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
recunoQJauUDoRSvh.description: Call 988. The Lifeline provides 24/7, free and confidential support for people in distress, prevention and crisis resources for you or your loved ones, and best practices for professionals. Also available via text and online chat.

recy56hKmj3I2uMKE.name: AARP Social Isolation Prevention for Adults 65 and Older
recy56hKmj3I2uMKE.description: Take the AARP three-minute assessment to help you understand your risk level for social isolation and receive helpful information and local recommendations based on your results.

recuSrT9qiFt7lZjn.name: Directory to find access, information, and funding to people seeking an abortion
recuSrT9qiFt7lZjn.description: A national searchable directory to find abortion care providers, funding, and support. Does not provide direct referrals or actual procedures, but instead connects you to information about places that do.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recoYwsn1j3CAGbx1.name: Support Groups for Gender-Expansive Children, Transgender Adolescents, Their Families & Communities
recoYwsn1j3CAGbx1.description: The Gender & Family Project (GFP) of the Ackerman Institute offers a variety of support groups in addition to other services. There are groups for children 5-10 years old, for gender expansive and transgender adolescents, for siblings, and for caregivers and family members. Support groups take place once per month with no obligation to attend consecutively, and they cost from $5 up on a sliding scale.

recfoDie8avd23BgB.name: Free Store in Greenpoint
recfoDie8avd23BgB.description: Free store open 24/7 at the corner of Adelphi St and Greene Ave in Greenpoint. Anyone can come anytime to donate or take items from the store’s shelves, from clothing and linens to toys and home decor. Please no large items, make sure things are suitable for redistribution, and help keep things tidy.

rec313dYFp06SP6Ir.name: Helpline For Education-Related Information in New York City
rec313dYFp06SP6Ir.description:
Call (866) 427-6033 Monday through Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm to speak to an education specialist. 

Advocates for Children’s Jill Chaifetz Education Helpline is a resource for information and guidance on all education-related matters in New York City. If your child is struggling in school or experiencing school discrimination of any kind, specialists will assess the problem and provide free assistance, ranging from information you can use to advocate on your own, or assign you an education specialist or attorney to work with you directly.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Activities for Individuals with a Traumatic Brain Injury
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
Comprehensive range of interest-based activities. Participants have the opportunity to engage in social groups, art projects, community volunteering, cooking and financial literacy. Provide comprehensive psychological services that address the unique needs of each person supported. 

Apply through email form: https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Residential Services and Support for People with Developmental Disabilities
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
To apply, contact the referral and information center. Call 212-780-4491 to get more information on making referrals or contact the Referral and Information Center online at https://www.ahrcnyc.org/ric/contact/. 

Residential supports fall under three models:
1. Individualized Residential Alternatives (IRAs)
Supervised IRAs are traditional family-style group homes, providing 24-hour staff support and supervision for up to 14 residents.
Supportive IRAs provide need-based supports and services for those who are living in their own homes or apartments but do not require 24-hour staff support and supervision. Supportive IRAs are limited to 3 or fewer residents.
2. Supervised Apartments
3. Residential settings for people who are medically fragile (with 24/7 Nursing Care) AHRC NYC operates two residences for aging individuals who require full-time nursing oversight.  Support staff are comprised of nurse practitioners and supervising registered nurses, who are on-site 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  Residents also have access to speech, physical, and occupational therapies as needed, as well as a day habilitation program operated within the residence.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Education for families of people with developmental disabilities to obtain services
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
AHRC's Family Educational Series includes workshops and informational sessions for families in obtaining services for their family member with a developmental disability and help families to come with challenges that may arise as they care for their loved one. 

Join AHRC's mailing list to receive invitation to their education workshops via email.

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Respite Opportunities for Family Members and Caretakers: Out and In-Home
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
Contact AHRC's referral and information center to connect with their staff and make a referral for yourself or someone you know.

AHRC provides respite opportunities for family members and caretakers of a person with a developmental disability who lives in the home with them.  The need for respite care can range from a caretaker needing to go food shopping, visiting the doctor, or simply relaxing. AHRC's respite care ranges from a period of a few hours to a few weeks, also offering programs that engage people with disabilities after their day programs, on weekends and during vacations.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Day Habilitation Program for People with Developmental Disabilities
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
NYC’s Day Habilitation programs are tailored to adults 18 and over. Programs provide diverse services that cater to people’s individual preferences.​

Day Habilitation is available to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities who are over the age of 18, in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx. 

To enroll the participant must have Medicaid, Care manager enrolled in CCO (Care Coordination Organization).
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Home Health Care Services and Assistance
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
A range of home health care services to meet the needs of eligible persons with and without disabilities, including home health aides, personal care aides / companions, nursing, physical, occupational and speech therapies, respiratory therapy, and social work services

To contact or ask questions about home health care services, contact the referral and information center, available 24/7, or visit the office Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

Fill out the form to contact the referral and information center. Additionally, they accept fee-for-service and long-term care insurance.

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: In-Home Respite for People With Developmental Disabilities
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
For people with developmental disabilities who reside at home with their families, AHRC New York City provides out-of-home and in-home respite opportunities, ranging from a period of a few hours to a few days.

To apply for respite services, contact the referral and information center on AHRCNYC's website.

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: College Programs for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description: Individuals aged 21 or older with intellectual disabilities who reside in New York City can apply for admission to the Melissa Riggio Higher Education Program at the participating CUNY campus in their borough of residence. To be eligible, applicants must qualify for services from the New York State Office for People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD), be enrolled in the Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver, and have a Care Manager from a Care Coordination Organization.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.name: Clinical Supports, Services, & Treatment for Children and Adults
recrhgJq7FbA5DbLS.description:
Provides services on a sliding scale fee basis. Services include: Psychological Assessment, Psychosocial Evaluation, Sexuality Assessment, and Additional Assessments, to assess and assist in determining needs for individuals with developmental disabilities. Additional clinical services include: Psychotherapy/Counseling, Crisis Intervention Services, Recovery Supports and Wellness Services, OT, PT, & Speech Services, Nutritional Counseling, and Family Reimbursement.

Clinical Services are available to people with developmental disabilities, ages 5 and up. Additionally, certain support services can be provided to other family members who do not themselves have a disability.

Clinics are in Manhattan (Financial District) and the Bronx (Fordham Heights) and open by appointment only; please no walk-ins.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recW3vFbZbIvzEC2u.name: 24-hour Drop-In Center offering free medical and mental health care and services to homeless LGBTQ+ youth
recW3vFbZbIvzEC2u.description: Call 212.206.0574 ext. 100, or stop by the Drop-In Center at 307 West 38th Street, 3rd floor New York, NY 10018. Open for new intakes Monday-Friday from 8 AM - 8 PM and Saturday and Sunday from 10 AM - 6 PM, except closed Wed 2-4pm.

recHqRU1DmWPrbPwU.name: Free Virtual Support Groups for Eating Disorders
recHqRU1DmWPrbPwU.description:
Communities of Healing virtual support groups are free and open to anyone with an eating disorder. Each group is facilitated by someone who has personally experienced and recovered from an eating disorder. Groups meet weekly to share with and learn from other people who understand what it means to fight for recovery.

To join, fill out the information request form, and ANAD will contact you with more information and joining info.

recjq0Erm2OKrLI0A.name: Pet Loss Support Program
recjq0Erm2OKrLI0A.description: Free virtual support groups for those who have lost a pet in the last 12 months. Meetings are approximately twice a month on Zoom on Tuesday starting at 6:15 pm. Space is limited and first-come, first-served. Registration closes at 4pm on the day before the meeting.

recFO3eanXRxLNqfC.name: Emergency Financial Aid for Professional Visual Artists
recFO3eanXRxLNqfC.description:
The Artists’ Fellowship provides one-time emergency aid to professional visual fine artists and their families in times of sickness, natural disaster, bereavement or unexpected extreme hardship that can be documented through paid or unpaid invoices, bills, or contracts.

Eligibility: please note that “Professional” is defined as those visual artists who make their livelihood through sales as reported on a Schedule C with a U.S. Federal tax return. An active exhibition history is also an important part of documenting “professional.”

recWFYn4vI938wy4I.name: Community Services for Tenants, Immigrants, Seniors, and Youth
recWFYn4vI938wy4I.description: Asian Americans for Equality (AAFE) works with clients one-on-one to ensure their rights to safe and decent housing, to secure and extend appropriate government housing subsidies, to make sure they have access to social support programs, such as food stamps and Medicaid, and to provide assistance with immigration matters.  Counselors are available in storefront offices in Manhattan’s Chinatown; the Lower East Side; Flushing, Queens; and Sunset Park, Brooklyn. Contact by phone or fill out contact form on website.

recbrcvt8yqA49Vye.name: Free Food Distribution Mondays and Saturdays in Astoria
recbrcvt8yqA49Vye.description: Pick up a pre-packaged bag of groceries Mondays 8am-10:30am and Saturdays 1-1:30pm. No sign-up, id, or name required. 25-82 Steinway St in Queens.

recuSDgzVpby0ENhD.name: Youth Mentoring for Children Ages 7 to 16
recuSDgzVpby0ENhD.description: Children between the ages of 7 and 16 will be matched with an adult mentor who will offer friendship, guidance, and advice. There's no cost for mentoring, but each child should be committed to this program for 8 hours per month, for a minimum of one year. Visit the website to enroll.

recLSY40H84utldr0.name: Sliding-scale Bicycles and Bike Repair in Brooklyn
recLSY40H84utldr0.description: If you are in need of a complete bicycle, email bikeplantnyc@gmail.com with your height, what you will use the bike for, and your phone number, and you will be added to our list. If you're in need of repair, bring your bike to the shop during our regular business hours.

recfitL8bHuVFce1E.name: Black Trans Travel Fund
recfitL8bHuVFce1E.description: The Black Trans Travel Fund helps to cover monetary expenses for Black transgender women in New York and New Jersey states in need of money for transportation, in order for them to be able to self-determine, and have access to, their safest transportation options. There is a bi-weekly cap of 75 applicants.

recXjBhHbC5nHPkFa.name: Mental Health Resource Directory for Black/African-American Communities
recXjBhHbC5nHPkFa.description: A Directory of Mental Health Providers and Programs serving the African-American community.

rec8OGa4st1MmTDMX.name: Affordable Housing through Breaking Ground
rec8OGa4st1MmTDMX.description:
Offers affordable housing for low-income working professionals and the formerly homeless, some of whom live with HIV/AIDS, mental illness, or physical disabilities.

Call the Central Intake Hotline at 800-324-7055 to request an application, or fill one out online. Fill out a separate and specific application for each building to which you are applying.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recE53a1ezu67cLdy.name: Volunteer Program for New Yorkers
recE53a1ezu67cLdy.description: On the website, Bright Light offers volunteering events throughout the city.

recc1FQnVFaWhApRF.name: My Bronx Impact: Find Free or Cost-based Resources by Zipcode
recc1FQnVFaWhApRF.description: Enter your zip code to find free or cost-based local resources like medical care, food, job training, education, and more.

rec26EuDhn1FxJ64F.name: Free Food Distribution, Clothing, & Community Care on Saturdays in the Bronx
rec26EuDhn1FxJ64F.description: Pick up free produce, hot food, clothing, books, and toiletries every Saturday from 1 - 2pm @ St. Mary's Park 601 E. 149th St, Bronx, NY.

recJxHBjPmT9VuOHH.name: BronxWorks Economic and Social Services and Programs
recJxHBjPmT9VuOHH.description:
BronxWorks provides a range of programs and services including help obtaining health insurance; family and adult shelter; eviction and prevention services; foster care prevention, senior homelessness prevention; chronic illness and health management such as HIV/AIDS; education and youth development; SNAP assistance; food pantry;  immigration and legal services; and workforce development. 

Auxiliary aids and services are available upon request to individuals with disabilities.
TTY: 1-800-662-1220
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recJxHBjPmT9VuOHH.name: BronxWorks Programs for Elementary School Aged Children
recJxHBjPmT9VuOHH.description: Access directory of childcare resources including after-school programs, summer camps, and community-center based recreational and education activities for children 5-12 years old operated by BronxWorks.

recEYMTRC6Lxureqr.name: Free Meal Distribution Saturdays in Greenpoint
recEYMTRC6Lxureqr.description: Visit Greenpoint Community Kitchen at 155 Milton Street every Saturday from 11 am to 1 pm to receive hot meals and coffee. Meals can be enjoyed on-site or taken to go. Bread is packaged and available to take home as well.

recFHspmkE9TIcHMH.name: Brooklyn Grange CSA
recFHspmkE9TIcHMH.description:
A Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program that offers a sliding scale for locally grown vegetables. Runs for 22 weeks from late May through October.

Accepts SNAP benefits.

recWcn476NI7NzN1d.name: Community Economic Development Program for Community Groups and Nonprofit Legal Support
recWcn476NI7NzN1d.description: Attorneys provide both short-term legal advice and ongoing representation for community groups and nonprofits, offering a full range of transactional services including corporate formation, contract drafting and negotiation, employment matters, commercial leases, regulatory issues, and real estate transactions.

recWcn476NI7NzN1d.name: Legal services for individuals who face domestic violence
recWcn476NI7NzN1d.description: For domestic violence-related inquiries, please reach out to our office by phone or email and request the Domestic Violence Program. In-person meetings are by appointment only.

recflaIlMFsuvtR5c.name: Community Fridge at Hart and Myrtle
recflaIlMFsuvtR5c.description: Community fridge in Bushwick always accepting food donations 24 hours /day. DIY don't ask just go.

recz1NRo0D0wDVR3Z.name: Bushwick Free Store
recz1NRo0D0wDVR3Z.description: Tuesdays, 3-5pm at Maria Hernandez Park: Suydam St and Knickerbocker Ave. Share what you have, take what you need. Check Facebook or Instagram (@bushwickfreestore) for weekly updates and/or cancellations for weather.

recAxHiXvrLCcAp4F.name: Digital Resource Map by and for Transgender, Non-binary and/or Intersex People
recAxHiXvrLCcAp4F.description:
TransAtlas is a map-based guide to community organizations, agencies and spaces across the 5 boroughs of New York City, made by and for people of transgender, non-binary and/or intersex experience. 

Drawn from Callen-Lorde’s Transgender Resource guide and Surgeon guide, and made by a team of transgender folks, TransAtlas maps hundreds of services and organizations across the 5 boroughs where TGNB folks can find trans-competent and friendly resources to help with anything from primary care to hair removal, addiction support, and religious institutions. You can search through dozens of surgeons, therapists, dentists, lawyers, barbers, case managers and more.

recAxHiXvrLCcAp4F.name: Free Health Clinic for Sex Workers
recAxHiXvrLCcAp4F.description: Sex workers can call 212-271-8134 to schedule an appointment with COIN, a free healthcare program through Callen-Lorde for sex workers in an affirming, supportive environment. The clinic offers primary medical care, sexual health, HIV treatment & prevention, transgender health, GYN care, and more.

recD3CAhL0o96i8Rz.name: Exchange childcare with people you trust
recD3CAhL0o96i8Rz.description: Carefully is a free playdate and childcare exchange platform to build a network of parents you know and trust to share care, redefining the traditional 'care circle' model for the digital age (available for iOS and Android).

reckZYwAn3JZiAnKE.name: Free & Low-Cost Primary Care, Behavioral Health Services, Dental and Podiatry for the Homeless
reckZYwAn3JZiAnKE.description: Call (833) 423-4273 24/7 for information or a same-day appointment. Find walk-in locations on the website. You will be treated regardless of your ability to pay.

reciUOlX02yLKXRmX.name: CaringKind Helpline for Support with Dementia
reciUOlX02yLKXRmX.description: Call (646) 744-2900, fill out an online form, or email helpline@caringkindnyc.org for resources for caregivers of those diagnosed with Alzheimer's or dementia. Social workers can meet, by appointment, in person in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and The Bronx or by phone and email.

recd8ZNooek5wd9A9.name: Catholic Charities Help Line
recd8ZNooek5wd9A9.description: Call 888-744-7900 8:30am-5:30pm to get connected with Catholic Charities' wide range of services for New Yorkers of all religions, including food pantries, housing resources, and services for immigrants and refugees.

recRKQYFQKrutb2mx.name: Free Benefits Counseling for People with Disabilities
recRKQYFQKrutb2mx.description:
Call 1-844-862-7930 to reach counselors available 9 am until 5 pm, Monday through Friday. You can also request to be contacted by a counselor by filling out the form at https://www.cidny.org/getnyconnects
Support includes SNAP, Unemployment Insurance, Social Security, Medicaid, etc. for people with disabilities and older adults; help getting connected with various resources including food, toiletries, mental health, etc.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recskYN3dX3ihAjvg.name: From Shelter to Apartment: A Guide to New York City's Department of Homeless Services
recskYN3dX3ihAjvg.description: A foldout poster (English and Spanish versions) that breaks down people’s rights in homeless shelters and the different programs available to help them leave shelter and find affordable permanent housing. It also provides resources on other services shelter residents may have access to, like transportation benefits and storage grants, and what to do when your rights have been violated.

recTIADSzGfLDIUtq.name: CERF+ Emergency Assistance
recTIADSzGfLDIUtq.description:
CERF+ offers $3,000 Emergency Relief Grants to craft artists with a public-facing practice who experienced a recent and substantially disruptive emergency or disaster. Applicants must be at least 18 years old and reside or work in the United States or U.S. territories.

To apply, visit the website and complete the online application with supporting documentation.

reclTnqdWY9q23Wd8.name: Affordable Housing Resources and Tenant Advocacy
reclTnqdWY9q23Wd8.description: Chhaya is a HUD-certified counseling agency providing pre-purchase and post-purchase counseling services, as well as a tenant advocacy team. Needs addressed include: First-time Homebuyer Program, Foreclosure Prevention Program, and Tenant Advocacy Program

reclTnqdWY9q23Wd8.name: Financial Counseling and Workshops for South Asian Small Businesses
reclTnqdWY9q23Wd8.description:
To apply for services, fill out survey on the website. 

Chhaya is a community development corporation with the mission to build the power, housing stability, and economic well-being of South Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities. Chhaya executes this work by providing free direct services in the areas of housing counseling and homeownership, asset building and financial empowerment, policy and advocacy, and community organizing.

recj9iQOiAMcMmegW.name: Benefits Access Counseling and Enrollment Assistance
recj9iQOiAMcMmegW.description: Provides free counseling on entitlements, health insurance, financial guidance, social services, and legal services. On-site health insurance and SNAP enrollment are available. These services are open to the community for people of all ages, with or without children. Locations in Jamaica, NY and Flushing, NY.

recGjnlGleFTbhNct.name: Children Wellbeing Programs for Underserved New Yorkers
recGjnlGleFTbhNct.description: Call to connect to educational, health and wellbeing, and family support resources. Visit the website to search for specific programs by age group and neighborhood. Program areas are focused on academic and social-emotional learning, health and nutrition, and support to parents and guardians.

recncdYVfJuUJV41k.name: Legal Support Services for LGBTQIA, Polyamorous, and Underserved Families
recncdYVfJuUJV41k.description: Call (732) 639-1657 or fill out an intake form on the website to access legal support services, including: name and gender marker changes on identity documents, will and estate documents, known donor agreements, family formation such as cohabitation and coparenting agreements, parentage petitions, and nuptial agreements. Requires documentation of residency and income.

recaDqyn9nuzioOTu.name: Free Meals in Park Slope
recaDqyn9nuzioOTu.description: CHiPS serves breakfast (9-10:30am) and lunch (11:30am-1pm) Monday-Saturday at 200 4th Avenue in Park Slope Brooklyn. Meals are available to anyone who is in need.

recCi455NHfiqT2Gm.name: Job Application Platform for People with Disabilities & Chronic Illness
recCi455NHfiqT2Gm.description: A job application platform specifically designed to connect folks with disabilities and chronic illness to employers who have committed to offering flexibility and support of these employees' personal needs to ensure their success in the job.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

reck5Wn4TDV78EAFU.name: NYC Affordable Housing Lottery Application Process Info and Training
reck5Wn4TDV78EAFU.description:
Go to website to book an in-person appointment at one of multiple locations to receive one-on-one application assistance, including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy, needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

There are also a range of referrals available for additional services such as credit repair, tenants rights, legal support, immigrant rights, ELA, job training, domestic abuse assistance, and more.

reck5Wn4TDV78EAFU.name: Housing Workshops to Learn About Housing Lottery Application Process
reck5Wn4TDV78EAFU.description:
See website for locations to book an appointment. Receive step-by-step advice on what to expect through the housing lottery application process, including a review of the application and other required documents; information on financial empowerment and managing credit and debt portfolios; and additional support through the selection and interview process. 

In addition to larger workshops, CUFFH also provides One-on-One Application Assistance including information and training on the necessary interview skills and financial literacy needed to obtain an affordable housing unit.

recKab2y2r2icqh9U.name: Free Legal Hotline for People with Limited Income
recKab2y2r2icqh9U.description:
Call the Legal Hotline or fill out an online application to connect with staff attorneys who assist callers of limited income on a range of civil legal issues, including matrimonial and family law, housing law, domestic violence, bankruptcy, and debt collection and benefits. Our staff includes bilingual attorneys who speak English and Spanish, and we can accept calls in any language through interpreting services.

The Hotline is open Monday through Thursday from 10am-12pm and 2pm-4pm, and Friday from 9am-12pm.

rec7QDun6J2YmNBsg.name: City Harvest Map of Food Distribution Sites
rec7QDun6J2YmNBsg.description: Map of locations that are currently distributing free food throughout NYC. Location sites include soup kitchens, food pantries, City Harvest Mobile Markets, and City Harvest Community Partner Distributions.

recPTUBNSANTcPMuH.name: Free Gender-Affirming Clothes and Resources - Marsha's Closet
recPTUBNSANTcPMuH.description: Give what you can, take what you need! Pull up every 3rd Monday of the month on 135th and St Nick to drop off/pick up Clothing Donations for our queer and unhoused community in Harlem & beyond.

receiFlcUx1MtCHqW.name: Emergency Meal Delivery for Homebound Elderly New Yorkers
receiFlcUx1MtCHqW.description:
This resource is only accessible through a case management agency. If eligible, enter address to get the phone number for the Case Management Agency of your district. The Case Management Agency will guide you through the process of getting meals. 

To qualify, you:
-Must be 60 years of age or older
-Must be physically or mentally incapacitated and in need of some assistance
-Must be unable to prepare nutritious meals or have no one to do so for you
-Must be able to live safely at home if services are provided for you
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.name: Community Fridge in Brooklyn
recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.description: Access the Classon Community Fridge, a refrigerator and pantry, on the street outside of Dean Crossfit that is open 24/7 for both food donations and food access.

recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.name: Free Monthly Grocery Distribution in Brooklyn
recQCxwPPXZFjvE2Q.description: Grocery distributions at 641 Classon Avenue on the second Monday of each month.

recDvVLiCoHx3BOiD.name: Free Phone Caption Service
recDvVLiCoHx3BOiD.description: Caption service for phone calls. Can be used on internet phones, landlines, and mobile phones. You must be a U.S. resident and certify that your hearing loss inhibits your ability to use the phone.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.name: Eviction Prevention Program
recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.description: People in danger of being evicted can call the Eviction Prevention Hotline at 888-850-2712 on Wednesday mornings beginning at 9:30 am. Appointments are limited and first-come, first-serve. To qualify for a one-time payment of $1000 (on average), you must be in court, have a signed court stipulation, and have future ability to pay your ongoing rent.

recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.name: Crisis Intervention Hotline for Shelter Services
recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.description: Call the Crisis Intervention Emergency Hotline at 1-888-358-2384 with questions about accessing shelter or other services, including if you have been denied access to shelter. Leave a detailed message, including your phone number. The Intervention Program is based in NYC and only able to respond to questions regarding NYC services.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.name: Know Your Rights Resources on Shelters and Housing
recJw0RVILZDmauPQ.description: Informative guides on the NYC shelter system, disability accommodations, and finding permanent housing.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recpgQyo3TpdNpYTz.name: Mercadito Solidario Project
recpgQyo3TpdNpYTz.description: Community initiative that provides fresh and free food to the TransGNB community every Wednesday 3-6pm at 3763 83rd St Suite #1B, Jackson Heights, NY 11372.

recJIcDMIK2kiMELF.name: Food Distribution Tuesdays in Washington Square Park
recJIcDMIK2kiMELF.description: Weekly distro of food, hot coffee, and more on Tuesdays 12:30pm-2:30pm in Washington Square Park across from Holley Statue. Take what you want, leave what you can.

recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.name: Free Food and Clothing Distribution in Brooklyn
recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.description: Tuesdays, 12-2pm at 1046 Broadway in Brooklyn. Free food distribution available to anyone.

recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.name: Community Fridge Finder
recuFG6Mq0hDM43E4.description: Find community fridges containing free food near you. Go to the site and click the "Find A Fridge" button for the full map and list of fridges. Update the status of fridges in your own community.

recVUclk7MmyiDLn9.name: Hotline for Substance Use Disorder and Mental Health Care Resources
recVUclk7MmyiDLn9.description: Call 888-614-5400 for assistance in accessing treatment and insurance coverage for substance use disorders and mental health treatment. Hotline is confidential.

recwXdBrHgvhJqFeK.name: Free Assistance with Health Insurance, Healthcare, Medicaid
recwXdBrHgvhJqFeK.description: Call (888) 614-5400 or email cha@cssny.org for assistance with understanding how to use your health insurance, resolving medical billing and debt issues, disputing coverage denials and eligibility determinations, getting the most from your coverage (get prior authorizations, access specialists, and out-of-network services when needed), accessing affordable health care services, and hospital and prescription financial assistance program.

recAOFy8P6p8w4iDR.name: Free weekly grocery distribution in Bedstuy and Long Island
recAOFy8P6p8w4iDR.description:
Find a Food Share location and weekly date/time on the website: Bedstuy, Farmingville, Wyandanch, Hemstead, and Huntington

Anyone can come to a Community Solidarity Food Share and get most, if not all, of the groceries they need for the week. Each Food Share is a free supermarket where community members share instead of pay for what they need. There are no prerequisites, there is no paperwork, all are welcome and everyone will be helped. We also share clothing, books, toys, school supplies, and other necessities.

rec3ggacriV3pGPhH.name: How to Start and Run a Bulk Buying Club With Your Community
rec3ggacriV3pGPhH.description:
A guide to starting and running a bulk food buying club. This covers: food sourcing, organizing members, running operation, and logistics. Also includes information about different student-run
bulk buying clubs in the CoFED network to learn about their strategies.

recUOyGsehgZmmcuS.name: Covenant House crisis shelter and resources for youth experiencing homelessness
recUOyGsehgZmmcuS.description: Any youth 16-21 and their minor child(ren) may go 24/7 to Covenant House NY crisis shelter at 460 West 41st near the Port Authority Bus Terminal. They have beds, clothes, food, showers, laundry, chargers, toiletries, and holistic services. No referral and no immigration status restrictions. States they are a LGBTQ safe space.
