rec7TI5mVAAPmwlh4.name: Crisis Text line: Free text-based crisis counseling
rec7TI5mVAAPmwlh4.description: In the United States, text HOME to 741741 at anytime 24/7 to reach a volunteer crisis counselor.

recDiMg0pHyatodZn.name: Call or Chat to Get Connected with Social Services and Support in NYC
recDiMg0pHyatodZn.description:
CUCS Benefit Centers provide individuals and families with coordinated access to resources, including income support, health insurance enrollment, legal support, and financial coaching. 

Email or call to make an in-person appointment.

rec7Ozef2M8fhqHXU.name: Services for immigration questions, or help with citizenship, green card, DACA, or TPS applications
rec7Ozef2M8fhqHXU.description:
Fill out the form on the website to request a call back. Get help with green card renewals, citizenship, DACA, and TPS. Includes support for checking eligibility for benefits, help with forms, and guidance on required documents and process. Priority to CUNY students, but all New Yorkers are supported.

Text: 929-334-3784
Call: 646-664-9400 or 212-652-2071

recdDyGw23pYlUquA.name: Tuition free access to youth dance company (ages 7-18)
recdDyGw23pYlUquA.description: Opportunity for year-long free dance and performance training for youth ages 7-18 at Dancewave (located in Gowanus, Brooklyn). Scholarship application available on the website. Please email school@dancewave.org with questions.

recEirZnAFofbZsoq.name: Organizing and Providing Critical Services to Low-Wage Migrant Workers
recEirZnAFofbZsoq.description: Email or call (212) 564-6057 to reach Riya Ortiz at Damayan Migrant Workers Association, a Filipino migrant workers cooperative. Helps labor trafficking survivors develop escape plans, secure emergency housing and financial assistance, access social and legal services, find employment, and facilitate family reunifications. Also engages in community and organizing for fair labor standards and labor trafficking.

recAai2YaRhnnO1mi.name: Free mental health resources for BIPOC in NYC
recAai2YaRhnnO1mi.description: Visit the website to get connected to free resources and tools including "Find Me a Therapist", a Black Mental Health Resource Packet, and a Black Mental Health Provider Database.

recUyJ2OfpWgDioJ3.name: Free Dating Abuse and Domestic Violence Services and Resources for Youth Under 24 Years Old
recUyJ2OfpWgDioJ3.description: For youth experiencing dating abuse and domestic violence, access the helpline by calling 800-214-4150 or texting 646-535-DAY1 (3291). Access prevention and know-your-rights resources on the website.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recg8RNoOjGSGRKyg.name: Drive Change
recg8RNoOjGSGRKyg.description:
Drive Change runs an 3-month paid fellowship for formerly incarcerated youth ages 18-25 that focuses on hospitality/restaurant industry training and professional development. Apply online.

To apply, you must be between 18-25, and prove you have 8th grade or higher math and reading level (TABE, GED/TASC or HS DIPLOMA preferred but not necessary).

rec3g1OG4UVRpKGMN.name: Domestic Violence Help
rec3g1OG4UVRpKGMN.description: Call 212-568-6616 9am-5pm to access individual counseling, shelter services or help obtaining an order of protection.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recKN0wWKnaLi6THO.name: Free Virtual Tutoring for NYC Public School Students
recKN0wWKnaLi6THO.description: EduMate NYC provides free virtual tutoring from volunteer college students for K-12 students enrolled in the NYC public school system. Priority will be given to students who are on free and reduced-price meal programs. Our tutoring covers all traditional school subjects, standardized test prep, and the college application process!

recMwIaNp1bFoPqm4.name: Paid Culinary Job Training Program
recMwIaNp1bFoPqm4.description:
Fill out application on the website to apply for a free 11-week culinary training program that pays its trainees full time minimum wage. Available for asylum seekers, refugees, and trafficking survivors who have come to the U.S. within the past five years. Offer a chef’s knife and a full uniform, free of cost, to every student.

This program is specifically catered towards people who arrived in the US within five years that were seeking asylum. Must be able to legally work in the US.

reczOXbRyW8IwldSN.name: Entertainment Community Fund Emergency Financial Assistance & List of Additional Funds
reczOXbRyW8IwldSN.description: Emergency Financial Assistance is available to eligible performing arts and entertainment professionals in times of unexpected critical need and to assist towards basic living expenses such as health care, housing and utilities to prevent eviction or shut-offs. Multiple funds in the entertainment industries are available to apply to, covering a variety of eligibility restrictions.

receyKSu1Fg1xB5s6.name: Episcopal Actors Guild Fund for Performers in Financial Crisis
receyKSu1Fg1xB5s6.description: You must live in one of the five NYC boroughs and have an established career working as a performer for at least five consecutive years. Call (212)-685-2927 if you think you may be eligible for the program. EAG's programs and services focus primarily on sustaining and supporting the careers of working performers. At the heart of EAG's charitable outreach is the EARP. Through this program, we give grants to qualified performers in financial crisis regardless of religion, race, national origin or ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental ability, political ideology/affiliations, or language. Through EARP we address critical issues like eviction, housing court stipulations, utility shutoffs, emergency medical and dental costs, and sustenance needs like food and transportation.

rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.name: Free Food Distribution Sundays in Tompkins Square Park
rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.description: Free food distribution Sundays, 12-2pm in the SW corner of Tompkins Square park at Ave A and East 7th St.

rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.name: Free Food Distribution Sundays in Lower Manhattan
rec6ljATc3TnoKXAe.description: Free food distribution Sundays, 12-2pm at the NE corner of Houston and LaGuardia Place.

recBB7h77e9niD19C.name: Get Someone to Accompany You During an ICE Checkin Date
recBB7h77e9niD19C.description: Got an upcoming ICE check-in date? Fill out the form linked on the website with your name, email, and ICE check-in date, and Families for Freedom staff will reach out to accompany you during the process.

recfUWygymsr0l522.name: Community Fridge in Ridgewood
recfUWygymsr0l522.description: Visit the community fridge at 586 Seneca Ave in Ridgewood. There is free food distribution for those in need every Friday at 5pm.

recuz5P52xiJZOlAK.name: Crisis Toolkit
recuz5P52xiJZOlAK.description: An assortment of resources that may provide perspective, comfort, and/or tools that could be of assistance to people experiencing various sorts of tough times. Includes links to informational guides, online peer support, and more.

recIPF1mALNR5kMIf.name: Find a Food Pantry Map
recIPF1mALNR5kMIf.description:
Visit the link to view a map of food banks operating in New York City. 

NOTE: Hours vary - call ahead to confirm when a food bank will be open.

recaFoKbv5zeTWnqN.name: Financial Support for Black Transgender People
recaFoKbv5zeTWnqN.description:
A Black, trans-led collective that curates parties to fundraise money to help Black transgender people pay for their rent, gender-affirming surgeries, smaller co-pays for medicines/doctor’s visits, and travel assistance. Visit website to view currently available applications and to apply for assistance programs. 

Only open to Black transgender people. Application through website. Depending on services, social media access might be necessary.

reci4hOr3GsyP8TK3.name: Free Clinic Directory
reci4hOr3GsyP8TK3.description: Free Clinic Directory is a directory of medical and dental clinics and community health centers that can help low-income and uninsured people by offering free and discounted rates for medical and/or dental care. Search by location, name, or phone number.

recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.name: Free Rapid PCR Testing in Brooklyn
recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.description:
Periodic free Rapid PCR tests for COVID, Flu A + B, and RSV. If you are positive for any of them, G-REBELS will provide you with a care kit and discuss support services so you can focus on rest and recovery. 

Tests, kits, and support services are completely free of charge to community members, but are limited to the uninsured to prioritize those who need it most. 

Find upcoming appointment times and locations on Instagram or the sign-up form.

recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.name: Peer-to-Peer Food Distribution in Brooklyn
recmMa6pMvg6FAo8B.description: Sign-up for peer-to-peer food distribution using the online form, and G-REBELS will match people who can offer assistance with people who need assistance. Both parties will receive an email with the other person's contact information, and they can connect directly. Mutual aid might look like: cooking and delivering food to their doorstep, arranging for grocery delivery, or meeting somewhere with purchased food items.

rec4gUhmL3kofpo9c.name: Crisis Shelter for Women Survivors of Domestic Violence with Disabilities
rec4gUhmL3kofpo9c.description: Freedom House is a safe, confidential and fully accessible shelter that offers private living spaces of various sizes to accommodate both singles and larger families. They are also equipped to serve all survivors and their children with disabilities including (but not limited to) wheelchair users, people who are D/deaf or hard of hearing and blind or visually impaired. Call (212) 400-6470 for more information and availability or email info@bflnyc.org.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recFExVAL1FofyRBh.name: Mentoring and Advocacy for Disadvantaged Girls, Femmes, and Gender-Expansive Youth
recFExVAL1FofyRBh.description: Call 347-918-8723 Monday-Friday 10am-6pm or email info@girlvow.org for mentoring and other support such as advocacy.

recD0VDY2OZn9cTMr.name: Gay Men’s Health Crisis (GMHC) Hotline
recD0VDY2OZn9cTMr.description: Call 1-800-243-7692 for a safe space to discuss a wide range of concerns. They provide information about topics such as HIV/AIDS, STDs, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), sexual health, and resources such as testing, healthcare, benefits, and counseling.

recVjbIafzytYIbLE.name: Free meal delivery for people with severe or chronic illness
recVjbIafzytYIbLE.description:
If you or someone you know is living with a severe or chronic illness and having trouble shopping or cooking, visit our website to confirm eligibility and apply for free, medically-tailored meals delivered to your door.

To be eligible, you must be living with a serious illness and have an ADL (Activities of Daily Living) limitation that prevents you from shopping or cooking for yourself which must be verified by a healthcare provider. Application forms and supporting documentation are available on the website and can be submitted electronically or mailed.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recOgoobH1wpOdE6k.name: Benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and other services
recOgoobH1wpOdE6k.description: Call 212-234-3481 on weekdays to make an appointment for the Resource Center, which provides benefits screenings, financial counseling, legal consultation, and support services for individuals and families.

recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.name: Safe Homes Project - Domestic Violence Programs
recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.description:
24-Hour Hotline 718-499-2151

Good Shepherd Services’ Safe Homes Project provides an array of free services, which include a hotline, counseling, safety-planning, as well as a 20-bed shelter for survivors and their children. It also provides targeted services for special populations, including Spanish-speakers, youth, and LGBTQ survivors of partner violence.

All services are offered in both English and Spanish.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.name: Social Service Support at Community Benefits Assistance Centers - Brownsville
recmIRiDxg9NqB06M.description:
Walk-in Tuesdays: 10am-3:30pm or call the office.

Community Benefits Assistance (CBA) provides individuals and families with hands-on assistance in applying for public benefits. At our centers, we offer easy access to public services in one place, connecting people to the resources to attain higher education, jobs, and financial stability, legal counseling, help with financial planning, immigration services and referrals to other community-based organizations, as needed.

reczijceHgFZEBcsF.name: Benefits assistance, senior and youth programs, and family services
reczijceHgFZEBcsF.description: Connect with Grand St. Settlement to access financial resources, opportunities for education, counseling, training, and support. Services include one-on-one appointments with Grand St. Settlement staff for financial and insurance support, access to job training and placement programs, and assistance in connecting with and navigating social services. They also offer early childhood and youth programs and services.

rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.name: Woodside Community Fridge
rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.description: Access or drop off free food at the Woodside Community fridge at 41-26 58th St in Woodside, Queens.

rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.name: Free Vegetable Distribution Sundays in Queens
rec9ngMxjXddSXsiZ.description: Free veggie distro every Sunday, ~2:30pm at Roosevelt Ave & 58th St in Woodside, Queens until November 2026.

recJXLPJ1fAiF726y.name: Help for Seniors Accessing Benefits & Support
recJXLPJ1fAiF726y.description: Call to make an appointment or find out about a regularly scheduled social work clinics. Connect with case managers for help to access benefits, including medical, financial, housing, and other needs; and get references for legal care and mental health care. Or enroll in the Daily Money Management program to help seniors with day-to-day financial tasks.

recwVmrMdwJY0WEk1.name: Workshops and Programming for Youth
recwVmrMdwJY0WEk1.description: A calendar of workshops and programming for youth in their late teens to early 20s with the goal of improving the quality of education, health care and life-skills training for underserved adolescents and young adults.

recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.name: Pregnancy and Substance Use -- Harm Reduction Toolkit
recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.description: Information for pregnant people and parents who use drugs, as well as their support network and service providers. Includes general tips for maintaining healthy pregnancies while using substances and for accessing quality care.

recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.name: National Harm Reduction Coalition Resources
recHcJ3hGUFuf7PfH.description: A collection of resources for harm reduction, offering information about sites for safe syringes and Narcan access, as well as toolkits, fact sheets, and training materials.

recQgfLX22mKHmVEP.name: Doula Access and Care for Black and Low Income Patients
recQgfLX22mKHmVEP.description: A reimbursement service that covers doula care under Medicaid. For New Yorkers who seek support through pregnancy and post partum.

recK7rCT3Atvzj6Cf.name: Free Food Delivery for East Asian Elders throughout NYC
recK7rCT3Atvzj6Cf.description:
Deliver weekly hot lunches, fresh produce, and bulk ingredients to East Asian elders while supporting local small businesses.

Fill out the form to join the waitlist. During the next onboarding cycle, they will review your eligibility for receiving Heart of Dinner care packages for free. The criteria:

1. Be a local NYC Asian American person aged 60 or above.
2. Have a gross monthly income as a single elderly at or below $1,869; or have a gross monthly income as an elderly couple at or below $2,518.
3. Unable to prepare meals because of the lack of money to purchase food, inability to shop or cook, or lack of facilities.
4. Isolated due to lack of family, friend or neighbor support.

recUgIYFXOUuccnRg.name: Interest Free Loans for New Yorkers Seeking Immediate Financial Help
recUgIYFXOUuccnRg.description: Hebrew Free Loan Society offers interest free loans for needs such as medical, addiction treatment, higher education, vocational training, and housing. Applicants must be defined as low to moderate income as a household. A government id is required.

rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.name: Services to support older adults in Brooklyn
rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.description: Call 718-596-8789 to access case management and caregiver services for older adults living in Brooklyn. Services support aging in place and can assist with meal prep, grocery shopping, housekeeping and other chores.

rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.name: Case Management Program for Older Adults in Brooklyn
rec6rIg8CQ6OIEJRP.description: Case management program to help adults over the age of 60 in Brooklyn stay in their homes and communities as they age. Email info@heightsandhills.org to learn more and schedule a home visit.

reco3fOTxEWWHuP5j.name: Community Cupboard in Hell's Kitchen
reco3fOTxEWWHuP5j.description: Free food pantry in Hell's Kitchen, open 24/7. Take what you need, leave what you can.

recTCv9sU5pt2448j.name: Health insurance enrollment, benefits screening, legal services, financial services, parenting guidance, and other services
recTCv9sU5pt2448j.description: Call 212-471-2400 to make an appointment for Dale Jones Burch Neighborhood Center, located at 269 Henry Street on the Lower East Side. Services include health insurance enrollment, benefits screening, legal services, financial services, and parenting guidance.

rec4aLDskvPdFx8B1.name: Legal Information Guides for Family Law and Divorce Issues
rec4aLDskvPdFx8B1.description: Access guides designed to help when you need to go to Family or Supreme Court without an attorney. Provide answers to common questions about divorce, spousal support, orders of protection, child custody and visitation, and child support.

recW5tGM3telgpMVu.name: Online or in-person counseling, health screenings, and additional resources for LGBTQ+ youth ages 13-24
recW5tGM3telgpMVu.description: 1-on-1 counseling via video/phone/chat and group counseling for various needs. Must become a member to access services. Send an email or a text to join@hmi.org with your name and phone number (if you have one) and someone within the organization will contact you.

recVm9bMvU5vfjvXv.name: Food Career Training Program
recVm9bMvU5vfjvXv.description: Apply for this free program on the "career programs" page. This resource is available for women and nonbinary people over 18 who are looking to find a job in food and restaurant services. Must be able to actively take courses for 5 weeks.

rec2gHjlzfUPZyBTs.name: Support for mothers impacted by the criminal legal system
rec2gHjlzfUPZyBTs.description: Support services for mothers who have been incarcerated including food pantries, thrift shops, supportive housing, job training, educational opportunities, and programming for children and teens.

recnsQIYlt2P2LfXc.name: Housing Court Hotline
recnsQIYlt2P2LfXc.description: Call (212) 962-4795 Monday-Friday 9-5 for information about housing court procedures, landlord & tenant rules and regulations, enforcement of housing code violations, and referrals for free legal help and other community organizations.

rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.name: Find Food Assistance By Address
rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.description: Enter an address to find a directory of nearby food assistance resources, including pantries and meal programs.

rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.name: Benefits Access for SNAP and WIC
rec9S7a1fjAGYCgqF.description:
Call (646) 355-1475 to set up a free, confidential consultation for assistance applying for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program for Women, Infants and Children). Hunger Free NYC will go over income eligibility requirements, check to see that you qualify, and then help you gather necessary documents. They also help with the re-certification process. Service in additional languages is available:
Spanish: (347) 599-1510
Mandarin/Cantonese: (646) 935-3513 
Russian: (332) 600-5425

recGfSfy1OiaZdXXY.name: NYC Neighborhood Food Resource Guides by Hunter College
recGfSfy1OiaZdXXY.description: A comprehensive guide listing food resources organized by neighborhood form the Hunter College Food Policy Center.

reczz8dmaa0sHOhKi.name: Small Claims Court Action Center
reczz8dmaa0sHOhKi.description:
Get free help with consumer problems and complaints in small claims court, such as the purchase of defective goods, shoddy services, unreturned security deposits, property damage or falling victim to deceptive business practices. 
While the Action Centers don’t provide legal advice or courtroom representation, they can help you resolve consumer problems and boost your chances of success in the small claims courts and with collecting a judgment.

recl1b4wqGw1HdN5l.name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Peer Counseling Services: Walk-in clinic, short-term counseling, support groups
recl1b4wqGw1HdN5l.description:
Walk-in center open Wednesdays 7pm – 9pm and Saturdays 6pm – 8pm. We also offer virtual sessions by appointment on Sunday evenings. Free (or $25 donation /session for those who can afford id) and open to all adults struggling with questions about sexual orientation and gender identity & expression, including alienation, relationships, and family. 

Counselors can provide resource information and referrals to short-term peer counseling or professional therapists after the walk-in clinic session.

Find information about groups at https://identityhouse.org/groups/.

recdNcict1HRXlJbu.name: Repro Legal Helpline
recdNcict1HRXlJbu.description: Call 844.868.2812 or submit a query online for free, confidential legal information or advice about self-managed abortion, young people's access to abortion or judicial bypass, and referrals to local resources. Messages are checked Monday-Friday from 9am – 8pm ET and responded to within 2 business days.

rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.name: Know Your Rights Information, Legal Resources, and Trainings for Immigrant Communities
rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.description: Know Your Rights information, trainings, legal resources, and FAQs for communities impacted by ICE stops and raids.

rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.name: Criminal-Immigration Helpline
rec8elD6b77ACEhfD.description:
Immigrants and their loved ones who are affected by the criminal system, including immigrants who have been arrested, ticketed, or convicted of a crime: call the helpline for limited immigration legal advice and information, referrals for free immigration legal services, and referrals for private immigration attorneys. 

The helpline is not live. Leave a voicemail with your name and number at any time and a staff member or volunteer will contact you .

recuJfKaPUf0X9Nmt.name: Wellness Gatherings for Undocumented People
recuJfKaPUf0X9Nmt.description: Register for 6-week virtual Wellness Support Groups led by trained mental health providers or registered clinicians, designed to help undocumented people feel less alone and more understood.

reckrD9pzaBFDYTZ3.name: Legal Help for LGBTQ and HIV-Positive Immigrants
reckrD9pzaBFDYTZ3.description: Find resource guides on topics including asylum, detention, family reunification, and visas. If your question isn't answered, fill out an online form to set up an appointment with a legal expert.

rec2fCP9AJfCTF6Sk.name: Virtual Recovery Meetings
rec2fCP9AJfCTF6Sk.description: An aggregated calendar of online recovery meetings. Create an account with an email address to access live virtual meetings for both support and socialization. Listed meetings include Alcoholics Anonymous, Al-Anon, Narcotics Anonymous, Overeaters Anonymous, and Coronavirus Support groups.

rec3rpoNrZX7gFYHE.name: Help Line to Access Resources for Families of Children and Young Adults with Disabilities
rec3rpoNrZX7gFYHE.description:
IncludeNYC seeks to support families who have children with disabilities for people ages 0-26 years of age. Services include providing access to education, family advocacy, employment and will assist in gaining independent living status. Call the help line to gain access to resources.
Helpline:  call: 212-677-4660
                 text: 646-693-3175

Español: llame: 212-677-4668
                texto: 646-693-3175
                whatsapp: 212-858-0795

You do not need to have a disability diagnosis to call, and immigration status is not considered.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recJx8PzBGDCM6I3m.name: Healthcare Enrollment Help Hotline
recJx8PzBGDCM6I3m.description:
Call 844-614-8800 for assistance with enrolling in and using managed care plans that cover long term care or behavioral health services.
Services include one-on-one counseling about health insurance options by phone or live chat on their website.

recCV0V2u4rtoMlDb.name: Informational Guides for Immigrants
recCV0V2u4rtoMlDb.description: Find information and links to organizations covering topics including DACA, TPS, mental health, education, and employment for undocumented and other immigrants.

recAPyPWEI9VlGEQG.name: Free Grocery and Supply Delivery
recAPyPWEI9VlGEQG.description: Free grocery and supply delivery to elderly, disabled, and/or immunocompromised New Yorkers. Call (732) 639-1579 (open seven days a week) or fill out the form on the website to request a delivery.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recWinJTyQd8PMBq3.name: Benefits Enrollment Assistance and Case Management Services in the Rockaways
recWinJTyQd8PMBq3.description: Call to connect with services, including a large kosher food warehouse, Medicaid assistance, Medicare enrollment and troubleshooting, SNAP enrollment and troubleshooting, housing assistance, Holocaust survivor services, crisis intervention, support for single mother families, holiday programs and much more.

recGkx7ATJk7Jhs1J.name: Free Food Distribution Second Saturdays in Jamaica
recGkx7ATJk7Jhs1J.description: Free food and produce distribution at 12pm every 2nd Saturday of the month at the corner of Jamaica Ave and Parsons Blvd, outside of the old Jamaica Multiplex.

recTtvii6mJWrofJg.name: New York City Family Legal Aid & Pro Bono Services
recTtvii6mJWrofJg.description: A list of organizations offering family legal aid and pro bono services in New York City.

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Legal Aid Society Access to Benefits Helpline
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description: Call 888-663-6880 for the Legal Aid Society's Access to Benefits (A2B) Helpline, Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Interpreters are available for all languages.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Health and Disability Benefits support for People Living with HIV/AIDS
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description: Call the Legal Aid Society's HIV/AIDS Representation Project’s helpline at 718-579-8989 if you are a person living with HIV/AIDS and need assistance with a legal matter.

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: School & Student Rights Legal Support
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description:
If The Legal Aid Society represents you or your child in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can reach out to the attorney to be directed to help with education issues.

If you are not involved in a Family Court or Criminal Court case, you can ask for help with your child’s education needs by calling The Legal Aid’s Civil Access to Benefits helpline at 888-663-6880.

If your child needs representation for an upcoming Superintendent’s Suspension Hearing, please call our Suspension Hotline at 718-250-4510.

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Legal support for discrimination for people with conviction records
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description: The Worker Justice Project combats discrimination faced by workers with arrest or conviction records living in New York City. If you have been denied a job or a license because of your arrest or conviction record and you live in New York City, email the Worker Justice Project at WorkerJustice@legal-aid.org or call 888-663-6880 Monday through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Arrest and Policing - Contact a Criminal Defense Attorney
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description:
If you, or someone you know, has been arrested and you have questions about a pending criminal case, contact your attorney or call the Criminal Defense Office in your borough to find out how to get help.

Criminal Defense Offices:
Bronx: 718-579-3000
Brooklyn: 718-237-2000
Manhattan: 212-732-5000
Queens: 718-286-2000
Staten Island: 347-422-5333

Juvenile Trial Offices:
Bronx: 718-579-7900
Brooklyn: 718-237-3100
Manhattan: 212-312-2260
Queens: 718-298-8900
Staten Island: 347-422-5333

recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.name: Consumer Debt, Tax & Small Business Help
recOCYrJymwAlyBSW.description:
For help with new and existing small businesses and not-for-profit organizations or existing HDFCs contact the Community Development Project at 212-298-3340, CommunityDevProject@legal-aid.org, or reserve a spot in our virtual clinic by completing our online questionnaire.

Visit website to access forms and questionnaires.

recaupMLWXNkBJASc.name: Free Legal Support for New Yorkers
recaupMLWXNkBJASc.description:
Call 917-661-4500 for the Access Line to speak to an intake specialist in any language.

The website also includes FAQs for common legal questions including topics related to immigration and asylum, LGBTQ+ rights, health and disability rights, housing and foreclosure, and more.

recnaUuZBGUt7LqKS.name: Lemontree Food Helpline / La línea de ayuda alimentaria de Lemontree
recnaUuZBGUt7LqKS.description:
Need food? Submit a webform with your phone number to get help from a real person 10a-6p every day. We can help you find the closest food pantry, apply for SNAP, and more.
¿Necesitas comida? Llena un formulario en línea con tu número de teléfono para conectar con una persona verdadera 10a-6p cada día quien puede ayudarte a encontrar comida gratis, aplicar para SNAP, y más.

rec0nCqutJdkYS2L7.name: LGBT National Youth Hotline
rec0nCqutJdkYS2L7.description: Call 800.246.7743 for volunteer LGBTQIA+ youth peer support hotline. Visit website for hours and one-on-one chat and chatroom options.

recF5VNzqAQ1WwePq.name: Sliding Scale Therapy in NY
recF5VNzqAQ1WwePq.description: Request sliding scale therapy through Liberation-Based Therapy. LBT provides culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and liberation-centered therapy for individuals, couples, families, and groups. Services are primarily virtual, with limited in-person availability in New York City. Sliding scale options may be available based on financial need, therapist availability, and fit. Complete the appointment request form to get connected with the intake team.

rectBt4wFpHYEsGnO.name: Free Vegan Meal Distribution Sundays in the Lower East Side
rectBt4wFpHYEsGnO.description: Free vegan meals served every Sunday at 4:30pm inside the SW corner of Tompkins Square Park (E 7th st & Ave A).

recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.name: Improving Access to Healthcare for Immigrants
recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.description: Call (718) 418-7690. Make the Road New York works to guarantee equal rights, access, and improved healthcare for the 2.5 million New Yorkers with limited English proficiency. Provides one-on-one assistance with health insurance and food stamp enrollment, hospital bill negotiation, health system navigation, nutrition education and emergency food services, Community Health Worker training and services, and HIV testing referrals.

recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.name: English, Citizenship Prep, and Community Health Worker Training Classes
recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.description:
Complete the online form to apply to Make the Road adult education programs, including: 
- English classes for speakers of other languages 
- Citizenship preparation
- Community health worker training program (Brooklyn only)

For more information, call your preferred location in Bushwick, Jackson Heights, Port Richmond, Brentwood, or White Plains.

recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.name: Legal Assistance with Employment, Immigration, Housing and Benefits, and TGNCIQ Rights
recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.description:
Call a neighborhood community center to access legal support in the areas of employment, immigration law, housing and benefits, and TGNCIQ rights, helping to tackle crises like an impending eviction or an order of deportation.

Bushwick Brooklyn: (718) 418-7690
Jackson Heights, Queens: (718) 565-8500
Port Richmond: (718) 727-1222

recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.name: Free Downloadable Deportation Defense Manual
recCEf8HaOH8Jw80G.description: Read this to familiarize yourself with how to respond to ICE.  Broken into three sections: Know Your Rights, Rapid Response to Raids, and Deportation Defense.

recwgsKrHaWCYeUez.name: Guide to Reduced-Cost Veterinary Care
recwgsKrHaWCYeUez.description: An informational guide to programs offering financial assistance to help pay for veterinary care for your companion animals in the New York City area.

rechNE648bhCkjdHp.name: Mood Disorder Support Groups
rechNE648bhCkjdHp.description:
MDSG is a bi-weekly free support group network for people dealing with a mood disorder. Meetings are Wednesday and Friday 7:30-9:15 over zoom. Groups available include Bipolar, Unipolar, Under 30, and Friends and Family.

A donation is requested, but no one is turned away.

recVbkL7FrTEZEcIk.name: Mentors and Educators for Students in NYC Shelters
recVbkL7FrTEZEcIk.description: Register and enroll a student, 5-21 years of age, living in an NYC shelter with educational programs and tutors that can assist them in strengthening their academic skills and achieving their educational goals.

recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.name: Resources on Evictions and Housing Court
recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.description: Contains information on: finding a lawyer, holdover evictions, illegal evictions and lockouts, handling housing court without a lawyer, nonpayment of rent eviction cases, and eviction moratorium FAQs.

recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.name: Tenants’ Rights Telephone Hotline: 212-979-0611
recQqRsSE09OYlYAr.description:
Call the free Tenants' Rights Telephone Hotline at 212-979-0611 to ask questions about:
Getting repairs from negligent landlords, getting adequate heat in the winter months, dealing with the threat of eviction, questions about leases and lease renewals, and legal rent increases for rent-regulated apartments.

recGZkfFWaQ5qkRz6.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Immigrants
recGZkfFWaQ5qkRz6.description: Call the MinKwon Center at 718-460-5600 for help with benefits enrollment, setting up vaccination appointments, immigration services, food, medicine, and rental assistance.

recXpQoushkEzeeGl.name: Legal Advocacy and Services for Low-Income New Yorkers
recXpQoushkEzeeGl.description: Free legal assistance to low-income New Yorkers throughout New York City to resolve legal problems in the areas of housing; foreclosure; civil, disability and aging rights; bankruptcy, tax, consumer, employment, government benefits, immigration, and kinship care.

recqtNhvHuOhvzQA7.name: Self-Sufficiency Grants
recqtNhvHuOhvzQA7.description: Emergency grant funding to assist individuals and families who, because they are working and live just above the poverty level, are ineligible for most types of conventional social assistance. Grants are typically between $750 and $1250. Grants come through donors to the national non-profit charity organization Modest Needs.

reczvGWr85qo2tbv2.name: Free Healthcare for Ages 10-26, Including Primary Care
reczvGWr85qo2tbv2.description: Call (212) 423-3000 for free and confidential care for young people ages 10-26. Fundamental care for all patients includes primary care, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, social services, optical, health education and prescriptions, plus specialized services for LGBTQ young people, teen parents, young people living with HIV, and young people dealing with trauma.

recxIjHMkfwvjEj1m.name: Therapy and Advocacy for Survivors of Sexual Violence
recxIjHMkfwvjEj1m.description: Call 212-423-2140. Mount Sinai Sexual Assault and Violence Intervention Program (SAVI) works with survivors who have experienced sexual assault and intimate partner violence. Provide therapy support and advocate for the safety of clients. Located at East Harlem, the Upper East Side, and Queens.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recgDaQfgFBW1rCJg.name: Mouse Create: educator resource for free STEM, Design & CS Courses for school groups
recgDaQfgFBW1rCJg.description: An online learning platform designed for young people to build the tech & design skills. Educators from schools, community centers, and afterschool providers can partner with Mouse to integrate Mouse project curricula into their programs and classes, choosing from courses that cover circuitry, game design, web literacy, coding, green technology, and more.

recE4wKh3f39pReQn.name: Free diabetes supplies/medication, insurance/PAP help
recE4wKh3f39pReQn.description:
Mutual Aid Diabetes (MAD) is available to help anyone with any type of diabetes to access free or low cost supplies and medication as well as assist with insurance coverage and patient assistance programs. To request aid, please fill out our intake form here: https://airtable.com/shrr0XQLbZXNn1oGv.

Aid hotline (text or call): 646-780-9571
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recr6Fv4mXSpYfJLY.name: Name and Gender Change Information for Legal Documents
recr6Fv4mXSpYfJLY.description: Check your state for state-specific instructions on general name change, name/gender change on a birth certificate, and name/gender change on a driver's license. Check also for instructions for name/gender change on the following federal documents: US Passports, Social Security Records, Selective Service, US Immigration Documents, Military/Veteran Records, and Consular Birth Certificates.

recN2y6m7ZJGHdZPm.name: Free National Mental Health HelpLine
recN2y6m7ZJGHdZPm.description: Call 1-800-950-6264 (NAMI) or email info@nami.org, Monday-Friday, 10am to 10pm. Operators can provide information about mental illness and refer callers to treatment, support groups, family support, and legal support, if needed.

recBi7S9UB1ltQauu.name: National Dance Institute Free Online Classes
recBi7S9UB1ltQauu.description: Platform of free online classes, where NDI teaching artists lead children in signature NDI choreography, a variety of high-energy dance classes for all ability levels, plus exciting music classes. Classes can be accessed at anytime. (Closed captioning is available.)

recugoZiz5YmZV36C.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
recugoZiz5YmZV36C.description:
Free hotline and online chat for victims of domestic violence.

Call: 1-800-799-SAFE (7233)
Text "START" to 88788
Chat online: https://thehotline.org/
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recNUhxaHCCAuz5OQ.name: Assistance with Supportive Housing
recNUhxaHCCAuz5OQ.description:
Call 718-538-3344, Monday-Friday.
Housing advocacy in the areas of evictions, complaints, housing code violations, landlord/tenant and tenant/tenant mediation, and dispossession’s and foreclosures preventions. Also provide legal assistance, advocacy on behalf of the client should they be denied, rejected, and/or terminated for the following: housing application forms of HPD/NYCHA section 8, tenancy forms, NYC FEPS application, OTDA FEPS, SNAP, DRIE, LINK, SCRIE, homeowner’s loan program and rent stabilization forms.

recNUhxaHCCAuz5OQ.name: Free Housing Legal Services & Eviction Prevention Program
recNUhxaHCCAuz5OQ.description:
Call 718-538-3344 Ext. 100 or 117, Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm.
NAICA's primary focus is geared towards providing legal eviction prevention services to families and individuals who are working, receiving public assistance, or that meet the low-income eligibility and are at risk of losing their homes.

recGy1FOdnxoNLt7H.name: Homeownership assistance for low-to-moderate income families in Queens
recGy1FOdnxoNLt7H.description: Non-profit offering a variety of free and low-cost counseling and seminars to aid people in achieving and maintaining homeownership.

recmbvuH4mFMcko3C.name: Neighbors Together Empowerment Program
recmbvuH4mFMcko3C.description:
The Neighbors Together Empowerment Program connects its members to important resources such as housing, public benefits, job training, health and mental health care, legal services, income tax filing, and other resources needed by our members. They offer regular on-site clinics to provide specialized support to members. Please call 718.498.7256 for more information or to schedule an appointment.

Staff offer personalized support to those who struggle with persistent barriers to stability, such as mental illness, addiction or chronic unemployment, with a focus on long-term planning toward increased stability.

recysk5FCoLaInYBI.name: NYC Financial Justice Hotline
recysk5FCoLaInYBI.description: Call 212-925-4929 for free information, legal advice and referrals on topics including banking, debt, credit, and remittances. Mondays 4-6 and Tuesdays/Wednesdays/Thursdays 12-2. Available to low income NYC residents and community groups only.

recYlChoAtTfertm5.name: Resource Guide for Survivors of Sexual Assault
recYlChoAtTfertm5.description: A Resource Guide providing a directory of NYC-based organizations serving survivors of sexual violence, sex trafficking, domestic violence, and abuse. Each organization listed has a brief description of its services, contact information, office location, and spoken languages. Resources are categorized by the type of need including helplines, healthcare, financial support, legal options, housing, and more.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.name: Friendly VOICES Program
reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.description: The Friendly VOICES program builds friendships and limits social isolation for older adults who are isolated for reasons such as COVID-19. Volunteers can do virtual or in-person visits. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or apply online.

reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.name: Silver Corps Volunteer Assignments for Older Adults
reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.description:
An AmeriCorps program that provides older adults with volunteer assignments at a partner organization, training, and/or credentialing to secure employment. 

Must be at least 55 years of age, an NYC resident, currently unemployed or underemployed, and commit to volunteering 15 hours per week in a nonprofit or government agency.

Attend a virtual information session by completing the Silver Corps Interest Form linked on the website.

reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.name: Resource List: Food, Health, and Benefits for Elderly People
reczR3jcehkLXRgwy.description: A list of resources available to New York City's elderly community, including food, healthcare, and benefits.

recJiwH2r5xdOzbNI.name: Empowered NYC: Financial Counseling and Coaching
recJiwH2r5xdOzbNI.description: Fill out the online form to schedule free one-on-one financial counseling. Help with debt reduction, credit scores, savings, budgeting, opening a bank account, and preparing income information for housing applications. Appointment options may be in-person or by phone.

rec5OuTRHXRWO1rFx.name: NYC Infant and Toddler Education and Care Programs
rec5OuTRHXRWO1rFx.description:
New York City offers free or low-cost early childhood education infant and toddler programs for qualifying families with children between six weeks and three-years-old (who are not yet age-eligible for 3K). Extended Day/Year Infant and Toddler Programs provide year-round care and learning for up to 10 hours a day and are available in two settings:
- Center-based care at NYC Early Education Centers (NYCEECs)
- Home-based care through Family Child Care Networks (FCCNs)

To learn about eligibility and to enroll, contact a program directly, or email CCapplication@schools.nyc.gov

rec5OuTRHXRWO1rFx.name: Childcare for Babies and Toddlers: EarlyLearn Program
rec5OuTRHXRWO1rFx.description:
EarlyLearn NYC is free or low-cost child care and education for children six weeks to four years old available for families who qualify for free or low-cost care.

Visit the link to review application process. Must provide proof of address, income, and your citizenship or immigration status.

recgNwDMwA40s6wGh.name: Free Water Testing Kits for Lead
recgNwDMwA40s6wGh.description: Fill out the request form to receive a free kit to test your drinking water for lead. The kit comes with a pre-paid label to send it to a laboratory for lead analysis, and the results will be mailed to you within 30 days of the sample being tested. Limited to one per household at a time.

recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.name: Citywide Doula Initiative to Find Free Doula Services
recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.description:
Find professional, no-cost doula services. Check website for contact information for specific doula services by borough. Care is provided depending on zip codes.  To enroll, you must live in one of the neighborhoods shown on the website and be income-eligible for Medicaid. 

The program prioritizes people who: live in a shelter, are in foster care, have no other labor support, are giving birth for the first time, had a previous traumatic birth experience, or have a high-risk medical condition

recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.name: Low to No Cost Sexual Health Care, Immunizations, and TB Care
recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.description:
The DOHMH Public Health Clinics provide sexual health, immunization, and TB services- regardless of insurance or immigration status. We’re especially focused on making sure care is accessible, LGBTQ+ inclusive, and welcoming for all. If anyone doesn't have health insurance, we offer services on a sliding scale based on income and family size. No income proof is required and no one is ever turned away due to inability to pay.

Clinics are located in Central Harlem, Morrisania, Chelsea, Fort Greene, Jamaica, and Corona

recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.name: NYC Mpox Information
recrVWeRMwFL3dtQY.description: Information on Mpox transmission, symptoms, prevention, and vaccine updates from the New York City Department of Health.

reckWtOb4K2OwoyCV.name: NYC Housing Connect to Find and Apply for Affordable Housing
reckWtOb4K2OwoyCV.description: A website to search for and apply for the lottery of available affordable housing apartments in New York City. Income requirements depend on the area where the apartment is, and can be found on the site. It may take several months for applications to be processed. You may apply to multiple different lotteries at once.

receIOujn0Tw2oBUA.name: Rent Stabilization for Senior Citizens
receIOujn0Tw2oBUA.description: SCRIE helps eligible senior citizens ages 62 and over stay in affordable housing by freezing their rent at a certain amount. Tenants pay the frozen rent. A property tax credit covers the difference between the actual rent amount and the frozen rent. See the website for eligibility requirements.

receIOujn0Tw2oBUA.name: NYC Fair Fares Program for Half-Price Transportation

recDDaCGnWLH4R63S.name: New York City Tenant Resource Portal and Eviction Prevention Tool
recDDaCGnWLH4R63S.description: The goal of this portal is to help tenants across the city find the resources they need in one place. This eviction prevention tool was designed by the Mayor's Office to Protect Tenants (MOPT) and the Mayor's Public Engagement Unit's (PEU) Tenant Support Unit (TSU) to help renters navigate public and private resources that can stabilize their housing situation. A tenant seeking help will be taken through a series of questions and directed to the most useful resources based on their responses. MOPT and PEU have included resources from multiple city agencies, Legal Service Providers, and Community Based Organizations.

recEBYAGRpXMD8FCh.name: Virtual 12-Step meetings for people who use crystal meth
recEBYAGRpXMD8FCh.description: A calendar of online and in-person (socially distant) meetings and social activities. Call the 24 hour helpline at 1-855-638-4373.

recSTajPApcT9oGV7.name: Legal Information and Preparedness Resources for Immigrant New Yorkers
recSTajPApcT9oGV7.description: A collection of resources for immigrants, including: A community toolkit, Know Your Rights information as printable posters and wallet cards, Know Your Rights curriculum with presentation and facilitator materials, immigration detention support information, family preparedness guides, and more. Resources are available in multiple languages.

recaGPMKJSTyLwHWC.name: Health Services for Indigenous New Yorkers
recaGPMKJSTyLwHWC.description: Call 718-215-8417 or enroll online to schedule health services or receive referrals at no charge. Services include urgent and emergency care, preventive care, primary and specialty care, behavioral health & recovery support, and transportation assistance. Note that we are only able to cover services arranged or referred by NYIC in advance. NYIC cannot reimburse members for services they book or receive independently (i.e. without prior approval).

rec76Ug34hxVRWIKT.name: Free Legal Support for People Experiencing Poverty or In Crisis
rec76Ug34hxVRWIKT.description: For legal assistance or financial counseling, contact the office by either filling out the online intake form or calling and leaving a message with full name, contact info, and description of legal or financial counseling needs. Legal support focuses on helping immigrants, survivors of violence and discrimination, and people who need support securing access to health care and essential benefits, demanding safe and affordable housing , and protecting their economic rights.

recCrfy11FlZ6UyRQ.name: Free Mediation Services for Brooklyn and Manhattan
recCrfy11FlZ6UyRQ.description: New York Peace Institute offers free in-person mediation for Brooklyn and Manhattan residents. Also offers conflict coaching and restorative processes to help you resolve your conflict.

recb9cC0pHQhqu4Eg.name: Connections 2026: A Guide for Formerly Incarcerated People in NYC
recb9cC0pHQhqu4Eg.description: A collection of resources for formally incarcerated people. The guide includes resources related to education, money, housing, mental and physical health, substance use, and more.

recb9cC0pHQhqu4Eg.name: NYPL Free Online Tutoring for Grades 1-12
recb9cC0pHQhqu4Eg.description: Get free online homework help with your library card from one-on-one tutors, daily from 2–11 PM. Available in English, Spanish, and French from early elementary through high school grades, in core subject areas. Video content and other resources are also available 24 hours a day.

rec9FAGexyxuvfLrF.name: New York State Social Services Information for Children and Youth
rec9FAGexyxuvfLrF.description: MS Navigator help users find and access health, education, human services, and disability information for newborns through age 22. Includes links to Medicaid help, mental wellness and well-being, youth peer advocacy, family peer advocates, and more.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recETPTPxpLM0zHd9.name: Resources for Parents: Caregiving Programs and Tips, Navigating Human Services
recETPTPxpLM0zHd9.description: The NYS Parent Portal provides access to parents ranging from those who are expecting, those seeking ways to build a family, and others looking for parenting tips and ways to further nurture their children's development. Includes links to childcare programs and social service guidance programs.

reciwBph8045y6bCo.name: Online Learning with Coursera
reciwBph8045y6bCo.description:
Free access to nearly 4,000 courses in data science, business, and technology for New Yorkers who are unemployed. Online email registration required.

Submit application for account to access courses. Use this link to apply and view courses: https://dol.ny.gov/online-learning-coursera

recVyzYUWQlLjiHn0.name: Health Insurance Information, Counseling and Assistance Program
recVyzYUWQlLjiHn0.description: Call 1-800-701-0501 Monday - Friday, 8:30am-5pm to get answers to questions about Medicare, Medicare Advantage programs (managed care), Medicare prescription drug coverage, Medigap, and other health and long-term care insurance issues

reccjQSMfj9LZTfFN.name: Community Health Access to Addiction & Mental Healthcare Project (CHAMP)
reccjQSMfj9LZTfFN.description:
Call the CHAMP live-answer Helpline for free and confidential assistance accessing mental health and substance use disorder care.   Monday-Friday 9am-4pm. Supports multiple languages and all insurance types (including uninsured folks).

CHAMP assistance includes help finding a mental health or substance use disorder provider, appealing an insurer’s denial of care, and understanding your rights to mental health and substance use disorder care.

CHAMP is a partnership among specialist organizations, community based organizations, and the New York State Offices of Addiction Services and Supports (OASAS) and Mental Health.

recn1XmnQ7MBeHcIf.name: NYS HOPEline: Gambling and Chemical Dependency Hotline
recn1XmnQ7MBeHcIf.description: Call 1-877-8-HOPENY or text 467369 at any time if you are experiencing substance abuse and problem gambling. This service is free, confidential, and offered in English, Spanish, Bengali, Traditional Chinese, Haitian-Creole, Korean, and Russian.

rec2hOes1PHD7vZht.name: Temporary Financial Assistance for Families and Individuals
rec2hOes1PHD7vZht.description: Temporary Assistance (TA) is temporary financial help for people who are unable to work, can’t find a job, or whose job does not pay enough. The two types of TA are Family Assistance and Safety Net Assistance. Apply via https://mybenefits.ny.gov or file an application at your local department of Social Services. Government ID is required. Call the OTDA Hotline for more information: 1-800-342-3009

rec2hOes1PHD7vZht.name: Emergency Rental Assistance Program
rec2hOes1PHD7vZht.description: New York State Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) will provide economic relief to help low and moderate-income households at risk of experiencing homelessness or housing instability by providing rental arrears, temporary rental assistance and utility arrears assistance. No immigration status requirements to apply. See website for eligibility and application requirements. Funds are not always available, so check website to see if applications are currently being accepted.

recso6F5tb1lzeFTv.name: Free Services for Residents of Upper Manhattan and the Bronx
recso6F5tb1lzeFTv.description: Call the hotline at 929-415-8970 to get assistance in a number of areas including a food pantry, tax preparation, unemployment insurance, benefits, housing, or immigration needs.

recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.name: Free healthcare access application for people with HIV/AIDS
recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.description: The Uninsured Care Programs provide access to free health care (Drugs, Outpatient Primary Care, Home Care, Insurance Premium Payments, and Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to prevent HIV infection) for New York State residents who are uninsured or underinsured. The Uninsured Care Programs are committed to working closely with providers and individuals to support access to the wide range of options for payment for health care services and medications for persons living with or at risk of acquiring HIV/AIDS.

recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.name: Growing Up Healthy Hotline for Families with Children
recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.description:
Call the hotline anytime at 1-800-522-5006. We're open 24/7. TTY 1-800-655-1789.

Help is available for health care, nutrition, pregnancy, family planning, children's needs, and more.

recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.name: Guidance on Applying for WIC for Families with Children
recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.description: Information on how to apply for WIC. The WIC program provides support with accessing food, nutrition education, and resources for expecting parents and caregivers. Government ID required.

recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.name: Health Insurance Enrollment Assistance
recc6SqTOMTFgK34n.description:
Free or inexpensive public health insurance is available for those meeting financial eligibility requirements.
Call 1-855-355-5777 to enroll directly or call the Medicaid Helpline (800) 541-2831 for assistance.
Free enrollment assistance through city - call 311 or text CoveredNYC (SeguroNYC en Español) to 877877.
For assistance enrolling through a local community-based organization: call (888) 614-5400 or email enroll@cssny.org.
All NYC Health + Hospitals centers will provide healthcare regardless of insurance coverage, and can help with insurance enrollment: call 1-844-NYC-4NYC.

recqafm6b8V5ei94V.name: Child Care Vouchers for Children 6 Weeks - 13 Years Old
recqafm6b8V5ei94V.description: Apply for vouchers from the city to help cover the cost of child care for children 6 weeks to 13 years old at home-based and center-based providers across NYC. Most families are required to pay part of the costs based on their income and family size, but your voucher will cover all of the costs if you are: a family on cash assistance, a family experiencing homelessness, or a foster care parent. Visit the website for eligibility and application details.

reczW4UUZ90qMpPYL.name: Hotline for LGBTQ and HIV-affected Survivors of Violence
reczW4UUZ90qMpPYL.description: Call 212-714-1141 to reach a free, bilingual (English/Spanish), 24-hour, 365-day-a-year crisis intervention hotline that offers support to LGBTQ & HIV-affected survivors of any type of violence, as well as to those who love and support survivors, including those who have lost a loved one to violence.

recaJeoyGUtMPQUN5.name: Information About Housing Rights For City Residents
recaJeoyGUtMPQUN5.description: Information from the NYC Commission on Human Rights about what NYC Human Rights law covers in relation to housing discrimination including specific scenarios in which a complaint might be filed.

recfbWM5dUiWfRDWZ.name: Rent Stabilization for People with Disabilities
recfbWM5dUiWfRDWZ.description:
Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE) helps eligible tenants with disabilities stay in affordable housing by freezing their rent at a certain amount. Tenants pay the frozen rent. A property tax credit covers the difference between the actual rent amount and the frozen rent. 

To apply, fill out the application and mail to:
New York City Department of Finance Rent Freeze Program - DRIE, P.O. Box 3179, Union, NJ 07083

You can also call 311 and request a DRIE specialist or register with their client portal and send a message at www.nyc.gov/contactdrie.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recoLLChB0SnghE78.name: Naloxone Access in NYC
recoLLChB0SnghE78.description: Use this guide to find how to access naloxone in NYC, as well as trainings in how to administer it.

rec5IxEhVt0JPkyhz.name: Plentiful App to Find and Make Reservations at Food Pantries
rec5IxEhVt0JPkyhz.description: Download the Plentiful app on Android or text "FOOD" to PANTRY (726-879) from any phone to find a food program and register, make a reservation, or sign up for updates.

recGDkaM3P2zYymPp.name: AfterCare Resource Center for Long COVID
recGDkaM3P2zYymPp.description: The AfterCare Resource Center provides information and tools related to Long COVID, and connects New Yorkers recovering from COVID-19 or living with Long COVID to the health and social resources to support them in their recovery. Support provided regardless of one’s ability to pay or immigration status.

recGDkaM3P2zYymPp.name: Low and No Cost Healthcare through NYC Health + Hospitals
recGDkaM3P2zYymPp.description: Visit NYCCare.nyc or call 1-646-NYC-CARE (1-646-692-2273) to enroll in the NYC Care program and access low- and no-cost healthcare from NYC Health + Hospitals, regardless of immigration status. Proof of identity, proof of income, proof of address, and insurance eligibility determination are required. Even if you are unable to provide the required documents, you may still be able to enroll.

recnhmUsWveqqHWs2.name: NYC City Government Housing Resource Portal
recnhmUsWveqqHWs2.description: A collection of New York City Housing resources, searchable and sortable by topic. Resources include information on legal and financial issues, repairs, safety, reporting problems to the city, tenants rights, and more. Compiled as part of the NYC government "Your Home NYC" initiative.

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP): Money for Heat, Cooling, and Utility Expenses
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Apply for money to pay for fuel, your utility source, equipment and/or repairs through the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP). Apply online or call the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance at 800-692-0557 for assistance. A government ID is required.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: Homebase: Support for housing stability to avoid shelter entry
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description:
Call 311 or visit nyc.gov/homebase to learn more about housing resources provided by the city of New York. Services include eviction prevention, assistance obtaining public benefits, employment search and assistance, financial counseling, relocation resources, and short-term financial assistance. This program is especially intended for individuals at imminent risk of entering the NYC shelter system/experiencing homelessness. 

Homebase is a homelessness prevention network with 26 locations across NYC’s five boroughs. Use the homebase locator to find the location in your borough.

This resource is currently only available over the phone. To access the hotline, call 311 and ask for homebase services. This service is specifically for people at risk of eviction/houselessness, and may not be useful for individuals already experiencing houselessness. 

A government ID is required.

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: One Shot Deal: Emergency One-Time Cash Assistance
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Government ID required. One-time emergency cash assistance, not dependent on immigration status - to prevent eviction, pay energy or utility bills, or buy health-related items. Apply via ACCESS HRA or call (718) 557-1399 for more information. (Processing times *should* be 30 days after applying.)

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: Emergency Grant for Burials
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Apply online or call 718-557-1399 for funds to meet funeral expenses for a deceased low-income New York City resident.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: Help with Moving Expenses
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Assistance for HRA clients related to moving, including help with moving expenses, broker's fees, and NYCHA security deposits. See Special Grant Document Guide webpage for specific forms.

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: NYC Government Information about SNAP Enrollment
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Call the NYC HRA info line at 718-557-1399 and press "2", or download the "Access HRA" app to learn more about and apply for SNAP benefits.

recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.name: Money to help pay for rent or mortgage that you owe
recLKylSpMtF5aiVe.description: Emergency grant to help pay for rent or mortgage that you owe. Must provide documentation showing how future rent payments will be made, including a statement from a third party who will help you pay your rent.

recoVlND460KSfQuQ.name: Affordable Community-Owned Internet
recoVlND460KSfQuQ.description: Fill in the join form to get connected to secure, affordable community-powered NYC Mesh internet

recHTsa5EdrrPeI8r.name: Financial guidance, marketing, and planning support for small businesses
recHTsa5EdrrPeI8r.description: Small Business Support Specialists offer businesses that are opening or reopening support with applying for grants and loans, digital marketing, getting online, lease negotiations, and business planning.

recXEDx7ADyNlfFKK.name: Free Digital Mental Health Resources
recXEDx7ADyNlfFKK.description: Library of apps and online services offering mental health support, including for depression, anxiety, and addiction.

recXEDx7ADyNlfFKK.name: Free & Confidential Mental Health Support via Call Or Text
recXEDx7ADyNlfFKK.description:
Text or call 988 for Free & Confidential Mental Health + Substance Use Support open 24/7. A chat service is also available on the website.

Interpreters are available for 200+ languages. Stay on the line, and you will be connected with a counselor who can connect you to translator services.

recHP65GEIpeJN8ze.name: Latinx LGBTQ+ Community Health Services: STI Testing, HIV Care, and Support
recHP65GEIpeJN8ze.description: Call 212-675-3288 or make an appointment online. For the Latinx LGBTIA+ community to access free testing, workshops, enrollment into programs that allow you to access clinical services, and large scale social events. Services include both in-person and virtual resources including STI testing, HIV prevention and treatment, and substance use support.

recDWSaHIVg2aweZy.name: Fiscal Hosting for Mutual Aid Groups in New York City
recDWSaHIVg2aweZy.description: NYC Mutual Aid Groups looking for a fiscal sponsor can get in touch at pactbk@gmail.com. A fiscal sponsor is an entity that holds money on behalf of a collective, and takes care of accounting, taxes, and invoices.

recOl9hPQ56oPzZL4.name: Senior Planet Virtual Events
recOl9hPQ56oPzZL4.description: A listing of free virtual events and activities including fitness classes and discussions. For tech questions, call the Senior Planet NYC hotline at (917) 936-4410.

reccBrLmJbwynRRrW.name: Supportive Network for Caregivers for People with Special Healthcare Needs
reccBrLmJbwynRRrW.description: Call 1-800-405-8818 if you are working with a parent of a child with disabilities or special health care needs looking for information about support groups and available resources.

recM2OEt3Mgmm36Om.name: Hire Harm-Reduction Medics with Sliding-Scale Rates for Events
recM2OEt3Mgmm36Om.description:
Hire harm-reduction medics from PartySafe Medics on a sliding-scale for events. Message on SMS, Signal, or WhatsApp, or visit the website or Instagram @partysafemedics. 

Services include safer drug use education, first aid, and overdose prevention. Medics are supplied with Naloxone, drug testing strips, safer drug use supplies, sexual health and hygiene products, oxygen tanks, and more.

recjKdJYMyoTeDSni.name: Phoenix Community Garden Food Boxes
recjKdJYMyoTeDSni.description: Subscription and single-purchase options for fresh produce boxes from the Phoenix Community Garden, with pick-up in Ocean Hill-Brownsville. Sliding scale pricing.

recrUs1KyU2XOASOK.name: Free Mental Health Support for Parents
recrUs1KyU2XOASOK.description: State-wide help line to support parents before and after having a baby. Call 7 days a week, 9am-5pm to access non-judgmental and confidential emotional support, educational information, healthcare and support group resources, and to connect to parental mental health peer support groups.

rec9YcoudBrBlZw96.name: Shelter-Based Clinics for Homeless People
rec9YcoudBrBlZw96.description: The shelter-based clinics located in Third Street, Fort Washington, New Providence, and Williams Avenue serve homeless adults from all over New York City. No one is turned away, regardless of their ability to pay. Services include primary care, diabetes testing, depression and substance abuse screening, HIV testing and viral load suppression, tobacco cessation, and detox treatments.

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Free Daily Showers
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description:
Hot showers, fresh towels and toiletries are available.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Ave
8:30-11:30 a.m. / 12:30-2:20 p.m.
Monday-Friday

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Help with Eviction Prevention and Other Issues at POTS Legal Clinic
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description: Speak with an attorney or legal advocate if you are behind on your rent or otherwise in danger of eviction, or for help accessing public benefits. POTS can also offer brief advice and referrals on other legal issues. Call 718-220-4892, ext. 101 and leave a message or send an email to legalclinc@potsbronx.org.

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Community Dining Room for Free Meals
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description:
Enjoy a healthy meal served to your table.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue
12:30 PM - 3:00 PM Monday-Saturday.

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Free Haircuts
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description:
Free haircuts for the first 30 clients (with ticket - given at POTS) of all ages.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue. Starts at 8:30 am – First 30 Clients Tuesday and Thursday.

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Free Medical and Dental Clinic
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description: Free Clinic operated by Care for the Homeless at our POTS 2759 Webster Avenue location.

recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.name: Provide Free Mailing Address to Pickup Mail
recXVAi68UcnRJrkK.description:
Clients may register for this service or pick up their mail.

Come to POTS 2759 Webster Avenue from 12:30pm-3:30pm Monday-Friday*.

*Important: This service closes at 3 p.m. on Wednesdays.

recI3bwq2VjgvsI5r.name: Circle of Care - Support for Caregivers of People with Chronic Illness or Memory Loss
recI3bwq2VjgvsI5r.description: If you care for someone who is frail, chronically ill or has memory loss call (866) 665-1713 or fill out an online form to get free personalized support from a Care Consultant. Services include telechat support groups, webinars, and temporary (paid) respite. All New Yorkers are eligible at all income levels.

recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.name: Affordable locally-grown produce in Queens
recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.description: A Food Box Program offering weekly boxed collections of locally grown produce that can be purchased affordably. See website for information on Community Garden, Food Justice programs, and Quarterly Potlucks!

recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.name: Generation Q, at Queens Community House
recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.description: An after-school youth center for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer youth and allies, between the ages of 13 and 21. They offer a wide variety of educational and recreational opportunities, as well as social and emotional support. Open Tuesday through Friday 3-7pm.

recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.name: Housing and Homelessness Prevention
recZ7sJIkveJDCZ5b.description: Tenants can call 718-592-5757 ext. 243, email skhan@qchnyc.org, or email mmoore@qchnyc.org to access housing counseling and tenants rights workshops and receive help with applying for rental subsidies, negotiating lease renewals, and obtaining apartment unit repairs. Low-income individuals and families who at risk of eviction can access: household risk assessment, application assistance, access to government benefits, budget counseling and advocacy, including referrals to Food Access, Health Care, Public Assistance, legal and other supportive services to help people remain housed and stable.

rece9SebSwj49qmqP.name: Case Management Program for Older New Yorkers
rece9SebSwj49qmqP.description: Call (718) 892-5520 to access the R.A.I.N. Case Management Program, which serves home bound seniors 60 years of age and over residing in Bronx Community Districts 7,8,11, and 12. Case Managers can assess and link seniors to a wide range of services such as transportation, housekeeping, home care, home delivered meals and assistance with entitlements and benefits.

recFI4oNIOjM9iIVS.name: Free Diapers and Wipes for Brooklyn Families
recFI4oNIOjM9iIVS.description: ​Visit Rain or Shine Diaper Fund every Monday at The Living Gallery in Brooklyn, NY, to receive free diapers and wipes. Get a number at 8am, and distribution is at 1pm. No ID or sign-up required.

recP4dfVk3838tXb5.name: Benefits and Social Service Guidance
recP4dfVk3838tXb5.description:
Contact customer service at 718-636-6994 or walk in to schedule an appointment at Restoration Plaza at the Financial Empowerment Center.

Restoration provides a continuum of services from case managers, licensed lawyers, financial counselors, housing ambassadors, and social workers including a free benefit screening, on-site food stamp and Medicaid enrollment, financial and legal counseling, social services referrals, and one-on-one case management.

recjIb7Q38VCQjIE9.name: Mental Health Resources for LGBTQ+ Community
recjIb7Q38VCQjIE9.description: Free membership-based community of LGBT adults living with a mental illness. Services include peer support groups and social activities.

recbrzpM04X4I3Mie.name: Right to Counsel Tenant Organizing Materials
recbrzpM04X4I3Mie.description: Tenant organizing resources including a pamphlet and fighting eviction, the case for rent strike, a list of tenant organizing groups across NYC, and Right to Counsel advocacy information.

recyzMGD05H7Kq61Z.name: Parents' Legal Rights and Information
recyzMGD05H7Kq61Z.description: This webpage provides links to information for parents related to your legal rights and child welfare and how to get support.

recawgSdcfEiFBIpo.name: RiseBoro HSE/ESL Program (English and Spanish)
recawgSdcfEiFBIpo.description:
Fill out the form to access free HSE Adult Education classes at RiseBoro (English and Spanish). Classes are designed to prepare students for the Test Assessing Secondary Completion (TASC) that will provide them with a High School Equivalency Diploma. Students will receive instruction in reading comprehension, writing, social studies, science and math. 
The Free English as a Second Language (ESL) classes (Level I - Level IV) are for non-native English speakers to improve listening, speaking, reading and writing.

recQhDRkVPzbBbav8.name: Resources for Survivors of Domestic and Family Violence
recQhDRkVPzbBbav8.description: Call 877-STEPS-94 (877-783-7794) STEPS to End Violence (STEPS) is a holistic program of services for victims of gender-based violence with a focus on prevention, intervention, and policy advocacy. We provide comprehensive, trauma-informed case management, crisis counseling, clinical intervention, and services to promote economic self-sufficiency to victims of domestic violence throughout New York City.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recoCsqvFqjgnL5DV.name: SAG-AFTRA Emergency Financial Assistance
recoCsqvFqjgnL5DV.description: See website for application and eligibility details. Emergency financial assistance is available for SAG-ASTRA members who are in urgent financial need due to an unexpected life crisis such as a natural disaster, accident, health crisis creating a financial burden, loss of work due to an illness, loss of housing due to an eviction, death in the family, or other emergency crisis situations covered under IRS guidelines which pertain to granting tax-free monies to individuals.

recekUvAzd0dfltBv.name: Immigrant Legal Support for Survivors of Violence and Abuse
recekUvAzd0dfltBv.description: We help immigrant survivors of violence and abuse obtain status and protection, enabling them to live and work safely in the United States. Our work focuses on humanitarian-based relief created specifically for immigrant survivors, such as U-visas, VAWA self-petitions and asylum, as well as “green card” applications, naturalization, and removal defense. We work with people from around the world who have experienced trauma and offer services in any language.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recekUvAzd0dfltBv.name: Domestic Violence Hotline
recekUvAzd0dfltBv.description: Call 1-800-621-HOPE (4673) for assistance in domestic violence situations, including crisis counseling, safety planning, assistance with finding domestic violence shelters, and information about resources.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recwOgtbix2cIygqg.name: Sakhi for South Asian Women Helpline for Gender-Based Violence
recwOgtbix2cIygqg.description:
Call (212) 868-6741, text (305) 204-1809, or email advocate@sakhi.org Monday through Friday, 10am-10pm, for assistance with gender-based violence in the South Asian diaspora.

The helpline is able to assist in English, Hindi, Urdu, and Bengali. In addition, they also have an over-the-phone interpretation service if needed for another language.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

rec2oeD2dooGnLOdP.name: Community and Family Services Counseling and Support
rec2oeD2dooGnLOdP.description: SCO Family of Services provides a range of community, family, and children's services in Brooklyn and Long Island including access to counseling, community centers, literacy, after school, and employment services.

rec3JOm7LiMSBadNe.name: Talkin’ It Out - Phone Chat for Older Adults
rec3JOm7LiMSBadNe.description: Call to learn more. Older adults 60+ can "chat” confidentially by phone for free with a bilingual (Spanish/English) licensed Master’s Level Social Worker, to discuss issues and concerns outside of formal psychotherapy.

recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.name: Behavioral Health Services for People Struggling with Mental Health and Substance Use
recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.description: Reach out via their phone or email for direction to applicable behavioral health services including care coordination, treatment, and recovery: 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.name: Veteran Housing and Employment Services
recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.description: For housing services, reach out to the supportive services arm of the organization (631-227-0777 or ssvfintakes@sus.org). For employment, contact 877-583-5336 or services@sus.org.

recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.name: Homeless Services for Individuals and Families in NYC
recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.description: Works to provide a a steady and growing pipeline of permanent low-income housing, and other services such as eviction support.

recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.name: Developmental Disabilities Services
recwlTpgvnmD7nUBj.description: Offers housing, employment, and other support for both children and adults. See each type of support for the best person to contact.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

rec0KbmujXVdFWFpf.name: Hotline and Legal Services for Jewish Victims of Domestic Abuse
rec0KbmujXVdFWFpf.description: Call/text/Whatsapp 888.883.2323 to speak to someone confidentially to talk about a domestic abuse situation. Shalom Task Force’s Legal Department also provides free, confidential legal services to victim-survivors of domestic and dating abuse, specializing in the Jewish community.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

rect1prBH0YaVuQFe.name: Access to Health Services and Other Benefits
rect1prBH0YaVuQFe.description: Call (718) 321-7929 or email sacss@sacssny.org to get help accessing both private and public healthcare coverage, as well as help getting public benefits. This service is open to all, including South Asian and other immigrants.

rec3PhxVIvBFRI3RX.name: Free Showers and Personal Hygiene
rec3PhxVIvBFRI3RX.description: Get free showers, toiletries, clean clothes, snacks, and water with Shower Power NYC’s Fresh City program in Harlem (Mon/Fri at Harlem United) and Ridgewood (Tues at Ridgewood Presbyterian Church), 10am–2pm. No ID or appointment needed.

recHOPdxMW9U3y2OT.name: How to Set Up a Mutual Aid Fund
recHOPdxMW9U3y2OT.description: A September 2020 essay about how the STL Mutual Aid Fund was set up, with tips for other mutual aid organizers.

recDNCEa91hUR5rax.name: Substance Use and Mental Health 24-Hour Helpline
recDNCEa91hUR5rax.description: Call (800) 662-4357 (HELP) for individuals and families facing mental and/or substance use disorders.
