Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) runs a 24-hour mental health hotline that provides education, support, and connections to treatment. The helpline is confidential; they collect no information. In English and  Spanish. Can also text your zip code to 435748 (HELP4U) to find treatment centers in your area.

recDNCEa91hUR5rax.name: Natural Disaster Distress Hotline
recDNCEa91hUR5rax.description: 1-800-985-5990, is a 24/7, 365-day-a-year. A National hotline dedicated to providing year-round disaster crisis counseling. This toll-free, multilingual, crisis support service is available 24/7 to all residents in the U.S. and its territories who are experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters.

recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.name: Free Food Distribution Thursdays in Sunnyside
recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Sunnyside on Thursdays at 1:15pm at Bliss Plaza on Queens Blvd & 46th St.

recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Woodside at the 61st St-Woodside Station
recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays at 1:30pm at the 61st St-Woodside MTA Station in Queens.

recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays at Woodside Houses
recK2w8iJyBZD2BOi.description: Free food from pop-up pantry in Woodside, Thursdays 1:30pm at the Woodside Houses at 49th St & Broadway

rec795pUt3p8Ho2ZF.name: Resources for fighting the criminalization of survivors of domestic and sexual violence.
rec795pUt3p8Ho2ZF.description: An organization that both offers support, resources, survivor advocates, legal experts, and policy advocates for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, but also organizes around fighting the criminalization of survivors. Provides access to mutual aid resources and joining community organizing efforts to free survivors from the carcerel system.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recPTgHSVcMWueXIL.name: Harlem Community Fridge at 155th St
recPTgHSVcMWueXIL.description: Harlem community fridge open 24/7 at 155th St and Bradhurst. Fresh produce on Saturdays 11 AM-1pm, and hot meals on Sundays 3-5pm.

recmAx54SyWVSuX46.name: Mutual Aid Legal Toolkit
recmAx54SyWVSuX46.description: Legal resource guide (published 2020) with grassroots mutual aid networks in mind. Includes information on entity formation, established charitable organizations, liability, governance and decision making, managing funds, sharing goods and services (i.e. bartering), and data security. Includes appendices with sample forms, case studies, and other resources. Licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-SA 4.0).

recr1uQeWX4ExlqDT.name: Lower East Side Harm Reduction Center
recr1uQeWX4ExlqDT.description:
Call 212-645-0875, x100 to make an appointment. Services include sterile injecting equipment; safer sex supplies; Narcan/Naloxone overdose prevention meds; HIV and hepatitis C testing; medical and mental health care, counseling, and referrals; and case management. Hours:
Monday-Saturday 9am-5pm (syringe exchange 9-4:30).

recwJFs0v50ZTJnxp.name: Assistance Fund financial assistance for health-related expenses
recwJFs0v50ZTJnxp.description: The Assistance Fund is an independent nonprofit organization that helps patients and families facing high medical out-of-pocket costs by providing financial assistance for their copayments, coinsurance, deductibles, and other health-related expenses for over 70 medical conditions (some are waitlist, some are open for application). Find eligibility and more info on the website.
community_focus: People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recYEI9ApnHslTets.name: Temporary Shelter and Help for Muslim Women and Families Facing Domestic Violence, Eviction, or Homelessness
recYEI9ApnHslTets.description: Call the Helpline at 718-833-2425. They provide shelter, legal and immigration services, help navigating public or government assistance, managing medical needs and mental health resources, assisting in securing long-term housing, and finding employment.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

rec5LaOexQMe0ElEN.name: Supportive housing for adults, seniors, and veterans living with serious mental illness and/or substance use disorders
rec5LaOexQMe0ElEN.description:
Call 212-663-3000.
Supportive housing. The Bridge houses 1500+ people in the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Manhattan, and offers a range of on-site services based on client level of need, including case management, advocacy, therapeutic activities, and linkages to community-based treatment and services.

rec5LaOexQMe0ElEN.name: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic
rec5LaOexQMe0ElEN.description: Provides a single, comprehensive hub for "clients" seeking treatment for their mental health and/or substance use issues. The Bridge partners with Ryan Health, a licensed health clinic, to offer behavioral and primary health care under one roof. Includes outpatient treatment and substance use treatment.

rechprWrdgnxKpdDI.name: Free Legal and Social Services Support for Low Income People in the Bronx
rechprWrdgnxKpdDI.description:
Call 718-838-7878 (Mon-Fri 9am-4pm) for free legal and social services for immigration, housing, criminal, and family defense, as well as social work support and advocacy. Legal Emergency Hotline: 347-778-1266 (Available 24/7)
Housing Hotline: 347-842-1122 (Available two Mondays* every month, from 9:00AM to 5:00PM)

recylwtaZfYuNiFM7.name: LGBTQ+ Affirming Mental Health Services
recylwtaZfYuNiFM7.description: Fill out the pre-intake form on the website to learn more and get connected to 1:1 short-term counseling services available to individuals ages 18 and over who reside in New York State. Sessions are provided in person and virtually.

recOUOm64TgSE66qk.name: Free Resources - Children's Mental Health and Learning Challenges
recOUOm64TgSE66qk.description: Visit the Family Resource Center to find information to help support children who are struggling with mental health, behavior or learning challenges. Resources available in English and Spanish.

recV6gQsVrahEnhTO.name: Legal Consultations for Immigrants
recV6gQsVrahEnhTO.description: Family-based immigration services including one-on-one legal consultations and application assistance on issues such as: adjustment of legal status, filing for citizenship and naturalization and family-based petitions. Email info@coalitionfreedom.org or call 212-781-0355 ext. 101.

recNWJZ8yLC4D8ExD.name: Lifeline Grocery Packages
recNWJZ8yLC4D8ExD.description: Sign-up online for this community initiative that delivers groceries free to families in Queens, NYC, but note that there is often a waitlist. This program prioritizes families who are out of work and do not qualify for unemployment or sufficient government assistance.

recYO2HAHSWCKwBpo.name: Employment Opportunities for the Long-Term Unemployed
recYO2HAHSWCKwBpo.description:
The Doe Fund offers employment opportunities for people who have experienced long-term unemployment but who are not homeless. To learn more, call one of the facilities or email info@doe.org: 
Brooklyn: 646-672-2973
Harlem: 718-417-2538

recYO2HAHSWCKwBpo.name: Workforce Training and Supportive Housing for Homeless Men
recYO2HAHSWCKwBpo.description:
Call Brooklyn: 646-672-2973 | Harlem: 718-417-2538 for more information.
Ready, Willing, and Able is a 12-month residential program with paid work—complemented by holistic social services, career training, education, and sobriety support. If you’re already in the New York City shelter system and would like to join Ready, Willing & Able, talk to your case manager or parole officer about a transfer to a Doe Fund facility. The Ready, Willing & Able program is open to all men able to work and maintain sobriety, ages 18 and up.

recI3NAnsZv61fRhX.name: Free Programs and Services for Young People Ages 12 to 24
recI3NAnsZv61fRhX.description: The Door offers a variety of services in health, mental health, legal, education, arts, housing, and more for youth and young people ages 12 through 24.

recwK3LEgFo2LcEQc.name: Community Fridge in Washington Heights
recwK3LEgFo2LcEQc.description: Community Fridge in Washington Heights at 181st St & Fort Washington Ave. Take what you need, give what you can. Open 24/7.

reciB8kfGiZemrc6e.name: Support for Formerly Incarcerated People
reciB8kfGiZemrc6e.description:
New clients call 212-691-7554 for services including intakes and enrollment, counseling, case management, access to benefits, job readiness training and employment services, education, mental health, treatment services, and food distribution.

Hours Monday-Thursday: 8 AM – 8 PM and Friday: 8 AM – 5 PM

recafixrxJpSRzKHe.name: Free Baby Formula Exchange
recafixrxJpSRzKHe.description: Submit an online form to offer or request baby formula on this nationwide platform. You can also search for available formula by location and contact donors directly.

recbt4RUnF54lIMnZ.name: Bronx Community Fridge and Food Hub
recbt4RUnF54lIMnZ.description:
Take food from the Friendly Fridge Bronx around the corner from the last stop on the 1 train at 242nd St, or leave fresh food to feed our neighbors and use up food unused food. Available for anyone.

Food Hub Hours: Tues, Thurs & Fri at 2 pm

recVHiId4WdbLUrIa.name: SNAP Enrollment Assistance
recVHiId4WdbLUrIa.description: Call 347-880-2922 to speak to local Met Council Nutrition Outreach and Education Program (NOEP) coordinator to help to determine if you are eligible to apply for SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and help you complete and submit your application. Free and confidential.

recyUJmxPLCM2vWVj.name: Free job training and placements
recyUJmxPLCM2vWVj.description: The HOPE Program is a non-profit organization that offers 5 different job training programs: job readiness training, construction training, industry certifications such as OSHA-30 internships, HSE prep, job placement, and more. Virtual Info sessions every Tuesday and Thursday at 1pm, as well as in-person info sessions every Wednesday at 1pm at both HOPE locations. Call 347-7730-4623 to learn how to apply. Government ID required.

recPercPqHTFMPWg3.name: Diaper Assistance Program
recPercPqHTFMPWg3.description:
Call 718-402-1212 Mondays between 9:30am-5pm to schedule an appointment for free diapers (walk-ins cannot be accepted at this time). Distribution is in the Bronx. 

To qualify, you must reside with a child 2 years or younger or be expecting (proof of sonogram or official doctors note required), live in the New York City area, and receive WIC and/or SNAP (food stamps). 

Required documents include:
- Photo ID
- Proof of address (no more than 90 days old-electricity bill/light bill/doctors letter/note with client’s name and address)
- Birth certificate(s) for baby or hospital discharge papers for newborn
- WIC proof (WIC app on cellphone or WIC card with a letter/note from WIC office) or Food Stamps/SNAP proof (recent budget letter)

recsC4ydBdD0fdjto.name: Health and Human Services Help
recsC4ydBdD0fdjto.description: Call 1.844.ONE.CALL (1.844.663.2255) during business hours to make an appointment for assistance including with mental health, family violence, and intellectual and developmental disabilities. There are no eligibility requirements.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence
People with disabilities and chronic illnesses

recNM4g5QrmvQ9hF2.name: Free Counseling and Assistance with Medicare
recNM4g5QrmvQ9hF2.description: Call 1-800-333-4114 to get assistance with understanding Medicare benefits, making enrollment decisions, coordinating Medicare with other insurance, appealing denials of care, determining eligibility for Medicare cost-saving programs, or another topic.

recoKgtKGCZzRJ0Ew.name: Free legal services for immigrant New Yorkers
recoKgtKGCZzRJ0Ew.description:
Call the city-funded, free, and safe MOIA Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365, or call 311 and say, "Immigration Legal," between 9:00am to 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, to get help in any language:

Get answers to immigration policy questions and information on how and where to find help at Legal Support Centers across the City, housed in community sites, public health facilities, public schools, and libraries. Must be a New York City resident and making 200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

recm0VO5FQSVVsTFe.name: Resources on Child Trauma
recm0VO5FQSVVsTFe.description: A diverse collection of resources to assist caregivers in helping children navigate traumatic experiences. Search by topic, language, or resource, including bullying, neglect, community violence, disasters, medical trauma, refugee trauma, separation, and more.

recxeuCdqZsMFb7Ea.name: Counseling, Legal, and other Resources for People Experiencing Domestic Abuse
recxeuCdqZsMFb7Ea.description: All free & confidential services: 24/7 domestic violence crisis hotline at (631)329-2200, individual and group counseling, legal advocacy, a residential shelter for adults and children, and violence prevention and education programs for children, teenagers and adults, taught in local schools and community-wide.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recEdPM9EUnKCfqKV.name: Emotional Support and Crisis Response Hotline
recEdPM9EUnKCfqKV.description: Call 212-673-3000 to reach The Samaritans of New York completely confidential 24-hour emotional support and crisis response hotline. It's available on an immediate and ongoing basis for individuals who are dealing with every kind of problem, situation, illness, trauma or loss and need someone to talk to who will listen and take you seriously.

recClVSLNBGB9N9Gc.name: Free Mental Health Crisis Intervention for LGBTQ Youth via Phone Hotline, Text, or Chat
recClVSLNBGB9N9Gc.description: Call 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678-678 if you are thinking about harming yourself. Get immediate crisis support, connect to a crisis counselor 24/7, 365 days a year, from anywhere in the U.S via text, chat, or phone. Confidential and free.

recBYGWua9aKnlEry.name: Advocacy for Unaccompanied Immigrant Minors
recBYGWua9aKnlEry.description: The Young Center accepts referrals for the appointment of Child Advocates. Fill out the form linked on the website.

recrZzCIdgLxP26Q4.name: Free Food Distribution Saturdays in Tompkins Square Park
recrZzCIdgLxP26Q4.description: Free food distribution Saturdays, 11am at Tompkins Square Park at the corner of East 7th Street & Avenue B. Dropoff donations of food and goods can be received at the distro 10:45-noon.

recuMBjTe0b3n3Kpq.name: Trans Lifeline Hotline
recuMBjTe0b3n3Kpq.description: Trans and questioning people can call (877) 565-8860 from 1 PM-9 PM Eastern and speak to a trans/nonbinary peer operator. Full anonymity and confidentiality, and no nonconsensual active rescue (calling 911, emergency services, or law enforcement).

recC2mgB67TAaxgNE.name: Free Bikes for Fellow New Yorkers
recC2mgB67TAaxgNE.description: Donate a spare bike or apply for a free one at bikematch.nyc. Fill out a form, get paired with a neighbor of about the same height, and arrange a time to meet up and exchange the bike.

recas8VzgGzRzb1Zj.name: Trans Needle Exchange
recas8VzgGzRzb1Zj.description: Trans Needle Exchange is a non-profit mail-based service providing free HRT needle supplies for trans folk who cannot access or afford their own.

reckuwuA4zsYEcYeR.name: Cost saving programs and resources for HDFC co-op members
reckuwuA4zsYEcYeR.description: Call 212 479 3337 to learn more about resources for HDFC  co-ops (Housing Development Fund Corporation co-ops), including free classes, cost savings on fuel and insurance, and more.

recvcjFQuiB7DdUrs.name: Dial-A-Teacher Homework Help
recvcjFQuiB7DdUrs.description:
What: Homework help line for students and their parents, run by classroom teachers
Where: Call (212) 777-3380
Who: Students in K-12
Hours: Monday through Thursday, 4 to 7 p.m. when school is in session.

recQvzUArnjG7l5Fy.name: Free Adult English Classes
recQvzUArnjG7l5Fy.description:
A 10-month program to help improve  listening, reading, speaking and writing skills. Textbooks are provided. We offer English for Speakers of Other Language (ESOL) classes at a variety of levels to adult immigrant students during the daytime, evenings, and weekends, free of charge.

Requirements: 
- Must be at least 18 years old
- Must be a NYC resident and provide proof of address
- Must be able to attend 10 months of in-person classes

recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.name: Source of Income Discrimination (SOI) Mapping Tool
recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.description: Explore the crowdsourced map to see how widespread discrimination based on housing vouchers is in a specific NYC neighborhood.

recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.name: Rights Recorder and Chatbot: Report Housing Discrimination
recjhV4p6NZjvboVh.description: Turned down by a landlord or broker because of your housing voucher? Record a call and/or report it using the Unlock NYC chatbot and they'll help hold them accountable.

rec4RGp1bPNWosJq7.name: Find an HRSA-Funded Health Center Tool
rec4RGp1bPNWosJq7.description: Find a Health Center the receives government Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) funding by location. Primary care health services should be available at a reduced cost or free of charge depending on your economic status.

rec6sXk7ng8dmt9Vt.name: Employment Services: Job Readiness, Training, and Counseling
rec6sXk7ng8dmt9Vt.description: Urban Upbound’s Employment Services team provides job readiness training and one-on-one counseling to help community members gain and retain meaningful employment. Includes job readiness assistance, 1:1 counseling, job training, and computer labs.

recyl4z4wfIW9ix5l.name: Live 24 Hour Domestic Violence Hotline
recyl4z4wfIW9ix5l.description: Call 800-664-5880 24/7 to reach Violence Intervention Program (VIP), a Latina-led organization that provides healing, housing, and economic justice to thousands of survivors of domestic and sexual violence in NYC each year.
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recVMjdII9dMKJU5f.name: National Hunger Hotline
recVMjdII9dMKJU5f.description:
Hunger Free America operates the National Hunger Hotline for people seeking information on how to obtain food. The National Hunger Hotline staff connects callers with emergency food providers in their community, government assistance programs, and various social services.

For English, call 1-866-348-6479
For Spanish, call 1-877-842-6273
Text 914-342-7744
Hours: 7AM - 10PM EST

recQBLS0vZ7IQIfoK.name: Narcotics Anonymous Meetings by Phone and Zoom
recQBLS0vZ7IQIfoK.description:
Both online and phone meetings of Narcotics Anonymous hosted from different countries around the world.
All the meetings on the Virtual NA meetings lists are sorted by language and day of the week.

reclRoz7ouIR0Fgp0.name: VOCAL-NY Syringe Exchange
reclRoz7ouIR0Fgp0.description: Access sterile injection equipment and other supplies for safer injection, fentanyl testing strips, and hygiene supplies. VOCAL-NY is a New York State-licensed Syringe Exchange Program (SEP). Find the Syringe Exchange Team at Douglass St between 3rd & 4th Aves in Brooklyn. May be able to deliver supplies to you through the Peer-Delivered Syringe Exchange (email paula@vocal-ny.org).

recOd8L5i1nuyOwOD.name: Free food, clothes and supplies in Washington Square Park
recOd8L5i1nuyOwOD.description: WSP Mutual Aid collects and distributes free food, clothes, and supplies in Washington Square Park every Friday starting at 5pm.

recgVbYwhnUi8DIwe.name: Social Services on the Upper West Side
recgVbYwhnUi8DIwe.description: Email socialservices@wscah.org or call 212-362-3662 ext. 126 to be connected with the Social Services department. Benefits include referrals to access shelter, substance abuse treatment, mental health services, financial counseling and tax preparation, educational programs, immigration legal assistance, and sign ups for health insurance, SNAP, SCRIE, and DRIE

recvAb6TSyXLFOdbz.name: Free confidential anti-violence chat & hotline in multiple languages
recvAb6TSyXLFOdbz.description:
Highly trained helpline advocates can answer general questions about domestic violence, human trafficking, and sexual violence across the lifespan, provide crisis counseling and help develop safety plans, and/or make referrals for ongoing support. Womankind also provides emergency safety shelter.

Online chat & text available Mon-Fri 10am-6pm (English, Chinese)
Text Womankind for help in: English 1.929.207.5907, Chinese 1.929.207.5901
24-Hour Multilingual Helpline: 1.888.888.7702 (English, Spanish and 18+ Asian languages and dialects, including Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Tagalog, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, and Vietnamese)
community_focus: Survivors of domestic and intimate partner violence

recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.name: Family Support Program and Benefits Counseling in the Bronx
recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.description: Call 718-839-1100 to learn more about WHEDco's Family Support Services or to ask for an appointment. Family support services include public benefits counseling for benefits such as: SNAP, WIC referrals, cash assistance (PA, TANF, SafetyNet), Safelink and Assurance cell phones, social security, health insurance, citizenship and green card applications and renewals (plus fee waiver assistance), housing applications, Senior Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE), and childcare.

recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.name: Home-Based Childcare Program
recTjFKE3TmDMXrpM.description: Contact WHEDco’s Home-Based Childcare Program (HBCC) at 347-708-7800. They work with families to help them explore options, determine their eligibility for childcare subsidies, and provide orientation on how to select the right caregiver for their needs. Also offer support services to licensed, registered, and legally-exempt service providers through the Home-Based Childcare Training Program.

reczLMvOYciMOt2Gn.name: Free dancing lessons, group exercise, and interactive activities
reczLMvOYciMOt2Gn.description: The Y @ Home includes free programs for all ages and populations open to the wider community, including exercise activities, congregate lunches, dance classes, and more.

recnqi4Jj9YpkQiB8.name: Mutual Aid + Sisterhood Centering Young Black Women
recnqi4Jj9YpkQiB8.description: Connect with YBQ.NYC for free hygiene products, clothing support, food assistance, community events, & mutual aid opportunities for Black women in Brooklyn + Queens. Join our sisterhood-centered community focused on care, empowerment, joy, & accessible support.
